Sports.title: New PM Andy Burnham actively considering letting football fans drink in stands again
Sports.content:
ANDY Burnham’s Government is actively considering letting football fans drink in the stands again.

Officials are considering whether to review restrictions which stop people consuming alcohol in view of the pitch.



The ban was introduced in 1985 to stop football hooligans fighting.

Other sports like rugby were not affected.



A government spokesperson said: “We are considering the case being made by some clubs and supporter groups for reviewing the current restrictions on alcohol consumption at football matches.

“The safety of football fans remains our priority, and any future consideration of changes would need to be evidence-led and informed by the views of policing and safety authorities, as well as clubs, supporters and other partners across the football sector.”

It comes just weeks after the new Prime Minister said it was “wrong” that spectators could not enjoy a pint during matches.

Everton fan Mr Burnham made the comments while watching a rugby league match at the club’s Hill Dickinson Stadium.



In a social media clip while holding a pint, he said: “How come these lads can do that in my seat here when we can’t do that at an Everton home game?

“There’s something wrong there, we need to take a look at that.”

This week the new Prime Minister announced that pubs, social clubs and live music venues will be given a 20 per cent cut to business rates from April.

Landlords welcomed the change but called on the Labour leader to go further by slashing VAT on boozers too.

The new Prime Minister insisted he was ready to protect “working-class culture” – in a win for The Sun’s Save Our Sups campaign.



More than 30,000 venues will save an estimated £1,100 each in the next financial year from the business rates cut.

Sports.title: ‘Sky’s the limit’ – Ayden Heaven talks up England hopes and could benefit from Man Utd mentor Harry Maguire’s misfortune
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED star Ayden Heaven insists “the sky is the limit” this season as he targets a dream England call-up.

And the Old Trafford teenager could be ready to carry the torch, just as mentor Harry Maguire’s proud Three Lions career likely enters its final chapter.



The 19-year-old centre half is targeting a major breakout year under Michael Carrick after waiting in the wings last term.

While Maguire has not retired from England duty, missing out on the 2026 World Cup squad at 33 suggests a natural transition is underway for the Three Lions—one Heaven has his eyes on.



When asked about pushing to be part of England’s Under-21s Euros title defence next summer, Heaven skipped a step to aim straight for the top.

He said: “I could push further than that. Maybe try and get into England, the main men’s team. The sky‘s the limit.

“I’ve just got to keep working hard every day. Harry has helped a lot, he has 20 years of experience.

“He’s always telling me to be vocal so I’m always ready when I get the opportunity to play.”

At this stage of his career, Heaven has only reached England Under-20 level.

He started 11 Premier League games last season, often when one of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt or Harry Maguire were unavailable through injury or suspensions.

Heaven said: “I’m young and I’ve got to be patient, especially in my position. You don’t see a lot of 19-year-olds playing week in, week out.

“I know it’s nothing personal and I’ve just got to be patient. I’m waiting for my opportunity.”

It’s almost certain Heaven will not be called up by Thomas Tuchel in the next September international break, but this season should be a banner with more games back in the schedule.

The teen is pushing to start alongside Maguire in United’s opening day clash against Hull City on August 22, having been the starting duo so far in pre-season.



With Lisandro Martinez forced off injured during the World Cup final and Matthijs de Ligt recovering from back surgery, the door has opened for the young centre-back.

Heaven’s main rival for a spot is Frenchman Leny Yoro, who is just a year older.

But with United’s World Cup stars still on break, Yoro has been deployed at right-back in their opening two pre-season friendlies against Wrexham and Rosenborg.

Heaven said: “We’re both young. We work hard every day in training together and we are close friends off the pitch.”

The Londoner earned high praise after filling the void left during crucial wins against Chelsea, Brentford, and Liverpool as United racked up three wins on the bounce to help secure Champions League football.



He added: “To hear the manager’s praise as an extra boost that he’s given up. He played a big part for this club when he played.”

Heaven, under contract until 2029, was former boss Ruben Amorim’s second signing, snapped up from Arsenal’s academy by Ineos for £1.25m.

Spanish media have given their say on the possibility of Vinicius Jr joining Arsenal. The Real Madrid winger is wanted by the Gunners but talks between the clubs have yet to begin.

‌



The 26-year-old is in the final 12 months of his contract and if Real can't secure an extension, they could be open to selling in order to avoid losing him for free next summer. A number of Spanish newspapers have weighed in on whether the transfer could actually happen.

‌



Sport claims that Real president Florentino Perez has set a non-negotiable fee of £136million (€160m). The media outlet understands that the club will not bat an eyelid at a figure below this for Vini's signature.

‌



Real are considering this fee to be an initial purchase with a number of add-ons, including performance bonuses and trophies won. Should Arsenal meet these demands, Sport sees no reason as to how the deal couldn't go through.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update READ MORE :

Arsenal have trump card to beat Man Utd in £40m Ollie Watkins transfer race READ MORE :

Marca aren't as confident that the transfer will happen though. The Spanish newspaper states that Vini is demanding at least £25m (€30m) per season to bring his salary close to Kylian Mbappe's.

They believe the contract extension negotiations are entering a "delicate phase" and if these conditions aren't met, it is unclear what the future holds for the winger. Cadena SER believes that the arrival of Yan Diomande could be the end of Vini in Spain.

View 2 Images Vini Jr wants a similar salary to Kylian Mbappe (Image: Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

The media outlet claims that Real's pursuit of the Ivory Coast international showcases the club's movement into a new era. The La Liga giants saw a £85.4m bid rejected by RB Leipzig and are now submitting an improved offer, believing that a deal can be done.

The pair would be competing for the left wing spot and Real's growing interest in Diomande is a hint to the media that Vini Jr is on his way out. They did admit that there is a world where both wingers remain in Spain but Vini's recent links to Arsenal could mean the 19-year-old is his replacement under Jose Mourinho.

Sports.title: Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update
Sports.content:
Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update

Arsenal want Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior and are exploring a move for the Brazil international, but have already agreed to sign another player this summer

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are adding another player to their academy (Image: Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Cardiff City's youngest-ever player, Axel Donczew, is set to sign for Arsenal next week.

The Gunners have agreed a deal for the Wales under-19 international, who Fabrizio Romano claims has already had a medical.

Donczew, 16, debuted for the Bluebirds as a second-half substitute during their EFL Trophy match against Newport County in October, aged 15 years and 234 days. He broke a record that his team-mate Rob Tankiewicz set barely an hour earlier by starting the group stage game.

Aaron Ramsey had previously held the record for 18 years. He was also the last player Arsenal signed from Cardiff.

The Gunners spent £7million on a 17-year-old Ramsey in 2018. That move came after the midfielder made 22 appearances across all competitions for Cardiff, whereas Donczew has played just twice.

The Telegraph initially reported that the Gunners were keen on the teenager, who is expected to join their academy.

News of the deal surfaced less than 24 hours after Arsenal's interest in Vinicius Junior emerged. Real Madrid's winger would likely cost a record-breaking fee for the Gunners to sign, but they are believed to be exploring the possibility.

Jose Mourinho is reportedly reluctant to lose the Brazilian, but his lack of a new contract at the Bernabeu means Real could cash in this summer.

In terms of Donczew, he has been missing from Cardiff City's pre-season activities this summer following interest from Premier League sides. Fulham had previously expressed interest in the right-footed left winger, who can also play centrally as an attacking midfielder.

View 2 Images Manchester City's former Elite Development Sqyad head coach Brian Barry-Murphy believes Axel Donczew is a brilliant player (Image: Ryan Hiscott, Getty Images)

Donczew last played for Cardiff in December, making another substitute appearance during an EFL Trophy round of 32 tie against Wimbledon. A fortnight later, Donczew was included in the matchday squad for their EFL Cup quarter-final against Chelsea, but did not feature.

Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy said late last year: "I think if they're good enough, and he clearly is, then they're old enough for us with Axel. The former Manchester City youth coach hailed Donczew as a "brilliant player".

He has already earned recognition as a Wales under-19 international. Donczew has represented his national side since the under-15s.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The youngster has racking up 11 appearances across various age groups, and also holds eligibility to feature for Poland. Wales senior side head coach Craig Bellamy, however, is said to be an admirer of the youngster.

Under-21s coach Darren Purse told WalesOnline: "I think Axel came into fruition because I think Craig Bellamy really liked him as an Under-16 playing for Wales. I think that came through him and the gaffer's (Barry-Murphy) conversations."

CAA (Creative Artists Agency) Stellar represents Donczew. The prominent agency's lengthy list of clients also notably includes two current Arsenal academy players: Angelinou Pedro and Theo Julienne.

Sports.title: Jeremy Jacquet's Liverpool absence explained as summer signing left OUT of pre-season squad
Sports.content:
Jeremy Jacquet's Liverpool absence explained as summer signing left OUT of pre-season squad

Liverpool saw off Sunderland in a pre-season friendly on Saturday but they did so without Jeremy Jacquet as the summer signing was left out of the squad

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet was left out of Liverpool's squad at the weekend

Andoni Iraola admits Jeremy Jacquet's long-term injury led to him being left out of Liverpool's squad on Saturday with the Reds prepared to "take it easy with him".

‌



The French defender was signed in January for £55million from Rennes, but allowed to play out the season with the Ligue 1 club. He's since made the move to Anfield but did so off the back of a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

‌



The 21-year-old was forced to miss the final few months of last season after picking up a shoulder injury. Given that he have surgery on the issue, his last game came all the way back on February 7.

‌



As a result Liverpool are taking a cautious approach to bringing him back into the fold and he was left out of the team that beat Sunderland 4-2 in Nashville. Iraola explained to LFCTV: “With Jeremy, we decided to take it easy with him."

“He has been a lot of months without playing with a shoulder injury. So, I think we are going to take it easy with him. He will play probably the last game of this US tour and he will have time to have minutes. It's true that we were kind of happy but we've lost one now.”

Iraola was referring to the injury sustained by Joe Gomez, who failed to complete ten minutes during Liverpool's clash on Saturday. There is no diagnosis on his injury but the defender has been plagued by injuries for years and could further test the team's backline depth.

‌



"Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe," said Iraola. "We were happy because we were going through training without losing any players and unluckily for us we've lost Joe straight away."

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet's move to Liverpool was confirmed this summer

Liverpool have seen Ibrahima Konate depart for Real Madrid after his contract expired whilst Giovanni Leoni is still getting back to 100 percent after rupturing his ACL last September. Virgil van Dijk has just turned 35 and will see his contract expire in the summer.

Article continues below

Jacquet is highly rated and was tipped to move to Chelsea, who had chased him throughout January, before Liverpool swooped in to complete a deal. He's relatively inexperienced but is likely to play a big role with Liverpool's resources already being tested in pre-season.

Sports.title: Man Utd 'won't make Champions League spots' due to major concern and Bruno Fernandes factor
Sports.content:
Man Utd 'won't make Champions League spots' due to major concern and Bruno Fernandes factor

Manchester United enjoyed a stunning second half of last season but they still have their doubters as Michael Carrick looks to make an impact across an entire campaign

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is out to prove himself in his first full season at Man Utd (Image: MARKKU ULANDER, Lehtikuva/AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United won't make the Champions League places next season according to Troy Deeney - who believes they'll struggle with the added amount of games.

‌



The Red Devils enjoyed a huge renaissance under Michael Carrick, who took charge in January. They had been inconsistent until his arrival before going on an impressive run, winning 12 of their final 17 games to finish third.

‌



That run came with United not in any European competition and out of both domestic cups at the first hurdle. It means, from January, they only had their Premier League assignments to focus on, which was advantageous.

‌



They will not enjoy that benefit again as Carrick looks to prove himself across a full season - and Deeney cannot see Bruno Fernandes having the same level of influence. The Portuguese playmaker won numerous individual accolades and set the record for assists.

Mason Mount opens up on new Man Utd role handed to him by Michael Carrick READ MORE :

Man Utd 8th and Liverpool 15th in list of biggest earners from World Cup payouts READ MORE :

He told talkSPORT: "I don’t think they’ll make the Champions League places right now. The reason is we don’t know what Carrick’s like with three games in a week at this level. Obviously, we saw a bit of Championship, but not at this level.

"Now, having to look at the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cups, Carabao Cups, you can’t go out as early as you have done in previous years. There’s an expectation now to do more. Bruno Fernandes, do you really think he’s going to have the season he had last season again this season?

‌



"I just think that with the squad currently constructed as is, I don’t think there’s enough depth to get through all of those competitions, which I think will ultimately leave them short."

View 2 Images Man Utd finished an impressive third last term (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

United have made it a priority to add midfielders this summer as they look to prepare themselves for next season. They built up some impressive momentum last term and have since added Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos with the middle of the pitch cited as a problem area.

Article continues below

Deeney has backed Arsenal to retain their title with Manchester City again second best. Liverpool, now under new management, are his pick for third whilst he's backed Xabi Alonso to get Chelsea back into the top four after a dire season last time out.

Sports.title: Real Madrid president has already made Vinicius Jr to Arsenal stance very clear
Sports.content:
Real Madrid president has already made Vinicius Jr to Arsenal stance very clear

Arsenal are eyeing up a move for Vinicius Jnr as his Real Madrid contract winds down but Florentino Perez is determined to keep him if a deal can be struck

View 2 Images Arsenal are weighing up a sensational move for Vinicius Jnr (Image: Denis Doyle, Getty Images)

Real Madrid president Florentino Perez admits he'd "love Vinicius Jnr to stay forever" as Arsenal look to seize on the uncertainty surrounding his contract situation.

‌



The Gunners have talked up a move internally as they consider making a move for the Brazilian, who is out of contract next season with no major progress yet made on an extension.

‌



Arsenal have just claimed the Premier League and want to add more star quality as they look to take the final step in the Champions League. Adding more firepower in attack is seen as an area where Mikel Arteta's side can improve and Vinicius is regarded among the best wingers in the world.

‌



The Brazilian has been at the Bernabeu since 2018 and has continued to blossom. He scored in Champions League final victories in 2022 and 2024 and Perez is on record stating his admiration for him.

Arsenal exploring stunning Vinicius Junior transfer as Real Madrid star's move approved READ MORE :

He said on his future: "Vinicius' renewal? There's time. I'd love for him to stay forever. He's won us the last two Champions Leagues and he identifies really well with the club. You know who doesn't like him? Those who aren't Real Madrid fans."

Talks between Arsenal and Real haven't taken place, reports the Athletic, but the La Liga giants may have to cash in on Vinicius if there's a risk of seeing him leave on a free transfer in 2027. The report adds that the winger would be due a significant loyalty bonus next season, having been at the Bernabeu for eight years.

‌



Arsenal have not made any bid yet but it is understood that Jose Mourinho, who has just returned to Real last year after having a public spat with Vinicius, would oppose Arsenal signing the forward this summer - he wants all his big names to stay. The Special One is adamant that he wants Vinicius, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham in his team.

View 2 Images Florentino Perez has expressed no desire to see Vinicius Jnr leave (Image: FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images)

Vinicius is understood to be on about £400,000 per week and signing a player on that type of wage would represent a huge shift for Arsenal, who so far have not signed a world class individual of that ilk.

Article continues below

The Gunners had their sights on Morgan Rogers but they were ultimately outbid by Chelsea. They landed the playmaker from Aston Villa for £117million, a British record, but Arsenal have cash to spend as they look to add another dynamic to their frontline.

Sports.title: Yan Diomande double ‘verbal agreement’ reached as Arsenal get boost in Vinicius Jr transfer
Sports.content:
Yan Diomande double ‘verbal agreement’ reached as Arsenal get boost in Vinicius Jr transfer

Real Madrid have reportedly reached a verbal agreement with RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande – a move that could have significant knock-on effects for Vinicius Jr's future at the club

View 2 Images Yan Diomande has reportedly agreed to join Real Madrid (Image: Getty)

Real Madrid have reportedly moved a step closer to completing a deal to sign RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande, which could have implications for Vinicius Jr’s future at the club.

‌



The Brazilian has been linked with a move away from the La Liga giants this summer, with Arsenal mentioned as a potential destination.

‌



It was reported on Saturday that Arsenal have joined the race to sign Vinicius, adding the 26-year-old to their list of potential transfer targets this summer.

‌



Diomande is another forward whose future has been the subject of intense speculation this summer, and now there has been a fresh update which could have a major impact elsewhere.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arsenal have trump card to beat Man Utd in £40m Ollie Watkins transfer race READ MORE :

Sky Germany reporter Florian Plettenberg has reported that Diomande has reached a 'verbal agreement' to complete a move to Madrid, provided Leipzig are able to agree a fee.

‌



Diomande is also said to have reached a similar agreement with Paris Saint-Germain, who have been strongly linked with the Ivory Coast international throughout the summer.

The report indicates that Real have agreed a contract running until at least 2031 with Diomande, while Leipzig continue to hold out for in excess of €100million (£85million) to finalise any arrangement.

The ramifications of Diomande's potential switch to Madrid could shape Vinicius' long-term future in the Spanish capital, suggesting Arsenal may well be monitoring developments closely for any further updates.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal are interested in a move from Vinicius Jr (Image: Getty Images)

Vinicius' deal with Real expires next summer, which has fuelled speculation that a move away could materialise this summer as the La Liga giants look to avoid losing their prized forward on a free transfer in 12 months' time.

What lies ahead for the 26-year-old this summer, and whether Arsenal's interest develops into anything more substantial, remains to be seen.

‌



A recent report in The Telegraph claimed, however, that new Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has made his position crystal clear to club bosses, insisting he wants Vinicius to stay put and would be firmly against the winger completing a transfer to Arsenal.

Vinicius netted 22 goals for Madrid last season as they finished runners-up in La Liga and reached the Champions League quarter-final, and recently featured for the Brazil side that reached the last-16 of the World Cup.

Sports.title: Man Utd 8th and Liverpool 15th in list of biggest earners from World Cup payouts
Sports.content:
Man Utd 8th and Liverpool 15th in list of biggest earners from World Cup payouts

Premier League clubs picked up handy bonuses thanks to their players' exploits at the World Cup

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez and Alexis Mac Allister's progress at the World Cup help their clubs bank millions (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

Almost half of the Premier League banked tidy sums from the World Cup as part of FIFA compensation payments. The competition will be viewed as an inconvenience to many clubs, given the risk of injury and interruption to pre-season.

‌



However, there is a financial benefit for players' clubs, as they receive compensation through the FIFA Club Benefits Programme. It was designed to recognise and financially reward clubs for their role in developing, employing and releasing players to participate on the global stage.

‌



Clubs are entitled to roughly £3,750 per day, per player from the release date of May 25 to their national team's final match in the competition. Therefore, the maximum payouts will be due to players from Spain, Argentina, England and France, who played the most games in North America.

‌



Given the Premier League's reputation as the world's top domestic league, English clubs figure prominently in the top 20 of clubs that earned the most from the tournament.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Tottenham Hotspur, who came in at 17th, are due £1.58m, one place behind Chelsea (£1.65m), reports The Athletic. Liverpool, in 15th, earned a similar amount to the Blues. The Reds had eight players at the tournament, including Alexis Mac Allister of runners-up Argentina.

‌



Sunderland are the next English club in 13th, one spot behind Aston Villa. Manchester United (£1.95m) are eighth on the list. They received payments for Kobbie Mainoo, despite the fact that he didn't play a single minute at the tournament, and Marcus Rashford, who spent last season on loan at Barcelona.

Crystal Palace (£2.03m), in seventh, were also well represented at the tournament with 12 players, including England back-up keeper Dean Henderson, France pair Maxence Lacroix and Jean-Philippe Mateta and Spain's Yeremy Pino.

View 3 Images Rodri of Manchester City led Spain to World Cup glory (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

‌



Paris Saint-Germain (£2.4m), Arsenal (£2.48m), Bayern Munich (£2.55m), Barcelona (£2.93m) and Manchester City (£3.3m) make up the top five. Barcelona had eight Spain players alone - Ferran Torres, Eric Garcia, Gavi, Dani Olmo, Joan Garcia, Lamine Yamal, Pedri and Pau Cubarsi.

Arsenal had 16 players at the World Cup, three fewer than City, who lost virtually their entire first-time squad to the tournament. Many of those players are enjoying post-World Cup breaks before returning to their clubs in August.

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford made money for Man United despite not playing for the club for 18 months (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

Article continues below

The Premier League kicks off on August 21, with champions Arsenal hosting newly promoted Coventry City. La Liga's World Cup stars get less time to recover, with the Spanish top flight getting underway on August 15.

Sports.title: Malaysia added to 2026 F1 calendar
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has added Malaysia to its 2026 schedule as the host of the Bahrain Grand Prix that was postponed earlier in the season.

The sport's bosses had hoped to reinstate the event to the calendar, but the continuation of conflict in the Middle East, which was the original cause of the cancellation of April races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, has forced a change of plan.

Instead, Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit will host an event that will still be titled the 'Bahrain Grand Prix', with the Gulf state funding the race in a show of support for the sport.

The event, which will see Malaysia host a race for the first time since 2017, is scheduled to take place from October 2-4, slotting between rounds in Baku and Singapore to create a triple-header of back-to-back races.

Image: Max Verstappen was the winner the last time Malaysia hosted an F1 race

The change to the calendar still needs to be approved by the World Motor Sport Council, but that step is considered a formality.

Formula 1 president Stefano Domenicali said: "We are delighted to confirm that Malaysia will host the Bahrain Grand Prix in 2026.

"Once again, the sport has demonstrated its ability to adapt, find solutions, and deliver, creating an exciting moment for everyone who follows Formula 1."

Adding Malaysia increases the current schedule to 23 races, but the inability of Bahrain to host a race in October creates major doubt over whether the final two rounds of the season - in Qatar (Nov 27-29) and Abu Dhabi (Dec 4-6) - will be able to go ahead.

As Formula 1 confirmed the addition of Malaysia ahead of Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix - the last race before a month-long summer break, the sport's bosses said that the schedule for the rest of the season currently remains unchanged.

Formula 1 2026 remaining races Netherlands* August 21-23 USA October 23-25 Italy September 4-6 Mexico Oct 30-Nov 1 Madrid September 11-13 Brazil November 6-8 Azerbaijan September 24-26 Las Vegas November 20-22 Malaysia October 2-4 Qatar November 27-29 Singapore* October 9-11 Abu Dhabi December 4-6 *denotes Sprint weekend

The speed with which Formula 1 has pivoted to add the race in Malaysia reflects an adaptability that suggests they will be ready to make further alterations to the schedule should they be required to.

It remains to be seen whether Formula 1 would seek to replace just one or both of the final two rounds in the event they are unable to be held at their planned venues.

Image: The Sepang International Circuit has previously hosted 19 F1 races

Sepang International Circuit organisers were understood to have been one of a number of venues to express interest in stepping in to host a Grand Prix this year.

Italy's Imola circuit is understood to be in the frame should another host be required, while Portugal and Turkey, both of which return to the sport's calendar in 2027, are other possible alternatives.

'Brotherly relations' between Bahrain and Malaysia aid F1

As Formula 1 sought a solution to avoid the commercial complications that could come with too many races falling off the 2026 calendar, the strong relationship between Bahrain and Malaysia has come in handy.

Bahrain Crown Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa said the staging of the event would build 'on the close and brotherly relations between our two countries."

He added: "This will be a wonderful experience for fans around the world and reflects Bahrain's enduring commitment to, and passion for, the sport.

"Amid ongoing regional challenges, Bahrain is proud to stand as a pillar of stability for Formula 1, and we will

continue to do everything in our power to ensure a successful and memorable race for everyone involved."

Malaysian Prime Minister Dato' Seri Anwar Ibrahim added: "Malaysia stands ready to welcome Formula 1, the FIA, the teams and fans from around the world back to Sepang.

"We look forward to showcasing our world-class infrastructure, operational excellence and warm hospitality, while further strengthening the bonds between our two nations through this special occasion."

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said that the sport's governing body had "worked tirelessly" in its attempts to reschedule the event in Bahrain.

Ben Sulayem said: "Throughout this process, the FIA, Formula One Management, and our partners in Bahrain have worked tirelessly to explore every option, with the safety and wellbeing of the teams, volunteers, officials, our colleagues, and fans remaining our highest priority."

Sports.title: Real Madrid in pole position to sign RB Leipzig's Diomande
Sports.content:
Real Madrid are in pole position to sign RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande, according to Sky in Germany.

The Spanish giants have already had a £85.4m (€100m) bid rejected for the 19-year-old but Leipzig want significantly more to let him go.

Sky in Germany are reporting that Real were working with RB Leipzig on Saturday night to strike an agreement for the player.

Diomande had previously indicated a preference to join Paris Saint-Germain earlier this summer and agreed a contract with them until 2031.

Real have now also agreed personal terms with Diomande.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at all of the reasons why Yan Diomande is high on the radar of clubs from across the world.

Jose Mourinho's side have been active in this window as Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konate, Denzel Dumfries and Marc Cucurella have all been snapped up.

Liverpool have also expressed an interest in winger Diomande but aren't willing to pay more than £85m.

Premier League clubs Arsenal and Manchester City also remain interested in Diomande.

With six weeks left of the transfer window, the situation has been described as an open race by sources close to any potential deal. Real have now come to the table with an offer amid uncertainty around the future of Vinicius Junior.

The fee Liverpool are ready to pay at this stage would dwarf the Premier League's record transfer for a teenager, surpassing the £58.9m Manchester United agreed to sign Leny Yoro from Lille for in the summer of 2024.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News brings you the latest transfer news with updates on the likes of Cristian Romero, Yan Diomande and Maxence Lacroix.

Arsenal are looking into a potential deal for Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior.

At this point there has been no club-to-club contact, but the interest is real. Vinicius Jr is one of a number of forward targets Arsenal are exploring, with Julian Alvarez, Diomande and Bradley Barcola also players of interest.

The Brazilian international, 26, has entered the final year of his contract and if an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Real could be open to selling, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Bayern confident of Olise stay amid Real links

Sports.title: Impressive Liverpool beat Sunderland in Iraola's first game in charge
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola won his first match in charge of Liverpool as his new side produced an impressive display to beat Sunderland 4-2 in their opening game of their summer tour of the US.

Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot at Anfield in June, will have been delighted with some of the football Liverpool produced in the Nashville heat, especially a fine team move that led to the opening goal for young midfielder Kieran Morrison after 13 minutes.

The Basque, like his opposite number Regis Le Bris, rung the changes after the first half, with Liverpool improving after the break to turn around a 2-1 deficit thanks to a characteristic Dominik Szoboszlai piledriver, followed by further strikes from fellow substitutes Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas.

However, there was one negative for Iraola, who saw stand-in captain and long-serving defender Joe Gomez forced off early on with what looked a muscle issue in an area of the team where Liverpool really could do without any injuries heading into the new campaign.

The key moments from Nashville SC Stadium

8: INJURY! A big worry already for Liverpool with captain Gomez down with an injury and this does not look good for the centre-back.

13: GOAL! The first goal of the Iraola era is scored by Morrison after a wonderful team move involving some impressive build-up from the likes of McConnell, Ngumoha and Elliott, who fed the midfielder in space on the right of the box and he then found the bottom corner with a low shot.

28: GOAL! Sunderland are level as McConnell loses possession deep inside the Black Cats' half allowing Le Fee to break upfield and as the Reds defence backed off, the playmaker fired an unstoppable effort past a helpless Mamardashvili from 25 yards.

49: GOAL! Sunderland have turned this one around to now lead after Frimpong lost possession in a bad area, with the ball then slipped through for Tuterov, with the half-time sub finishing confidently.

56: GOAL! It is now raining goals as Szoboszlai hits an absolute worldie to bring Liverpool level after an excellent break down the left involving Koumas and Kerkez and after Sunderland only half clear the danger, the Hungary midfielder lashes home an unstoppable volley from the left edge of the box.

72: GOAL! And now Liverpool are back in front as Ramsey feeds Chiesa in space in the box and from a tight angle and faced with the onrushing Moore to beat, the sub finds the back of the net from a tight angle.

85: GOAL! Liverpool score another excellent goal to surely wrap this game up as Sunderland initially give the ball away and Szoboszlai finds Koumas in the box and the sub does well to find the net with a confident finish.

'A lot of things to correct, but a good starting point'

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola:

"I think it was different halves. Especially, they were a lot stronger in the first half. We kind of balanced both teams, and you could feel the difference. A lot of things to correct, obviously, it's the first day.

"You could feel the heavy legs, the players have been training. So, we lacked some freshness. But it will give us a good starting point to improve things.

"Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe [Gomez]. We were happy because we were kind of going through all the training without losing any player. Unluckily for us, straight away we've lost Joe."

Lots of positives for Iraola to take

Sky Sports' Rich Morgan:

Lots of positives for Iraola to take from his first match in charge of Liverpool, starting obviously with the win, although this being preseason in many ways it was the performance of his players and how well they gelled at times that will have most pleased the new Reds boss.

Liverpool scored some eye-catching goals, the team got better as the game wore on, despite the heat in Nashville, and all 22 players used with be better for this first competitive runout of preseason.

Iraola sweating on nature of Gomez's latest injury

Sky Sports' Rich Morgan:

Iraola may have won his first match in charge of Liverpool, but there was some worrying injury news as Joe Gomez was forced off early on.

Image: Joe Gomez was substituted early on with an injury

The long-serving defender appeared to suffer a muscle issue and was replaced in the centre of defence by youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe just 10 minutes into the club's first preseason game of their summer tour of the US.

Gomez, 29, has a long history of injuries at Anfield, although Iraola will hope it is nothing too serious with Ibrahima Konate having left on a free transfer at the end of last season, while both Giovanni Leoni and Jeremy Jacquet missed the game in Nashville also with injury.

Leoni, signed last year from Parma, will not be back to full fitness for at least a few months after suffering an ACL on his Reds debut last September, while Jacquet, who joined the club from Rennes this summer, missed the game with a minor knock having only just recovered from a shoulder issue.

Sports.title: ‘We want to win the league’: Arsenal’s new recruits ink in WSL success
Sports.content:
Georgia Stanway looks at her arms and then down at her legs on day one of Arsenal’s pre-season. “As you can see, I’m covered in tattoos,” she says. “I only see the bare skin, the space, so I need to keep collecting more”.

Tattooing and being tattooed is her creative outlet, her way of expressing herself off the pitch. But seeing space is key to the 27-year-old England midfielder being exceptional on the pitch.

Stanway’s unveiling video, after her move from Bayern Munich, showed a delicate, cursive script reading “whatever the weather” tattooed on her arm. It was a bold statement to get the lyric from North London Forever, Arsenal’s anthem, etched into her skin before she has stepped on to the Emirates Stadium pitch in red and white. “It shows I’m going to give absolutely everything for this club. I want to hit the ground running , play my game, connect with my teammates, connect with the fans and look forward to an exciting future at the club.”

Stanway is emblematic of Arsenal’s summer of change, one of seven signings so far. Meanwhile, Lotte Wubben-Moy, a lifelong fan who joined Arsenal’s academy at 13, represents the core and culture that is a point of focus at the club. It is a culture players want to be a part of, so much so it leads to players getting a tattoo on day one of being there. “She has set a very high bar,” says Wubben-Moy, with a grin. “That’s Georgia. She goes all in and I like that.”

Wubben-Moy is ready to stake a claim in Arsenal’s starting XI after struggling to nail down a position in defence despite having performed exceptionally well when covering for injured players. “I’ve always felt ready,” says the 27-year-old. “When I get my moment, I deliver. Historically, as a club, we’re built on defensive solidity. If we have a solid defence, it allows us to create and score. That should be the stepping stone towards victories. So I will continue to contribute to the defensive solidity in whatever way, shape or form that is. But I want my spot”.

View image in fullscreen Lotte Wubben-Moy lifts the Champions Cup trophy during the Arsenal trophy parade in May. Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

There was widespread recognition that Arsenal’s squad needed a revamp, that the age needed to be lowered and changes made if they were going to take the next step. That meant big names leaving, most notably Beth Mead and Katie McCabe. “They’re both absolute legends of the game and we have so much respect for them,” says Jodie Taylor, the former Arsenal striker who became the club’s technical director in January. “But we always knew this window was going to come with some changes.”

“Change is inevitable in women’s football,” says Wubben-Moy. “If you speak to a player and they don’t say they’re nimble, you’ve got someone that’s not built for the game. We’ve become a nimble team, a team that can move with the ebb and flow of women’s football.

View image in fullscreen Beth Mead left in a busy summer for Arsenal. Photograph: Rhianna Chadwick/PA

“That’s not just within the playing group, it’s something replicated within the staff, the boardroom, the commercial team, the comms team. Everyone is so willing to move and to dictate what we want.

“If you’d asked me about change four or five years ago, I’d have been a bit intimidated, but now I know what to do and I’m part of the driver of it. The opportunity we have and that I see for us as a team, as a collective, is something that really excites me.”

Arsenal’s approach to Stanway’s recruitment was a contributing factor to her wanting to join the club. “Arsenal came in early doors,” she says. “I really enjoyed they were super loyal from the beginning and wanted me even when I wasn’t available. It’s nice feeling being wanted.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The last four years in Munich were unbelievable, but I knew I wanted to take the next step and I felt at Arsenal there was an opportunity for me to be able to progress, to make my game better and to play with world-class players.”

Arsenal have done most of their business early, with Stanway joined by experienced internationals Selina Çerçi, Géraldine Reuteler, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodríguez, as well as young talents Lisa Baum and Isabella Damm. No major international tournament and seven signings in for day one of pre-season is a big boost for Renée Slegers and her coaching staff, particularly after two seasons of slow starts to domestic campaigns.

“The market is not easy, though, it’s constantly changing and the pool of elite talent is small and several clubs are fishing from it,” says Taylor. “You try and plan as much as you can, but you also have to be reactive in the market. We’re always trying to keep an eye on the future, but we have to be quite agile.

“We can talk about positional needs, qualities, ages and succession planning, but if a player’s not available or they just don’t exist, it can be like trying to fit square pegs and round holes. As well as looking at current needs and positional profiles, we talk a lot about our core style of play, but we also want to play with variety, be unpredictable and have different qualities in players too.”

View image in fullscreen Former Arsenal striker Jodie Taylor, now technical director, is leading the strong recruitment this summer. Photograph: Zuma Press/Alamy

The players that have come in have brought energy, says Wubben-Moy, who was on an emotional rollercoaster during Arsenal’s men’s Premier League and women’s Champions Cup winning parade, with the bus looping past Highbury Corner, where she filmed her contract renewal video, and past Islington town hall, where she got married to cyclist Tao Geoghegan Hart a few weeks later.

“I like to focus on what they’re entering, which is a culture that has been created by history, by players and staff that are the core of this team and who have all lived through the changes to different degrees: Kelly [Smith], Renée, myself, Leah [Williamson], Kim [Little], Jodie, too. We’ve been privy to lots of different things all of us are holding on to and releasing, in a healthy way, the things we know we need to. It’s efficient, we’re focused, we know what we do next.

“It’s like you’re cooking the most beautiful recipe and then you add the final small ingredients that make the marginal difference, that elevate, and you create something that’s beautiful and that you can relish and enjoy. That’s what we’re in the process of now with a beautiful long pre-season. I’m desperate to get it out of the way so we can then serve what we’re cooking to the fans and be like: ‘Let’s eat and we’ll all eat together for the whole year.’”

The average attendance of more than 34,000 fans for WSL games at the Emirates last season and the club’s pioneering history in women’s football, as well as Champions League win in 2025, are huge selling points, and all concerned at Arsenal want more, including a first Women’s Super League title since 2019.

“We’re in a great place,” says Taylor. “But we would have liked to have won more trophies last season and that is our huge ambition coming into this year. I’ll flat out say it: we want to win the league. We are an ambitious club and with the signings we’ve made we feel like we’re in a great place to do that.”

Sports.title: How the death of Jayden Adams shook a community: ‘Being on the pitch was his happy place’
Sports.content:
For Jayden Adams, the South Africa midfielder who died this month at the age of 25, football was a “safe space”. Those words, used by Adams’s junior coach Steve Barker at his memorial service last Thursday, tell you everything you need to know about his life beyond the pitch.

Adams’s battles were bestowed on him almost from birth. Though he was born into newly democratic South Africa, by the early 2000s the revolution was well on its way to being betrayed. The vote was extended to all, but few could make full use of the freedoms available to them because socioeconomic circumstances in the country had barely changed. Stellenbosch, where the Adams family were based, is a perfect example.

Its facade is a tourist dream: a university town nestled among vineyards, Cape Dutch architecture and indie boutiques. Most visitors never venture beyond the town centre or into its suburbs, which are home to the far less privileged and are havens of neglect. Those areas are classic Apartheid hangovers, where the wealth has been preserved for a historically advantaged elite and those on the margins, working-class communities of people of colour, are all but invisible.

Ironically, that is how Adams is most often described. He moved in the shadows, both of society and the sport in which he excelled. “Jayden was a guy of very few words. He was quiet, very shy and the smallest among his teammates,” Brendine Johnson, an Adams family spokesperson, says. “Initially, a lot of people missed his football qualities because of his size, but he had a very good fighting spirit. It just wasn’t always on display.”

Adams, whose funeral took place on Saturday in Cape Town, loved the game dearly and his aunt Monica Thaoge recalled how, as a child, he would kick anything round – “even onions” she said at his memorial. His parents, Juanito and Candice, previously mentioned potatoes as their son’s football of choice. Nobody in the family talks about lacking in financial means because theirs was a community striving to make life better. But there were absences, especially early on.

View image in fullscreen Members of the Mamelodi Sundowns football club carry Jayden Adams’ coffin at the funeral service for the player on Saturday. Photograph: Esa Alexander/Reuters

“Everybody in areas like that is just trying to make ends meet,” says Roger Telemachus, the former South Africa cricketer who grew up on the same street as Adams’s father in Cloetesville. “For the kids, they may not have noticed so much because they were occupied, mostly with playing sport. Some fathers, like Juanito, really encouraged their kids and everyone used to play everything on the street: tennis, football, rugby, cricket. It was also the best way of staying out of trouble.”

Problems were there for everyone to see and, according to Telemachus, have got worse “in the last 20 years”. They include gangsterism, substance abuse and crimes that range from petty to serious. Adams was able to escape from that life when he moved to the slightly more affluent area of Ida’s Valley, but still he did not have a life of luxury. For a period, the family of six, which included four children, lived in a two-bedroom place. At other times, they were with his maternal grandmother, Marianna. “He basically grew up in her yard,” says Johnson.

Things started to change for Adams when he was picked for the Stellenbosch Academy Under-18 side at the age of 15. “The environment was tough, especially if you are not big or tall enough, but when physicality was no longer the most important thing, people saw that Jayden was technically very good,” says Johnson.

His coaches agree. Barker, the nephew of South Africa’s Afcon winning coach, Clive, and the current coach of Simba in Tanzania, gave an emotional assessment of Adams’s skills shortly after his death. “You get many good footballers but you get few great footballers. Jayden was great,” he told Newzroom Afrika.

“Jayden had three attributes that set him apart: an incredible first touch, his weight of pass – I’ve never seen anything like it – and he loved the game so much. Being on the pitch was his happy place. He didn’t pass the ball, he used to caress the ball. He was special and his football intelligence was just outstanding.”

View image in fullscreen Jayden Adams played in South Africa’s World Cup group game against Czechia despite the death of his grandmother the day before. Photograph: Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images

It was under Barker that Adams blossomed. He became the first player from the Stellenbosch Academy to play in South Africa’s top flight, the Premier Soccer League. Five years and an international call up later, the country’s richest club, Mamelodi Sundowns, came calling. This year, at the start of his second season with them, Adams shaved his head, in what he joked was a sign of maturity and called himself a “grootman” (big man). The nickname stuck.

Adams never said it, but he may also have realised how much he had grown up. By then, he had been picked, played for and dropped from the national side after arriving late at a training camp and irking the head coach, Hugo Broos. He had also lost two of his academy teammates, including a close friend.

In February 2023, Oshwin Andries, who was 19, died from stabbing injuries he sustained in Paarl, which is 16km north of Stellenbosch. Three years later, Jeandre Gaffoor, 20, drowned in the Krom River.

When Sundowns won the CAF Champions League in May, Adams dedicated his medal to Andries. To lose so much has weighed on the town, but through Adams they have had reason to celebrate.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Fortnightly Sign up to The Hotspot A new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisis Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Members of Adams’s family, including his father, Juanito (centre left), and mother, Candice (centre right), at his memorial service last week. Photograph: Rodger Bosch/AFP/Getty Images

His role in Sundowns’ continental victory and a call-up to the World Cup squad suggested Adams’s career trajectory was rising. After a first season at Sundowns where he was often playing off the bench and his place in the side was questioned, he had become integral to the team. At Adams’s memorial, the Sundowns senior coach, Steve Komphela, called him “the heart of our team and the heartbeat of our playing style” who “understood the game like a coach and played it as a player”.

In the past year, Adams was playing to the potential people who knew him well had seen years ago and surprising others with his courage and drive to succeed. South Africa’s captain, Ronwen Williams, recalled an incident at this year’s Africa Cup of Nations when the tiny Adams took on a tall Mali opponent with some choice local words. Williams asked Adams if he knew the size of the player he was sledging, but Adams shrugged it off and replied that the Malian wouldn’t understand anyway.

“That was the character he had,” Williams said at the memorial, smiling through his tears as he bade farewell to the teammate he called “my ma se kind” (my mother’s child, a term of endearment used in South Africa).

As his star rose, Adams was careful not to advertise his achievements. “Jayden knew what he had, but he never wanted to voice it. He was very competitive, but he would never brag,” says Johnson. “You get people who are very good verbally on social media. Jayden was not like that. And he wanted to give back. After every game, he would be giving away shirts and boots to kids who asked.”

He also concentrated on providing for his family because he “always promised them he would change their financial situation”.

View image in fullscreen Jayden Adams signs a South Africa shirt for a young Mexican fan who arrived at the team’s World Cup hotel. ‘He wanted to give back.’ Photograph: SAFA

At the World Cup, Adams played for them, even through immense pain. His grandmother Marianna died the day before South Africa’s match against Czechia and Adams opted to remain with the squad. He played that match and appeared in good spirits afterwards and called the 1-1 draw positive, even if he was feeling the opposite way.

He also played the next game against South Korea, which South Africa won to reach the knockouts for the first time. Post-game footage showed him sitting on his own while the rest of the squad celebrated with a signature song and dance.

At the memorial, Komphela offered the Adams family a Bible verse as a comfort, but it may as well be a summary. Psalm 23:4: “Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.”

They will know Adams took that walk many times over his short life and he did not fear. He leaves behind his parents, three siblings, a partner, two children and a community who have gone through what no neighbourhood should. In all that, he has gone from not wanting to be known to spending a week in the footballing world’s spotlight. A minute’s silence was observed at several World Cup games in Adams’s memory. That is not the way his family would have pictured him coming to global attention, but it has shown them that, in football, he was always far more valued than anyone thought.

“I don’t think the community knew how big he was and how people enjoyed his football,” says Johnson. “It’s a huge shock.”

Sports.title: Inter enter talks with Tottenham over signing captain Cristian Romero
Sports.content:
Internazionale have entered talks with Tottenham over the potential signing of captain Cristian Romero.

Romero helped Argentina reach a second straight World Cup final earlier this month, but could leave Spurs this summer for a significant fee after an eventful five-year spell.

Centre-back Romero has made 156 appearances since he joined Tottenham in 2021 and guided the club to Europa League success last year, but served four separate suspensions during a difficult 2025-26 campaign.

With Jan Paul van Hecke signed for £52m from Brighton and Marcos Senesi also joining as a free agent in June to boost the defensive options of Roberto De Zerbi’s side, Spurs will let Romero depart and his representatives have been in Milan for talks with Inter this weekend.

Inter’s sporting director, Piero Ausilo, said of Romero to Sky Italy: “It’s definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club [Tottenham]. These things take some time but there’s definitely interest. Let’s see.”

Sports.title: Liverpool start Iraola era in style to beat Sunderland but Gomez injury deepens defensive worries
Sports.content:
The Andoni Iraola era at Liverpool opened with a victory over Sunderland in Nashville – and a deepening of concerns over the defensive options at his disposal. The sight of Joe Gomez hobbling off after 10 minutes of the new head coach’s first game and two teenagers forming a raw central defence partnership in his absence intensified the spotlight on a department in need of work.

Liverpool had few issues at the other end of the pitch against Regis Le Bris’s side, resplendent in pink in Tennessee, where second half finishes from Dominik Szoboszlai, Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas delivered an ultimately comfortable win.

“Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe,” admitted Iraola, who will have been impressed by lively displays from Calum Scanlon, Kieran Morrison and Koumas.

“We were happy because we were going through training without losing any players and unluckily for us we’ve lost Joe straight away.”

View image in fullscreen Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola speaks with Federico Chiesa on Saturday. Photograph: Andrew J Clark/ISI Photos/Getty Images

Geodis Park paid tribute to the late Kevin Keegan before kick-off on Saturday with both sets of supporters applauding the Liverpool, Hamburg and Newcastle great prior to observing an impeccable period of silence in his memory. The crowd itself was sparse, with plenty of empty seats around the 30,000 capacity stadium, although the official attendance was given as 24,897. Charging from $129 to $392 (£96 to £292) for tickets to a pre-season friendly missing its contingent of World Cup players perhaps explains why.

Sunderland were without Granit Xhaka, Brian Brobbey and summer signing Thomas Meunier. Liverpool’s absentee list included World Cup finalists Alexis Mac Allister and Victor Munoz, Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch, who will join the tour next week, and Virgil van Dijk, Cody Gakpo and Alisson, who also resume pre-season training next week but back on Merseyside.

Liverpool also had a summer signing missing. Jeremy Jacquet, acquired for an initial £55m from Rennes, was left out as a precaution but is expected to feature before the tour concludes against Leeds in Chicago next Sunday.

“With Jeremy we decided to take it easy with him,” Iraola explained. “He’s had a lot of months without playing, he’s been training very well, but we’re going to take it easy with him. He will play probably in the last game of this US tour, he will have time to have minutes.”

View image in fullscreen Joe Gomez is helped by trainers after going down early with an injury. Photograph: George Walker IV/AP

Having expressed worry over his “very thin” defensive options earlier in the week, Iraola’s resources were stretched further when Gomez went down injured early on. The luckless Gomez was unable to continue after treatment and his departure meant Liverpool’s central defence comprised two 18-year-olds recruited in January, Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe. Kostas Tsimikas took the captain’s armband from Gomez, then passed it on to Szoboszlai when he was replaced at the interval.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Talla Ndiaye, a £1m signing from Amitie in Senegal, and Ndukwe, a £2.5m transfer from Austria Vienna who only teamed up with Liverpool this summer, reflect Liverpool’s policy of recruiting central defenders for the future. The here and now must also be addressed. With Ibrahima Konate exiting to Real Madrid, Giovanni Leoni yet to resume full training after his ACL injury, Gomez injury prone and Jacquet untested in the Premier League, though rated extremely highly, the responsibility on Van Dijk will be considerable next season. As it was last season.

The answer to the future quiz question of who scored the first goal of the Iraola era at Liverpool is Kieran Morrison. The 19-year-old winger started on the right, also known as the chasm left by Mohamed Salah, and slid a fine finish into the far corner of Melker Ellborg’s goal when released inside the area by Harvey Elliott, another player desperate to impress the new Liverpool head coach following a wasted season at Aston Villa.

View image in fullscreen Jaydon Jones and Timur Tutierov combined for a Sunderland goal. Photograph: Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images

Sunderland equalised in style when Enzo Le Fée broke from midfield and swept a superb shot into Giorgi Mamardashvili’s top corner from 25 yards. Le Bris made 10 changes at half-time, Iraola five, and Sunderland soon took the lead when Jaydon Jones picked out Timur Tutierov inside the area and the striker slotted beyond the Liverpool goalkeeper from 12 yards.

Szoboszlai gave the majority of the crowd what they had paid good money to see when controlling a loose Sunderland clearance 22 yards out and beating Ellborg with a convincing finish. Chiesa steered a clever shot inside the near post from Calvin Ramsay’s pass behind the Sunderland defence before Koumas, released by Szoboszlai, sealed the win.

Sports.title: Tottenham begin tour with victory over Auckland FC in front of record crowd
Sports.content:
Dane Scarlett and Richarlison were on target as an under-strength Tottenham opened their pre-season tour with an entertaining 2-0 win over A-League champions Auckland FC on Sunday.

Spurs coach Roberto De Zerbi rested most of his top players as the Premier League side dominated a match played in damp conditions in front of a record Eden Park crowd. The 40,112 who packed into New Zealand’s famed rugby ground was the biggest to watch a men’s football match in New Zealand.

It surpassed the previous best of 37,034 for a New Zealand World Cup qualifying match against Peru in 2017. They were treated to a fast-paced contest, even if both sides were missing several of their best players.

Tottenham have embarked on an aggressive summer of spending after narrowly avoiding relegation last season, when they finished 17th. However, the only notable new signing to take the field was former West Ham midfielder Mateus Fernandes, who scored in the 1-0 win over MK Dons in London on Wednesday.

De Zerbi said he would ease others into the tour, with Tottenham to play games in Sydney next week against A-League side Sydney FC and London rivals Chelsea.

“It’s a chance for the young players,” De Zerbi told TVNZ before kick-off, declaring Brighton signing Jan Paul van Hecke and former Liverpool stalwart Andy Robertson not yet up to speed. “After a very long trip, we can’t take a risk with the players who are not ready to play yet.”

Record club signing Sandro Tonali wasn’t considered because the former Newcastle United midfielder had suffered an unspecified injury – “one small problem” – before the team left London, De Zerbi added.

Fernandes entered the game with half an hour remaining and Spurs bagged their second goal shortly afterwards through the work of two other substitutes. Mathys Tel burst into the box and set up a tap-in for seasoned forward Richarlison, who was omitted from Brazil’s World Cup squad.

Scarlett, one of several Spurs Academy players in action, opened the scoring in the 12th minute, pouncing after Auckland goalkeeper Michael Woud parried Manor Solomon’s shot.

Sports.title: Arsenal make shock approach to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Arsenal are exploring a shock deal to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid. Arsenal have inquired about the Brazil international, who has one year remaining on his contract at the Bernabéu.

It is believed any move for Vinícius – who scored 22 goals for Real last season and four for Brazil at the World Cup – is at a formative stage as Mikel Arteta seeks a marquee signing to build on the club’s first Premier League title in more than two decades.

The 26-year-old Vinícius fits that bill, with Atlético Madrid’s Julián Álvarez, RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain also on their radar.

Arsenal bolstered their attacking options with the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge this week. Morgan Rogers had also been identified as a target, but it is believed Arsenal were not prepared to pay more than £80m for the England international, who has joined Chelsea in a £117m deal – a British record fee.

Vinícius’s future at Real is uncertain after José Mourinho’s return and the club could cash in on the player, rather than risk losing him for nothing in a year’s time.

Mourinho, who has signed a three-year deal at the Bernabéu, was criticised for comments he made after Vinícius accused Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni of racially abusing him during a Champions League tie in February. Mourinho, Benfica manager at the time, said “something happens, always” in matches where Vinícius plays. Prestianni was banned for six matches after he admitted to using homophobic language towards Vinicius.

Tzolis followed Piero Hincapié – who turned his temporary deal into a full-time switch – and the goalkeeper Illan Meslier, who was out of contract at Leeds, as Arsenal’s third addition.

Bruno Guimarães could also move to the Emirates with Arsenal keen on signing the Brazil international. After Newcastle’s 1-1 pre-season draw at Gateshead on Saturday, Eddie Howe said: “We don’t want to lose our best players. I’ve spoken to him [Guimarães] as I would do. Bruno is just a fantastic person. We’ve had some really good conversations, both before the World Cup, during the World Cup and after the World Cup.

Sports.title: Japan football great ‘King Kazu’ Miura, 59, scores first competitive goal in four years
Sports.content:
Japanese football icon Kazuyoshi Miura scored his first competitive goal ⁠in nearly four years on Saturday, finding the net at the age of ⁠59 as ⁠Fukushima ​United thrashed Iwaki Furukawa 7-0 to advance in the Emperor’s Cup.

Miura, affectionately known ⁠as “King Kazu”, struck in the 52nd minute to put Fukushima 5-0 ahead, capping a trademark ⁠run into the box by meeting a teammate’s ​cutback with a first-time ‌finish at 59 ‌years and 149 days.

The goal sparked celebrations among teammates ‌on the pitch and the bench before the veteran forward was substituted three minutes later.

It was Miura’s first competitive goal since November 2022, when he scored for Suzuka PG, now Atletico Suzuka, in ‌a Japan Football League defeat by FC Osaka.

The former Japan international is preparing for ​a remarkable 42nd season as a professional after extending his loan spell with third-tier Fukushima United until June 2027.

Miura joined the club from Yokohama FC in ⁠December and will remain with Fukushima after making six ​appearances ​during a shortened 2026 ​campaign.

With Japan’s professional leagues set to switch ​from a ‌spring-to-autumn schedule to ​an ​autumn-to-spring calendar, Miura will enter his 60s still playing professionally, adding another chapter to one of football’s most enduring careers.

Sports.title: Defoe’s shock Woking exit came after ‘growing concerns’, says club
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe’s departure from Woking came after “growing concerns” at the club with Jody Brown, the National League side’s director of football, claiming the former Tottenham striker failed to turn up for training.

Defoe’s contract at the National League club was mutually terminated on Thursday after four months in charge. In is first managerial job, the 43-year-old oversaw two wins and one defeat in six matches. The former England forward had said it was “impossible for me to continue” and described his time at the club as an “eye-opening” experience.

But the club responded strongly on Saturday. “The recommendation to appoint Jermain as manager was mine, and I take full responsibility for it,” Brown said. “After meeting with him on several occasions, I believed he was the right person to lead the club into an exciting new era.”

But he went on: “However, in recent weeks there had been feedback from across the club, including players, staff and other departments, regarding growing concerns.

“To better understand the situation, I asked Jermain and Paul [Bracewell, the assistant manager] for a brief report outlining the squad’s current depth, recruitment targets and any operational challenges, so we could provide the support required and accelerate preparations for the season. That report was requested on more than one occasion but was never received.
