“A meeting was subsequently scheduled involving the directors, manager, assistant manager and head of operations to review preparations for the season. Neither Jermain nor his assistant attended that meeting or that day’s training session. Throughout his tenure, Jermain had never communicated any serious concerns directly to me, so I am not going to speculate on his reasons.”



Defoe has not publicly responded to Woking’s claims.

Sports.title: Sunderland star reveals tactical fix Andoni Iraola has made to Liverpool after one game
Sports.content:
Sunderland star reveals tactical fix Andoni Iraola has made to Liverpool after one game

Liverpool are already proving to be a different beast after one pre-season game under Andoni Iraola.

The Reds played their first game under their new boss in a 4-2 victory over Premier League rivals Sunderland on their tour of the USA.

2 Iraola has already been hard at work putting his stamp on the squad Credit: Getty

And Black Cats defender Dan Ballard has admitted the Reds are a different prospect to facing Arne Slot's side last season.

The two teams played out a 1-1 draw at Anfield last December, with a late Nordi Mukiele own-goal rescuing a point for the home side.

Liverpool then became the first team to win away at the Stadium of Light in the Premier League in February after a Virgil van Dijk second-half header edged a 1-0 win.

However, the margin of victory was far greater in the US, with goals from Kieran Morrison, Dominik Szoboszlai, Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas seeing the Reds triumph 4-2.

While the match was only a friendly, Sunderland's Ballard revealed he has already felt the differences between Iraola's and Slot's football.

What has changed for Liverpool?

"I think there's a lot of differences," The 26-year-old told reporters post-match.

"The new gaffer sets the team up in the press very different and he's very intense the way he wants his teams to play.

"We did a lot of work looking at Bournemouth's team last year, and they're very aggressive in the press.

"They play very vertically, and they go straight for goal, which is a little bit different to Slot's team, a little bit more possession-based.

"They gave us a little bit more time on the ball last year, which we were quite surprised at playing Liverpool, knowing them throughout the years."

Former Liverpool talisman Mohamed Salah had previously hinted at the players not being enamoured with Slot's tactics last season.

The Egyptian, who is now a free agent after leaving the club, issued a written statement on social media, appearing to take aim at Slot.

Salah insisted the club should return to their 'heavy metal tactics', a reference to Jurgen Klopp's style of play in his early Anfield years.

Liverpool seemingly agreed by announcing their decision to sack Slot weeks later after concluding that 'the team’s trajectory is best addressed through a change of direction.'

Iraola's front-footed football that proved popular at Bournemouth was quickly identified for the next era at Anfield.

Speaking after his first unofficial win as Liverpool boss, the Spaniard said: "It was difficult to put rhythm into the game.

2 Iraola claimed Liverpool have given themselves a 'good starting point' after beating Sunderland Credit: AFP

"I think both teams were lacking some freshness and it was also humid. The pitch was quite slow.

"We had some good spells on the ball. I think we lacked a little bit of intensity. You can feel the timing is still not there.

"We have to work a lot more, but it's a starting point."

On his team going after the game to try to win in the second half, Iraola added: "It was a matter of using the game to push ourselves and to go back to the rhythm that we should have.

"You play 45, 60 [or] whatever the minutes you play, use them properly.

"It doesn't matter the result, but keep pushing, don't relax, get used to not playing too comfortable. We still have a lot of things to improve."

Sports.title: Arsenal set to step up Bruno Guimaraes transfer chase in bid to end Newcastle standoff
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to step up Bruno Guimaraes transfer chase in bid to end Newcastle standoff

Arsenal are set to accelerate talks for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes in the next week, talkSPORT understands.

The Gunners have made the Magpies captain a priority signing and have hope of striking an agreement before the month is out.

4 Newcastle skipper Guimaraes could be on his way out of St James' Park this summer Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Newcastle insist formal talks are yet to begin, but talkSPORT understands verbal discussions are ongoing with Newcastle's senior leadership now directly involved.

Arsenal to accelerate talks for Bruno Guimaraes

Arsenal are prepared to pay north of £70million, while Guimaraes has already agreed broad terms, as talkSPORT revealed earlier this month.

Newcastle have been left frustrated over speculation regarding Guimaraes' future, and insiders are surprised by Arsenal's lack of a formal bid to date.

Yet Arsenal sources have told talkSPORT three verbal offers have already been placed.

The clubs clearly disagree on what constitutes a bid, which may in part be down to semantics and also the use of intermediaries.

Newcastle can ill afford to lose their captain this summer, having already seen Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon depart.

Star winger Gordon joined Barcelona in a £70m deal, while Tonali moved to Tottenham for a total package worth around £100m.

The departure of Guimaraes would see Newcastle lose two of last season's midfield three, though they have strengthened in that area having brought in Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba from Ajax and Monaco respectively.

Guimaraes still has two years left on his contract, and the Magpies are under no pressure to sell after losing two of their key players already.

4 Arsenal are working hard on their title defence, and want to add Guimaraes to their midfield Credit: Getty

4 The Brazilian helped end a 70-year wait for a major trophy at Newcastle with League Cup glory last year Credit: Getty

Howe will this play out?

With Arsenal stepping up their pursuit of Guimaraes, Newcastle boss Eddie Howe admitted on Saturday he does not know what the future holds for his skipper.

The Magpies played out a 1-1 draw away at Gateshead, and after the match, Howe was asked about his captain.

He said: “I’ve spoken to Bruno before, during and after the World Cup. We have had some really good conversations. He’s just a fantastic person.

“I don’t know what’s going to happen with his future; that’s for other people to speculate about. There’s conversations I’m not part of.

"I don’t think it’s fair to compare (to Isak last summer). You’ve got to look at it in its own right.

“He’s captain of our club and been an unbelievable player, through the whole time we have worked together.

4 Howe is not sure if his captain will stay at the club beyond the summer Credit: Getty

"I speak on behalf of everyone at the club; we absolutely love him, and of course everyone would love him to stay.

“He’s due back on the 31st [of July], and there’s nothing to say he won’t be back.”

talkSPORT understands Newcastle also want quick clarity over Guimaraes' future.

Sources are reticent to compare the situation to the Alexander Isak saga given Newcastle believe Guimaraes won't refuse to participate in pre-season or play for Newcastle again.

He remains a popular member of the dressing room, and Newcastle have received no indication Guimaraes will act anything other than professionally.

However, Newcastle don't want speculation to drag on all summer, while those close to Guimaraes have told talkSPORT he would prefer his future resolved sooner rather than later as well.

The Brazilian is still on a break following the World Cup. Newcastle would be prepared to offer Guimaraes a new deal if he remains.

Newcastle sources also indicate a £70m bid would be rejected, but talkSPORT understands Arsenal are prepared to go higher than this reported number.

Sports.title: Argentina handed automatic World Cup 2030 spot as Gianni Infantino letter leaks
Sports.content:
Argentina will qualify automatically for the 2030 World Cup – despite hosting just one game at the tournament.

The 2030 World Cup, the competition's centenary edition, is being co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco – with three special anniversary games in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay.



3 Argentina reached a second successive World Cup final but were unable to defend their crown Credit: Getty

Uruguay won the inaugural 1930 World Cup, beating Argentina in the final.

Paraguay, meanwhile, is home to the headquarters of South American governing body CONMEBOL, the oldest of the six continental football federations.

Why will Argentina qualify for the 2030 World Cup?

As such, a match is set to be held in each of the three countries' capitals, Montevideo, Buenos Aires and Asuncion.



And, in an unprecedented move, FIFA have confirmed all six host nations will be given an automatic spot at the finals.

The fallout from Argentina's 2026 World Cup final defeat to Spain last weekend continues.



What happened after the 2026 World Cup final?

There were shocking scenes at full-time as scuffles broke out between Argentina players and staff and the victorious Spain team.

Before that, a number of Argentina players celebrated their semi-final win over England by displaying a banner reading 'Las Malvinas son argentinas' ('The Falklands are Argentine'), which the UK government urged FIFA to investigate.



And more controversy has been sparked by FIFA president Gianni Infantino's letter of congratulations to the Argentine FA leaking.

"Dear Mr. President, Yesterday, Sunday, July 19, 2026, at the magnificent New York New Jersey Stadium, Argentina won the silver medal of the FIFA World Cup 2026, after an exciting final against Spain,’ the Daily Mail report Infantino saying.

"I would like to reiterate my most sincere congratulations for this important new result for Argentine soccer.

3 Messi had to settle for a silver medal this time round but Argentina still got a letter from FIFA president Infantino Credit: Getty



"The FIFA World Cup 2026 will remain in memory as an unforgettable celebration of football, marked by spectacular matches, the irruption of new promises, the presence of the great figures of the sport and the extraordinary atmosphere lived in stadiums full of fans.

"The magnificent performance of the Albiceleste also contributed decisively to making this edition an exceptional event that captivated millions of football enthusiasts around the world.

"Please send my sincere congratulations to all who have contributed to this magnificent result: to the players, to coach Lionel Scaloni, as well as to the coaching and medical staff and, of course, to the many fans who have accompanied and encouraged the team throughout the competition.

"These victories are always the fruit of constant work, professionalism and attention to detail, but also of passion, commitment and love for this wonderful sport. All this augurs a very promising future and, without a doubt, will pave the way for new and great successes for Argentine football.



"I wish you, dear Mr. President, all the best for the next competitions and I hope to see you again very soon. With all my friendship, Gianni Infantino."

All three medal-winning nations – including bronze winners England – receive a letter from Infantino, but his message to Argentina was bound to provoke a strong reaction after FIFA opened an investigation into the Albiceleste's behaviour at the end of the final.

3 Argentina's Leandro Paredes (No5) was among those who lashed out after losing the 2026 World Cup final Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, over 20 million people signed a petition calling for Argentina to be permanently banned from the World Cup.



Infuriated football fans had accused FIFA of showing favouritism towards the three-time world champions – who won their most recent title in 2022 – and captain Lionel Messi, allegations FIFA's chief refereeing officer Pierluigi Collina vehemently denied.

The petition has since been closed.

What will the 2030 World Cup look like?

The 2026 World Cup was the biggest edition of the competition yet, increased in size from 32 teams to 48.

But the 2030 tournament looks set to be even bigger and feature 64 teams.

CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez has all but confirmed as much, posting on X: "In 2030, the World Cup comes to Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay, a great opportunity for football to celebrate the World Cup Centenary with a 64-team tournament."



Dominguez's post came as former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, currently FIFA's chief of global football development, lauded the expanded 2026 World Cup as "a great success".

"There were question marks about, 'but the countries were not good enough', and they were given the answer. Not only have they shown that they were good enough, but they gave some great games and entertainment," he said.

Sports.title: 2034 World Cup final venue to be one of world’s biggest arenas as host nation pours $26bn into project
Sports.content:
The 2034 World Cup is part of an unprecedented investment program that will transform Saudi Arabia.

2034 World Cup final venue to be one of world’s biggest arenas as host nation pours $26bn into project

Saudi Arabia is pulling out all the stops for the 2034 World Cup.

Much like Qatar in 2022, a massive nationwide building program will create the necessary infrastructure from the ground up.

4 King Salman Stadium is known as the ‘germinating seed’ Credit: Populous

The tournament will be held across 15 stadiums, with eight being built from scratch, three already in progress and four current venues being renovated.

King Salman International Stadium will be the pick of the bunch.

With around 92,000 seats, it will be one of the world's biggest football stadiums, albeit considerably smaller than the one Morocco hopes will host the 2030 final.

The project is being built north of Riyadh City with an estimated completion date of 2029.

A royal box will hold 150 guests, with 120 hospitality suites, three hundred VIP seats, and two thousand premium spaces to allow FIFA to host plenty of dignitaries -- and likely streamers.

Sustainable cooling systems will work on the seats and the ground, with screens and indoor gardens helping to keep it cool.

The tournament will likely take place in winter -- and may even be in 2035 -- when temperatures should be comfortable enough for fans to enjoy a rooftop walking path overlooking King Abdulaziz Park.

Saudi Arabia is keen to ensure the legacy of the tournament benefits future generations and King Salman International Stadium will be surrounded by training pitches, fan zones, an Olympic swimming pool and athletics track, as well as facilities for racket sports and basketball.

A sports trail over five miles long will connect the stadium and nearby park.

All of this comes at a price.

4 Fans will be able to walk on the roof Credit: Populous

4 92,000 fans will be kept out of the harsh sun Credit: Populous

Along with the stadiums, the country needed to build 65,000 new hotel rooms to meet FIFA's expectations.

SNB Capital estimated the total cost of hosting the tournament at $26 billion.

The hope is that the World Cup will be the culmination of an ambitious repositioning that began in 2019 when the Kingdom's Public Investment Fund launched a project called Vision 2030, hoping to turn it into a sport and entertainment hub.

By 2030, the sector is expected to provide $16.5 billion in benefits, accounting for 1.5 per cent of the national GDP, and create 100,000 jobs.

Saudi citizens have seen participation rates in physical activities increase dramatically with 50 per cent of the population now exercising regularly, up from 13 per cent in 2015.

Female participation has also increased by 400 per cent since 2015.

4 Designs show a thriving mixed-use development Credit: Populous

Esports and digital gaming form another prong of the project with $38 billion allocated.

The Kingdom has already hosted the Esports World Cup.

Can 2034 World Cup be moved?

A report from American outlet Politico has revealed an 'unprecedented scheduling dilemma.'

The Qatar World Cup was held from November 20 to December 18, which will clash with Ramadan in 2034.

Earlier in the year, the Winter Olympics is slated for January and February and March sees around two million pilgrims head to Mecca for Hajj.

Politico suggests that between Christmas 2034 and Hajj -- set for mid-February in 2035 -- could be the most logical window, which could be too short to fit in an expanded tournament with FIFA keen on 48 or even 64 teams.

Sports.title: Liverpool star who only joined last summer among three players fighting for immediate future
Sports.content:
Liverpool star who only joined last summer among three players fighting for immediate future

Liverpool's new era under Andoni Iraola unofficially gets under way this weekend with the club's first pre-season game.

The ex-Bournemouth head coach has been eager to dish out fresh starts for several players, who were fringe players in the old regime.

7 Iraola has a completely different project at Liverpool than he did at Bournemouth Credit: Getty

What's happened at Liverpool?

The Reds have been cleaning house following Arne Slot's sacking last month, with a host of background staff also relieved of their duties.

Michael Edwards has stepped down as Fenway Sports Group's (FSG) CEO of football, while sporting director Richard Hughes has been linked with a move to Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal.

Meanwhile, a consortium backed by the Mittal family are also in talks to buy a minority stake in Liverpool, talkSPORT understands.

On the pitch, Iraola has taken charge of a Liverpool team in transition, with Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson, and Ibrahima Konate all departing at the end of last season.

The Spaniard has brought Tommy Elphick from Bournemouth as a first-team coach, but transfer activity remains thin on the ground.

Jeremy Jacquet has officially arrived from Rennes after a deal for the 21-year-old was agreed on deadline day of the winter window.

During the World Cup, Liverpool then signed Spain's Victor Munoz, having successfully hijacked Newcastle's move for the winger.

However, Iraola's pre-season squad - made even thinner by stars on an extended break following their international exploits - has provided an opportunity for fringe players to stake their claims.

Here, talkSPORT.com runs through three players who have the most to prove to their new boss that they should be in next season's plans.

7 Szoboszlai won't have to worry after underlining his importance to Liverpool's project with his new contract Credit: Getty

Trey Nyoni: 'Pre-season tour is an opportunity'

The 19-year-old understandably realises that the Reds' pre-season tour of the USA is an ideal opportunity to prove his qualities to Iraola.

He told Liverpoolfc.com: “It’s exciting times ahead. It’s been good to be back and to see everyone again, and I’m ready to go.

“There are still a few players away [due to the World Cup] so obviously there’s an opportunity to play [in the USA] and just show what I can do in that sense.

“But I’ll just go out there and just enjoy it and just try to do my best.”

Nyoni was one of two Liverpool starlets tipped for a breakout season in 2025/26, with the other living up to the billing in Rio Ngumoha.

7 Nyoni wasn't afforded the opportunities Ngumoha was to steal the spotlight Credit: Getty

He impressed in Arne Slot's first pre-season in 2024, but made just five senior outings, with his fortunes unchanged last campaign.

The England U19 international only managed six Premier League appearances last season - which added up to a combined 21 minutes.

Now, with Curtis Jones looking increasingly likely to stay amid interest from Inter, a pathway to a midfield spot at Liverpool remains blocked.

For Nyoni, a move to Swansea City has been mooted, with former Anfield coach Vitor Matos in charge of the Championship outfit.

The ex-Leicester City academy talent will have a major opportunity in the USA to convince Iraola his immediate future is at Liverpool.

7 Nyoni made 14 senior appearances across all competitions last season

Elliott 'will have a chance during pre-season'

This time last year, Harvey Elliott had the world at his feet after his starring role in the Young Lions' defence of their U21 Euro title.

The 23-year-old was named the player of the tournament after scoring five goals for Lee Carsley's side - which was second only to Newcastle's record signing, Nick Woltemade.

His standout success escalated his ambition to leave boyhood club Liverpool, having made just six starts in the 2024/25 season.

He ultimately joined Aston Villa on deadline day on an initial loan with a £35million obligation to buy once he made 10 league appearances.

Unfortunately for Elliott, Unai Emery quickly stated publicly that his side had no interest in signing him from Liverpool permanently.

7 Elliott effectively lost a year of his career after being exiled at Villa Credit: Getty

Villa's stance meant the Fulham academy talent was either excluded from most matchday squads or left languishing on the bench.

Elliott played just 13 Premier League minutes from the end of September until returning to Liverpool for pre-season this summer.

The attacker only has one-year remaining on his Anfield contract, but new boss Iraola has claimed he will receive a genuine chance during pre-season rather than being forced straight back out the door.

“Harvey is here with us. He has come [in early] also,” Iraola told reporters in his first press conference earlier this month.

“I’ve seen him with this eagerness to show himself, to get himself ready again. He will have a chance during the pre-season; we will need him.

“It’s a good sign that he came a week earlier; he’s been training with the under-21s, and I hope we can see him in a good place.

“I think Harvey, last season, had to be very difficult for him, because it was a strange situation where basically they couldn’t even put him in to play.

“I think he uses what he has experienced, the bad situation, to make him even more eager to be a Liverpool player, yes.”

7 Elliott returned early to pre-season and began preparatory work with Liverpool's U21 squad Credit: Getty

Frimponged

Jeremie Frimpong was the first arrival of the Reds' record-breaking £416m summer spend 12 months ago.

The Netherlands international had the best opportunity to hit the ground running as the replacement for Trent Alexander-Arnold.

He scored in the Community Shield loss to Crystal Palace in August, but then suffered an injury on his Premier League debut.

That proved a sign of things to come, as Frimpong tweaked his hamstring in a 5-1 win at Eintracht Frankfurt in mid-September.

His second injury ensured that the Dutchman didn't start another Premier League game until after Christmas.

7 Frimpong had an injury-plagued first season as a Liverpool player Credit: Getty

A third hamstring setback in January only compounded his issues, and Frimpong ultimately missed out on a place in the World Cup.

In total, the former Bayer Leverkusen man started just 12 Premier League games, of which only seven were at right-back.

Conor Bradley remains a long-term absentee after suffering serious bone and ligament damage in his knee in January, with midfielders Jones and Dominik Szoboszlai forced to deputise in the position.

Iraola has already confirmed that the Reds are looking to find a solution at right-back, which could spell bad news for Frimpong.

"So with the centre-back and the right-back situations in terms of defensive depth, we are, I think, really thin right now, and it is a solution we are trying to find, yes," he said.

This pre-season will be a vital opportunity for Frimpong to see if he can convince Iraola that an understudy, not a replacement, is needed.

Sports.title: Liverpool fan tells club to avoid signing Vinicius Jr because 17-year-old star will be better
Sports.content:
Liverpool fan tells club to avoid signing Vinicius Jr because 17-year-old star will be better

Liverpool wouldn't sign Vinicius Jr because Rio Ngumoha will surpass him as one of the world's best footballers.

That's the confident view of one Reds fan, who called into talkSPORT following the news of interest in Vinicius Jr from Arsenal.

3 Vinicius Jr has emerged as a shock target for Arsenal Credit: Getty

The Premier League champions are understood to be contemplating a move for the Real Madrid winger this summer.

Vinicius Jr, who is regarded as one of the best players on the planet, is into the final year of his contract at the Bernabeu.

Liverpool have been offered the chance to sign the 26-year-old, but chose not to pursue a deal.

And supporter Paul has explained that there is no need for them to do so, because he believes teenage star Ngumoha is the real deal.

"There's two reasons why Liverpool wouldn't sign a player like Vinicius Jr," he said on The Transfer Insiders. "Number one, he's a bad seed for the dressing room.

"But, more importantly, he's nowhere near as good as what Rio Ngumoha's going to prove to be, nowhere near."

Ngumoha signed for Liverpool from Chelsea in 2024 and has since made 30 senior appearances for the club.

He scored the winner in a 3-2 victory over Newcastle United on his Premier League debut in August.

The winger later became the youngest player to score his first goal at Anfield in a 2-0 win against Fulham.

England boss Thomas Tuchel then handed him his first international cap in the 1-0 pre-World Cup friendly win versus New Zealand.

3 One Liverpool fan believes Ngumoha will become better than Vinicius Jr Credit: Getty

Other side of the coin

Arsenal are yet to engage in club-to-club talks for Vinicius Jr, who has 128 goals and 100 assists for Madrid in 375 appearances.

He is also viewed as an option for the Gunners rather than a number one target.

However, with Madrid working to sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, the possibility of Vinicius Jr leaving could increase.

It would be a statement signing for Arsenal, and one Gunners fan went as far as to say that he could reach deity status.

"I've got to be a little bit balanced, because obviously there's a long way to go," Nicholas said when asked about his excitement for a deal.

"But this will be the first time, I think, in our history that we've signed not just a good player, but the best player from one of the biggest clubs in European football.

3 Arsenal would arguably make the signing of the summer if they brought in Vinicius Jr Credit: Getty

"It just doesn't happen, usually it's the other way around. We're so used to Manchester City and Real Madrid hand-picking all of our best players.

"It wasn't too long ago when we had to sell players because we couldn't afford to keep them, or we weren't good enough. Now, we are the Premier League champions, the best team in England by far.

"And we have a unique opportunity because he's only got one year left on his contract.

"Real Madrid cannot afford to let one of their biggest assets go away for nothing, so it all comes down to what Vini wants, really.

"Does he want to become number two at Real Madrid, number two to (Kylian) Mbappe?

"Or does he want to come to Arsenal and become, pretty much, a footballing God?"

Sports.title: Erling Haaland reveals Hollywood actor once tried to convince him to join Tottenham
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland reveals Hollywood actor once tried to convince him to join Tottenham

Tom Holland may well be Spider-Man, but even his super powers were unable to convince Erling Haaland to join Tottenham Hotspur.

The Hollywood megastar is an avid Spurs fan, and once admitted that his support of the club has taught him a key lesson in resilience.



4 Holland was among the stars to attend the glitzy Monaco Grand Prix in 2021 Credit: Getty

4 Haaland was also there, but Holland couldn't get a hold of him Credit: Getty

Holland attended the 2021 Monaco Grand Prix and spotted Haaland who, at the time, was a rising talent in football at Borussia Dortmund.

He just scored a stunning 41 goals in as many appearances during the 2020/21 season before visiting Monte Carlo for the Formula 1 race.



Eyeing an opportunity to meet, Holland messaged the Norwegian on Instagram but, despite being universally renowned, nothing arose.

Haaland admitted on A Laget that he didn't know who he was, and therefore chose not to respond to the message.



Holland then admitted to contacting him during an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon.

"That is exactly the type of humbling experience that is important for actors," he humorously explained amid a lack of response.



Haaland reacted to the interview on his YouTube channel and was on hand to reveal what Holland penned in his unsuccessful message.

"'Hiya mate, just saw you in Monaco," Holland wrote.

"If you want to grab a drink or something, give me a shout. And please come join Spurs.'"

"I don't watch Spiderman," Haaland explained, before addressing a claim that said he thought Holland was 'a random person'.

"I said it in a funny way, but it got taken out of context. I sounded a bit rude, I even sent him a message because I felt bad...



4 Holland attempted to inspire Haaland to join Spurs, but he later chose City Credit: Getty

"'There's a story going out that I was ignoring you. Just want to make sure that wasn't my intention or whatever...'"

Haaland then recalled how he responded to Holland's request for him to sign for Spurs, before joining Manchester City a year later.

"And by the way, not too sure about Spurs at the moment, but who knows in the future?'"



Spider-Man meets Erling?

After recalling his failed attempt to message Haaland, Holland was asked if he would still like to go to dinner with the football sensation.

However, the interview took place days after England beat Norway 2-1 in the World Cup quarter-finals, so he was unsure of its possibility.

"I don't think he would have dinner with me after the other day," he said, before agreeing that Haaland would be 'hurting' from the loss.

4 Thanks to the power of social media, Holland is finally set to meet Haaland Credit: Getty



The story of the thwarted meet in Monaco was uploaded onto social media, and caught Haaland's attention.

In the comments on the Instagram posted, he tagged Holland and said: "Dinner invitation accepted. A little late. Just name the place!"

Sports.title: Sorry Morgan Rogers, you're wrong. Here's the definitive proof that Arsenal are the BIGGEST team in London as James Sharpe gives Chelsea's record signing a history lesson
Sports.content:
Sorry Morgan Rogers, you're wrong. Here's the definitive proof that Arsenal are the BIGGEST team in London as James Sharpe gives Chelsea's record signing a history lesson

Thanks a bunch, Morgan. Kick the hornets’ nest, why don’t you.

‘I am joining the biggest club in London,’ declared Morgan Rogers after completing his £117million British record transfer to Chelsea from Aston Villa. Perhaps he genuinely means it. Perhaps you’re contractually obliged to say it when your new club fork out quite so much for you.

Elliot Anderson did his bit after his £116m move to Manchester City, too. ‘For as long as I’ve known, Manchester, City have been the Kings of Manchester,’ said the lad born in 2002.

Anyway, back to London. Rogers’ bold claim about a club that finished 33 points behind actual Premier League champions Arsenal last season stoked up all the old feelings and arguments. So, who are the biggest club in London?

Daily Mail Sport have donned a tin hat and bravely taken it upon ourselves to provide the definitive answer to the most divisive of questions…

Morgan Rogers boldly declared he had joined London's biggest club after completing a £117m move to Chelsea, but Arsenal will also stake their claim for that title

Trophies

What do the biggest clubs do? They win stuff. And the more you win, the more your reputation grows, as do your coffers, and your size.

But it also depends on what you win. A case full of League Cups and Community Shields is far less impressive than one of Premier League trophies and European Cups.

Arsenal have more than double the league titles of Chelsea, won over a far longer period of time, and almost twice as many FA Cups. Domestically, there is only one winner.

HONOURS Competition Arsenal Chelsea Premier League/First Division 14 6 Champions League/European Cup 0 2 FA Cup 14 8 League Cup 2 5 Europa League 0 2 UEFA Conference League 0 1 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup 1 2 Club World Cup 0 2 UEFA Super Cup 0 2 Full Members' Cup 0 2 Inter Cities' Fairs Cup 1 0 Community Shield 17 4

Only, isn’t being champions of Europe (or the world) bigger than being champions of England? Arsenal’s continental shortcoming is their glaring weak spot. The biggest clubs have won the European Cup. Arsenal haven’t.

A penalty shootout against Paris Saint-Germain away from glory, of course, but Tottenham have won a European trophy more recently, so have West Ham, so have Crystal Palace.

Chelsea have two Champions Leagues, two Europa Leagues, even a Conference League.

They boasted that they are the only club in history to win every major European trophy, which, more than anything, made you spare a thought for fans of the Inter Cities Fairs Cup.

As soon as Gabriel sent his penalty high into the stands, Chelsea posted an invitation to book a stadium tour at ‘London’s Home of Trophies’, with Big Ears front and centre.

They are two-time Club World Cup winners, too, which sounds cool but is only starting to feel important now that there’s £100m to win.

Verdict: Tie

Arsenal have more than double the league titles of Chelsea and almost twice as many FA Cups

Chelsea, however, have won the Champions League twice with Arsenal's contiential shortcomings their glaring weak spot

League position

Gravitas comes with a weight of history, too. That all but one of Chelsea’s league titles have been since 2005, with a Russian oligarch signing bigger cheques than anyone else, will tell you that time is on Arsenal’s side.

Since Arsenal joined the Football League in 1893, their average league position is 8.3. Across Chelsea’s history, theirs is 12.7. Tottenham’s is 11.7.

Across the 110 seasons in which both clubs have existed, Arsenal have finished higher in 77 of them.

Even in the Premier League era, when Chelsea stormed to power, the two clubs have split a higher finish 17 times apiece, though 16 of those for the Blues’ came across an 18-season period from 2004-05 to 2022-23.

However, Arsenal’s average position of 3.8 across the entire Premier League era still betters Chelsea’s of 5.

And even now Arsenal are current champions, after finishing second three times, during which time Chelsea finished 10th and 12th.

Verdict: Arsenal

Across the 110 seasons in which both clubs have existed, Arsenal have finished higher in 77 of them

Stadium and crowd

There’s simply no comparison between the Emirates Stadium, which Arsenal moved into in 2006, and Stamford Bridge. Bigger, better, fuller.

There was a brief five-year period before Arsenal’s move during which Chelsea boasted the marginally bigger crowds but, across history, the Gunners have had the greater attendances.

Chelsea’s average crowd even dropped below 13,000 in the early 1980s. Until Chelsea get an extension, or move, they cannot compete with Arsenal. Or Tottenham.

Yes, you can suggest, as the club’s supporters’ trust did during the malaise of Wenger’s final years, that Arsenal have not always been completely honest with their attendance figures — filled seats or tickets sold — but when the club’s fans come out they do so in force. Islington Council estimated more than a million people turned up for their Premier League title bus parade.

When Chelsea had theirs in 2015, official numbers were around 70,000. Around 200,000 turned up for their first under Jose Mourinho in 2005.

Verdict: Arsenal

There is no comparison between Arsenal's Emirates Stadium and Stamford Bridge

Over a million people reportedly attended Arsenal's Premier League title parade in May

Spending Power

The biggest clubs splash the biggest cash, right? Few spend it like Chelsea. As we saw with Rogers, they have the power to do it from right under Arsenal’s noses.

What began under Abramovich has continued into the BlueCo years. Chelsea’s net spend — that’s NET spend — over the past five years is more than £800m, nearly £150m more than any other Premier League side and £262m more than Arsenal.

Chelsea announced a Premier League-record pre-tax loss of £262.4m earlier this year for the 2024-25 season. They have spent well over a billion but not much of it well.

BIGGEST SIGNINGS Arsenal Fee Chelsea Fee Declan Rice £105m Morgan Rogers £117m Nicolas Pepe £72m Moises Caicedo £115m Eberechi Eze £67.5m Enzo Fernandez £106.8m Kai Havertz £65m Romelu Lukaku £97.5m Viktor Gyokeres £64m Mykhaylo Mudryk £88.5m Martin Zubimendi £60m Kai Havertz £75.8m Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang £55.4m Wesley Fofana £75m Noni Madueke £52m Kepa £71.6m

Kieran Maguire, the football finance expert, recently listed the biggest wage bills in Premier League history, adjusted for football inflation and the spending power clubs had at the time.

Chelsea made up eight of the top 10 with all their seasons from 2003-04 to 2010-11 at the height of their Abramovich era.

Arsenal’s first appearance on the list, their 2011-12 season, is in 51st place. Ahead of them are 16 different Chelsea seasons, 17 Manchester United seasons, 12 Manchester City seasons and five Liverpool seasons.

And yet over previous two sets of results, Arsenal have blown Chelsea out of the water in terms of their revenue: £691m to £491m.

Declan Rice is the only Arsenal signing of more than £100m.

Chelsea now have three: Rogers, Moises Caicedo and Enzo Fernandez. Their top seven all come in higher than Arsenal’s second most expensive arrival in £72m Nicolas Pepe. If they are to get Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, they will have to go higher than that.

Verdict: Chelsea

Chelsea showed their financial power by signing Rogers from right under Arsenal nose

Rogers is one of three Chelsea players to cost over £100m, while Rice is Arsenal's only one

Star Power

Big spending brings big names and big managers. In the Premier League era, Arsenal have had Wenger, Unai Emery and Mikel Arteta in the dugout. Chelsea have had Mourinho (twice), Carlo Ancelotti, Rafa Benitez, Antonio Conte and Thomas Tuchel. The biggest names in the game. But then they have also had Graham Potter and Liam Rosenior.

On the pitch, few have ever had the aura of Thierry Henry, Dennis Bergkamp or Patrick Vieira. Saka will be next. Chelsea will point to Didier Drogba and Eden Hazard. And Cole Palmer, perhaps?

Arsenal have taken a couple of Chelsea’s cast-offs in recent years, too, with Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke, and yet they are both now champions.

Arsenal lead the way, too, when it comes to producing England stars. Rice, Madueke, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze’s involvement in the World Cup quarter-final against Norway, took the club past 1,000 caps for Arsenal players.

Chelsea, the first club to field an all-foreign team, in 1999, stand at less than 750.

Verdict: Tie

Jose Mourinho is among a host of big name managers to have taken charge of Chelsea

Few can match the aura of former Arsenal stars Thierry Henry, Dennis Bergkamp and Patrick Vieira

Social Media

The true test of how big a club is in the modern era is, surely, how many followers they have on social media.

I would have staked everything on Arsenal winning this. Few supporter groups make their voices quite so piercingly heard than the Gunners’, and certainly when they feel, as they often do, that they have been wronged or robbed.

And, yet, Chelsea win on all counts. They have more followers on X, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube, to the combined tune of more than 33 million.

Verdict: Chelsea

Insider’s view

It’s clear they both crave the title. Chelsea previously trademarked their ‘CFC LDN’ branding — what better way to prove you’re London’s big dogs? ‘There’s only one answer,’ replied one Arsenal source when posed the question.

‘The way Arsenal conduct themselves comes from a place of prestige,’ a prominent agent who has dealt with both clubs tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Chelsea have more of a big-club approach in the way they get things done. They are very much: if we want the player, we will do what it takes to get them. Put our cards on the table. That is a big-club mentality.

‘There’s definitely two different cultures, through which both see themselves as the biggest club in London but go about it in a different way. Arsenal are like your old money, slightly entitled aristocrat who can fall back on title and family history. Chelsea are the nouveau riche, super successful city worker who isn’t shy about showing off how much money they have and uses that to drive more success.’

Elon Musk might be the richest man in the world and Tesla the largest automobile company by market capitalisation, whatever that means, but good luck convincing anyone they are really bigger than Mercedes or Ferrari.

Verdict: Arsenal

Sorry Morgan, your new club may be big spenders but most metrics confirm the Gunners are the capital’s major players.

Overall verdict: Arsenal

Sports.title: Simon Jordan airs Anthony Joshua conspiracy theory after boxer knocked out rival despite hitting the canvas TWICE to set up money-spinning Tyson Fury fight: 'Something not quite right'
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan has questioned the nature of Anthony Joshua's victory over Kristian Prenga as he recovered from two knockdowns to set up a lucrative showdown with Tyson Fury.

Joshua, who had been returning to the ring after seven months of inactivity, appeared on the brink of defeat in the opening round against Prenga.

The Albanian heavyweight knocked Joshua down just 20 seconds into the contest with an uppercut.

Joshua then survived another knockdown later in the round, with fans fearing the long-awaited showdown with Fury was at risk.

The second round proved dramatically different as Joshua unleashed a series of heavy blows to force Prenga towards the ropes, before delivering a knockout blow.

Joshua's stunning turnaround, coupled with Fury's victory over Mariusz Wach just 24 hours earlier, cleared the path for the two British heavyweights to finally meet in one of the most lucrative fights in boxing.

Anthony Joshua survived two knock downs in the first round against Kristian Prenga

Joshua responded in the second by delivering a second round knockout of the Albanian

Simon Jordan questioned the nature of Joshua's victory given the difference between the two rounds

talkSPORT presenter Simon Jordan controversially questioned the dramatic difference in the rounds between Joshua and Prenga.

Jordan declared 'something not quite right' as he appeared to reference the sums on offer for Joshua's fight with Fury.

'Not having that… #anthonyjoshua fight,' Jordan posted.

'Dropped twice and sets the tempo, how's that ? … Prenga totally different in 2nd

'Something not quite right, all designed to rinse maximum amount of money…'

Punch stats for the fight revealed the stunning difference between the two rounds, with Joshua landing just five of his 22 attempted punches in the first, while Prenga connected with 15 of his 32.

The second round swung with Joshua landing with 13 of his 46 punches, as Prenga dramatically dropped off by landing three of 17 attempted.

Despite Jordan's comments on social media, Joshua insisted that 'champions rise' in a post-fight interview after coming through the test.

Prenga had stunned Joshua in the opening round and landed 13 of his 32 attempted punches

He landed just three of 17 punches in the second round as Joshua became the aggressor

Prenga was sent to the canvas by a brutal blow from Joshua, who later declared 'champions rise' when asked about the dramatic turnaround

'He [Prenga] gave me a good test but this is what champions do, we rise,' Joshua said.

'We get knocked down and stand up. That is life, that is life's motto.

'I want to give a massive thank you to Prenga and his team for putting up a good fight. It means a lot to them and it means a lot to me and that is why you see what you see in the ring.

'I want to give thanks to God. It was more than me in that situation, it can't just be me in them type of situations. There is a higher power that is calling.

'He's a strong guy and I think Eddie [Hearn] wants to sign him now! He is going to do well and he has a bright future.

'Maybe with a bit more experience, he [Prenga] will be up there with the rest of us. He is strong and durable.'

Looking ahead to the showdown with Fury, with contracts having already been signed, Joshua said in the ring: 'Have we got Tyson Fury in the room? Is he here or not?

'I am the meanest, most vicious champion. Nobody can stop me. He is no Oleksandr [Usyk].

'All jokes aside, there are two sides. One is the fighter and the other is respect. I respect everything he has done and everything that he has achieved, but as a fighting person, we're here now.

'I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat.'

Joshua had paid tribute to his two close friends, who were killed in a car crash in December.

Joshua will finally face Tyson Fury in a money-spinning contest with his rival having beaten Mariussz Wach a day earlier

Joshua paid tribute to his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele, who died in a car crash in December

Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele died while the car they were travelling in struck a truck on a road near Lagos in December. The pair were on holiday with Joshua after he beat Jake Paul in Miami.

The heavyweight boxer, who was also in the vehicle, was taken to hospital before being discharged and flying home to the UK - where he attended the funerals of his strength and conditioning coach Ghami and Ayodele, one of his trainers.

Fighting in honour of Ghami and Ayodele, Joshua paid tribute to his friends by having their names printed on his military camouflage trunks.

He also walked to the ring wearing a military-style jacket to match his camo shorts. The jacket featured a medal bar displaying the IBF, IBO, WBA, and WBO titles - which he previously held - alongside pennants bearing Ghami and Ayodele's names.

Meanwhile, ‘Latz x Sina, My Brother's Keeper, MBK’ was printed on the canvas in his corner.

Asked about how he has been coping after beating Prenga, Joshua said: 'It's been tough,' before becoming emotional. 'That's my brothers. I don't want to talk about that.'

Speaking on DAZN, Matchroom Boxing chief Eddie Hearn admitted he feared the heavyweight had returned to the ring too soon after witnessing his struggles in the opening round.

'Nobody can imagine what he's been through in that last seven months. In that first round, I thought we'd come back too soon,' Hearn said.

'Boxing got him through. To even be in the ring tonight is astonishing. You don't know what he's been through. He had to go to the depths one more time to get up, like he has done the last seven months.'

In February, Joshua memorialised Ghami and Ayodele by having their names tattooed on his arm.

Sports.title: 'F*** you and them': Jermaine Jenas hits back at his critics in bizarre pancake video after former BBC star's car-crash Good Morning Britain interview
Sports.content:
'F*** you and them': Jermaine Jenas hits back at his critics in bizarre pancake video after former BBC star's car-crash Good Morning Britain interview

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jermaine Jenas has unequivocally hit back at his critics in bizarre fashion after uploading a topless video of himself dancing in his kitchen.

Former England and Spurs star Jenas, 43, was one of the BBC's rising stars before he was axed from his role on Match of the Day in August 2024 following the discovery of inappropriate messages sent to two women.

Jenas had served as a regular presenter on The One Show and 5Live before his wife, Ellie Penfold, confirmed she had split from the former footballer in the wake of the scandal - having been together for 16 years.

He is now in a relationship with Parisien estate agent Anne Leplaideur, 31, with the pair spotted holidaying together this summer.

He spoke at length about how he had 'lost everything' during his 'tough two-year period' in a car-crash appearance on ITV's Good Morning Britain last month, in which he was grilled by presenters Kate Garraway and Ranvir Singh.

Jenas took issue with Singh's 'line of questioning' and later claimed the presenters had 'a thirst for blood', with the former footballer accused of 'skirting around the issue' of his behaviour and responding to questions in a defensive manner.

Jermaine Jenas has hit back at his critics in a defiant Instagram message on Saturday

But taking to Instagram on Saturday, Jenas posted a defiant message while dancing and spinning a plate of white chocolate pancakes.

'I no longer care how the story gets told,' the caption read. 'F*** you and them… Respectfully.'

Rio Ferdinand responded to the post by saying: 'Okaaaaay… these tunes don't fit the caption ffs.'

The ITV interview saw Garraway ask Jenas what he had 'learned'. Jenas replied: 'To say I was happy in the industry I was in is an overstatement. When it comes to what I've learnt, it's a very specific thing to put my finger on.

'It's probably a little bit of an unfair question to find that one thing. You go through life, you make mistakes and there were things happening on the outside of work also affecting my behaviour.'

Singh then accused him of 'skirting around what you've learnt', but Jenas responded: 'I'm not skirting around anything, Ranvir.

'I'm more than happy to have the conversation, which is why I'm here. I'm not here to be defending myself in any way, shape or form.

The 43-year-old ex-footballer was grilled during a car-crash interview on GMB last month

He was accused of 'skirting around the issue' of his BBC sacking in August 2024

'I know what I did was wrong and I accept those punishments. Nobody is skirting around the responsibility of what I did. I know what I did and I know what I did was wrong. So I don't understand where that line of questioning is coming from.'

Singh then asked him for his 'advice to other men who are in positions of power in any industry and who think they are just flirting with women at work who… what is your advice to other people then who might be learning from your mistakes?'

Jenas replied: 'I think they can look at what happened to me and make their own assumptions about what they have to do with their own lives.

'I'm not here to preach to other people about what they should do with their lives. I'm here to explain to people my own experiences of what I've been through and what I've done and the impact that it's had on everybody in my life.

'I'm not here to dictate to people in terms of what they want to do. I understand why you have to come at me with this line of questioning and it's completely fine and if you feel like I have not been punished enough then go ahead and keep going.'

Singh said she was 'not saying that', adding that Jenas had spoken about 'what's been taken away from me' – but 'people might say you put yourself in that position, you risked it all by doing what you did'.

Jenas replied: 'Oh, 100 per cent. I did put myself in that position and I'm not sat here begging and pleading for my job back.

'I'm fully accepting of what has been taken away from me. I put myself in that position and that's where the learning comes from – and that's where I have to now look forward to what is coming next. That's where the post comes from.

Jenas, 43, split from wife Ellie Penfold after inappropriate messages sent to two women were discovered

'It's impossible to not learn about yourself when you are put into the position that I was put into, that I put myself into. You have to take stock, look around yourself, look at your own behaviour and realise that things have to change.

'I've done that over a period of time where it's been very tricky – granted I put myself in that position.'

Jenas deflected throughout his ten-minute interview, pleading for forgiveness because everyone 'makes mistakes'.

The 43-year-old learnt of his sacking from the BBC while live on radio.

He added: 'The learning from it doesn't always have to be negative. We are so obsessed in this industry with "oh, he's been cancelled" – everything has to be negative.

'Hang on a minute, I'm a person who has learnt a lot from my mistakes and spent ten to 12 years in this industry and had a brilliant career and really enjoyed my time on television. There's a lot for me to give back.

'I'm not saying on television, it could be on any different platform where I know a lot of people feel how I feel.

'I'm a human being. We make mistakes. You two [Singh and Garraway] can't sit in front of me and say you've never made a mistake in your life. We all make mistakes, we live in the public eye.

'Every mistake I made was made public and I had to handle that as a man. That's exactly what I did. The thing now is about moving forward and what I'm about to do next. Currently, I'm not sure.'

Sports.title: World Cup hero Vozinha, 40 - who gained 29MILLION followers after denying Lionel Messi - set to join iconic South American club despite links to David Beckham's Inter Miami
Sports.content:
World Cup hero Vozinha, 40 - who gained 29MILLION followers after denying Lionel Messi - set to join iconic South American club despite links to David Beckham's Inter Miami

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

World Cup cult hero Vozinha is set to complete a move to famous Chilean side Colo Colo despite links to David Beckham's Inter Miami.

The 40-year-old was one of the heroes of Cape Verde's surprise run to the last-32 stage before they were beaten 3-2 by Argentina after extra-time.

As well as keeping a clean sheet against Spain and Saudi Arabia, Vozinha made 18 saves across the tournament and outperformed his xG against by 0.9.

His standout performances were among the highlights of Cape Verde's debut appearance at the World Cup.

At the start of the Spain match in Cape Verde's World Cup opener, he only had 50,000 followers on Instagram, but after making a memorable seven saves, that number dramatically increased, with Vozinha now having 28.6million followers.

FIFA announced last week that Vozinha had been named in the World Cup's team of the tournament.

Vozinha is expected to join Chilean side Colo Colo despite links to David Beckham's Inter Miami

The keeper was one of the stars of Cape Verde's run to the last-32 stage of the World Cup

Vozinha had been without a club heading into the tournament after leaving Portuguese second division team Chaves at the end of last season.

His availability led to speculation over a possible move to join Messi at Inter Miami, with Vozinha asked about the possibility in a television appearance after the tournament.

'I love football to still be here at 40 years old is because I truly have this passion,' Vozinha said.

'I want to play for at least another one or two years, depending on how my body feels and reacts.

'We never know what tomorrow brings, but I want to keep playing.

'I just hope I can find a club that truly wants me as a footballer, not for marketing purposes.'

Vozinha is now expected to complete a move to Chile's most successful club Colo Colo, who have won a record 34 league titles.

Anibal Mosa, president of Blanco y Negro, the company that manages the Chilean club revealed Vozinha is due to fly to Santiago in the coming days to complete the move.

'Vozinha is going to be a Colo Colo player,' Mosa said.

'In the next few days, he will travel to Chile, undergo the necessary medical examinations, and then be presented here at the Estadio Monumental.'

Colo Colo are currently 12 points clear at the top of Chile's Liga de Primera.

Vozinha has had a nomadic career, playing for clubs in his homeland, Moldova, Slovakia, Cyprus and Portugal's second tier and he has won 94 caps for Cape Verde.

Sports.title: 'Hurt' Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after surprise Commonwealth Games bronze: Star reveals family feud has taken its toll and admits he 'doesn't know what went wrong'
Sports.content:
'Hurt' Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after surprise Commonwealth Games bronze: Star reveals family feud has taken its toll and admits he 'doesn't know what went wrong'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

First came an apology. 'Sorry guys,' said Adam Ramsay-Peaty, as his voice began to tremble. He wiped away a tear from his face and stared at the Tollcross floor to find his words.

The bronze medal around his neck felt like a heavy weight. 'It's hard because I know how hard I've worked. I know the s**t I've been through, which is no fault of my own. It does take a toll.'

After standing upon the podium, the 31-year-old walked around the pool and stopped for selfies with his adoring fans. An Englishman has not received a reception like this in Glasgow for a long time.

He stopped to hug his pregnant wife, Holly – the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay – before kissing her pregnant stomach. They are expecting a daughter in December and, as the swimmer confessed, family life has changed his priorities.

'She's always super proud of me,' he said. 'As a father, it doesn't matter if you come home with the gold, as long as you come home with the teddy, which I did. That's what matters.

'As you can tell, the emotion is always something that I'm going to carry. I'm never going to be afraid to show weakness because it's so important for making stronger people, making stronger men, stronger fathers, stronger husbands.

'I think 'S**t, how have I worked so hard at this age?' - then you get a result like that. I'm better than that. Maybe it's because I've had two years out, but it does hurt. There's a lot going on in my head right now.'

Adam Ramsay-Peaty was brought to tears as he reflected 'I'm never going to be afraid to show weakness' after securing bronze at the Commonwealth games

Adam Ramsay-Peaty stopped to hug his pregnant wife, Holly - the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay - before kissing her pregnant stomach

The pair wed on December 27 last year at Bath Abbey

Ramsay-Peaty was chasing from the start. He was not the leader of the pack. Perhaps he will fare better over 50 metres but here, over two lengths, he finished almost three seconds off his world record.

Australian Sam Williamson won gold and 18-year-old Filip Nowacki, of Jersey, claimed a brilliant silver that bodes well for the future of British swimming.

'I'm not crying because it's a bronze instead of a gold,' said Peaty, choking up throughout. 'I'm crying because I know that swim could have been better. I don't really know what went wrong in these last two weeks but something isn't hitting right, whether it's pace or focus.

'I feel like I couldn't have put more in, so you ask, 'What's the point of all the 5.30ams. What's the point of all the metres every day? What's the point of feeling exhausted all the time? What's the point of saying, 'No' to all the family events because of training?' It's because you want excellence and that isn't excellence for me.

'I enjoy a scrap but I lost that scrap in the last 25 metres. That's sport. Most of the time I've won the scrap. For some reason, the Commonwealths is that humble reminder.'

The wedding stories, the family feud and the social media abuse have taken their toll. The pool should be his place of escape but he swam with the world on his shoulders.

'People who comment and read headlines have got to look themselves in the mirror. Ignoring that comes at a cost. That hasn't played a part in that result here but it has to stop. Do better. I don't want young Filip to go through that.'

Join the discussion Has obsession with gold medals made us forget the human cost athletes pay for success?

Ramsay-Peaty was overcome with emotion in the mixed zone reflecting on his bronze medal

Throughout his decorated career, Ramsay-Peaty has been so far ahead of the field that he has had to look in the mirror to find competition. He has broken 14 world records, asserting a similar dominance to Sweden's serial pole vault champion Armand Duplantis. Untouchables. Now people will ask if time is finally catching up with Britain's greatest swimmer.

Nowacki is still waiting for his A Level results but the schoolboy from Millfield has already beaten his idol's teenage records. In 2012, Jason Kenny beat Chris Hoy to become the top dog of cycling. Lamine Yamal overcame Lionel Messi in last week's World Cup final. Swimming insiders believe it is a matter of time until Nowacki pulls a similar stunt.

'For me, he's got a very bright future ahead of him,' said Ramsay-Peaty, whose gold earrings caught the light of the cameras. 'He's my favourite for the 200m. He's definitely got the speed and he's about 25kgs less! He's got many many miles ahead of him, whereas my miles are probably coming to an end. I guess two years isn't that long to try and find that in me.'

Side by side, they look like David and Goliath. Nowacki is five inches shorter and does not have the same popping biceps. Ramsay-Peaty changed the game with his powerful upper body stroke but Nowacki's strength is in his kick. He keeps his hips high and moves more gracefully than his senior, who forces his way through the water.

Nowacki will discover his maths, economics and physics exam results during next month's European Championships. Then he plans to enrol at Loughborough University, where he can master his craft in time for the LA 2028 Olympics. Major medals are in his sights, although Ramsay-Peaty is not ready to stand aside just yet.

'To be racing one of the best in the world – arguably the greatest breaststroker of all time – is very special to me,' said Nowacki, who won the world junior championships last year in a time of 2:07.32, which would have medalled in every senior Olympics, bar one

Ramsay-Peaty knows a promising swimmer when he sees one. He has already signed up Nowacki to his own agency and will continue to mentor his prodigy.

'If I compare myself to 2014, 12 years ago, it's very exciting where Filip and his career can go,' he said. 'It's sport, it's beautiful, but f**k me, it can hurt.'

Sports.title: Chelsea ready to demand major fee for Pedro Neto amid Liverpool and Man City interest - as former boss Enzo Maresca eyes reunion
Sports.content:
Chelsea are not surprised by the reported interest in Pedro Neto, though would not allow their winger to leave on the cheap after noting the rising valuations of other wide men in this window.

The Premier League club are not actively touting their Portuguese 26-year-old for sale, but Blues insiders are aware of the asking prices being issued elsewhere in Europe, and specifically for RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande and Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola.

Diomande and Barcola are both considered £100million-plus players by their respective clubs, and while Neto would struggle to fetch such a large fee, it does give Chelsea an idea of their own wide man’s worth. The Blues have not quoted a valuation on Neto as of yet.

Manchester City and Liverpool, along with sides in Saudi Arabia, have been linked with Neto.

Chelsea sources believe it is only natural that Neto has attracted interest because of a lack of top wingers in the current market.

City are also now managed by Enzo Maresca, who favoured Neto as his right winger while in charge at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea are not surprised at interest in Pedro Neto but will not allow him to leave on the cheap

New Man City boss Enzo Maresca favoured Neto on the right wing while in charge of Chelsea

Join the discussion Should Chelsea cash in on Pedro Neto or hold out for a massive transfer fee amid rising winger prices?

Neto is not currently on Chelsea’s tour, which has started in Sydney, Australia, as he is still having downtime after representing Portugal at the World Cup.

Chelsea’s other Portuguese right winger, Geovany Quenda, is due to join up with his team-mates after the Australian leg of this tour as they move on to Asia.

Quenda, 19, picked up a ‘small injury’, per sources close to the player. Chelsea's new striker from Strasbourg, Emmanuel Emegha, will return to training at a later date after suffering a hamstring issue during their behind-closed-doors friendly win over Bromley.

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport, Chelsea beat Bromley 3-0 and also Crawley 3-1 in secret training matches at Cobham, with Emegha scoring in both games.

Sports.title: F1 news: Lewis Hamilton hit with new penalty as untelevised moment emerges
Sports.content:
F1 news: Lewis Hamilton hit with new penalty as untelevised moment emerges

F1 round-up ahead of the Hungarian Grand after Lewis Hamilton leaves one of his rivals furious

View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton will line up fifth for the Hungarian Grand Prix after receiving another penalty (Image: Formula 1 via Getty Images)

A thrilling Hungarian Grand Prix is on the cards after world champion Lando Norris took his first pole position of the season. With 2026 pace-setters Mercedes struggling at the tight and twisty Hungaroring track, Ferrari went into qualifying as the favourites for pole.

‌



However, Norris took advantage of an upgraded McLaren to set the fastest time. Joining him on the front row will be Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, with the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri third and Max Verstappen of Red Bull fourth despite a spin at the end of Q3.

‌



Hungaroring specialist Lewis Hamilton had to settle for fifth after being hit with a three-place grid penalty. Mercedes' George Russell, who desperately needs a good weekend after his no-score in Belgium last weekend, lines up sixth, a place ahead of team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who was also given a grid penalty.

‌



Here's a round-up of the latest F1 news ahead of the final race before the summer break…

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Fresh penalty for Hamilton

Having just missed out on pole, Hamilton suffered another blow when he was relegated three places. The seven-time world champion was deemed guilty of blocking Piastri at the first corner as the Australian started a quick lap.

‌



Ferrari failed to tell Hamilton about the oncoming McLaren and the mistake could be costly in the 41-year-old's title challenge. Hamilton has recently been no stranger to penalties. He was given a five-second penalty at the British Grand Prix for moving before the lights went out.

Lewis Hamilton one of two brutally punished as new Hungarian GP starting grid confirmed READ MORE :

In Belgium, he was controversially hit with the same sanction for his part in the first-lap clash that ended Russell's race, despite most observers viewing it as a racing incident.

Reacting to his Budapest penalty, he wrote on Instagram: "Sometimes you just can’t catch a break. Another weekend when I've been feeling great throughout all the sessions, but then it just falls apart.

‌



"To go from being so close to pole to then starting P5 is extremely frustrating. I always do my best to keep positive - sport is always about the highs and lows, but it’s also in the margins. Every point counts and you have to seize every opportunity.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"After 3 penalties in 3 weekends, it's becoming difficult to hang on to that positivity. Still, I won't let the setbacks take away from the progress we've been making as a team. With the pace we have, I'm hopeful we can get something out of the race."

‌



In a subsequent twist, Antonelli, who Hamilton trails by 45 points, was also served with a three-place grid penalty for failing to slow sufficiently under yellow flags following Verstappen's last-corner spin.

View 2 Images Oscar Piastri wasn't happy with Hamilton (Image: Getty Images)

Piastri's gesture

A previously unaired clip of Piastri's reaction to being blocked by Hamilton has emerged. The 25-year-old was impeded by the Ferrari at the start of Q3, with the Brit copping his aforementioned penalty.

Article continues below

The usually unflappable Piastri was left irate by the incident, calling it "pretty bad." In-car footage of the incident shows Piastri being clearly baulked by the Ferrari.

He then pulls up alongside Hamilton and gives him a sarcastic thumbs-up. Piastri said: "I saw him from the start line and kind of watched him, expecting him to get out of the way, and I've watched him basically all the way up until I nearly hit him."

Sports.title: Adam Peaty breaks down in tears and makes heartbreaking comment about family feud
Sports.content:
Adam Peaty breaks down in tears and makes heartbreaking comment about family feud

Adam Peaty was in reflective and emotional mood after his bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games

View 3 Images Adam Peaty had to settle for bronze in the 100m breaststroke (Image: Getty Images)

A tearful Adam Peaty appeared to bring up his family feud after being forced to settle for bronze in his premier event at the Commonwealth Games. The three-time Olympic champion's private life has been a source of intrigue since he got engaged to Holly Ramsay, the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon .

‌



The pair got married in December last year following a much-publicised rift with the majority of his family, which escalated after his mother, Caroline, was not invited to the bride's hen do. Peaty, who has taken on the Ramsay name, has not publicly spoken about the feud, a stance that has continued in the build-up to the Games in Glasgow.

‌



But after he surprisingly fell short in the 100m breaststroke final, he broke his silence, saying: "It's hard because I know how hard I work. I know the s**t I've been through, which is no fault of my own, but it does take its toll.

‌



"I'm not crying because it's bronze instead of gold. I'm crying because I know I am better than that. I feel like I couldn’t have put any more in and that's where it hurts, because I'm like, 'What’s the point of all the metres every day, what's the point of being exhausted all the time?'

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"What's the point of having to say no to family events so you can go to training? It has to mean something and for me, it has to be human excellence and that is not excellence for me. So that's the emotion that is unfortunately coming out."

‌



Heartbreak for Adam Peaty's mum as he competes in first race since fallout with new name READ MORE :

Adam Peaty issues defiant statement after wedding scuffle and family fallout READ MORE :

Peaty also took aim at his critics, declaring, "you can't hurt me" and telling them to "do better." He was cheered on by his wife, Holly, who is expecting the couple's first child in December. Peaty has another child from a previous relationship.

After collecting his medal, he kissed his new wife on the belly and said: "She's always going to be proud of me. And as a father, it doesn't matter if you come home with gold. As long as you come home with a teddy. That's really what matters.

View 3 Images Peaty couldn't hold back the tears (Image: TNT Sports)

‌



"But I'm never going to be afraid to show weakness, because it's so important for making stronger people, making stronger men, stronger fathers, husbands. And it's a realisation of how much I do work."

The 31-year-old was pipped by Australia's Sam Williamson and 18-year-old Filip Nowacki of Jersey in a race he had dominated for eight years before shockingly finishing out of the medals in Birmingham four years ago.

View 3 Images Peaty's wife Holly was proud of his efforts in Glasgow (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Meanwhile, England's William Ellard and Georgia Sheffield both set new Games records as they won the respective men's and women's S14 200m freestyle finals. Sheffield pipped team-mate Poppy Maskill, who took silver.

England's Ollie Morgan won a silver medal in the men's 50m backstroke final, finishing behind South Africa's Pieter Coetze. England's mixed 4x100m freestyle relay squad took silver behind Australia, with Wales in third.

Sports.title: Liverpool dealing with 'the worst news' as Andoni Iraola makes transfer demand
Sports.content:
Liverpool dealing with 'the worst news' as Andoni Iraola makes transfer demand

Liverpool saw Joe Gomez go down within 10 minutes of their pre-season outing on Saturday as Andoni Iraola bemoaned his fitness issues and talked up the need for new transfer arrivals

View 2 Images Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola is already dealing with squad issues

New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola admits Joe Gomez's pre-season injury was "the worst news" as the defender failed to play ten minutes.

‌



The Reds were playing in Nashville, seeing off fellow Premier League side Sunderland 4-2, but they've been dealt a major injury blow. Gomez has had his fair share of fitness issues and is again facing time on the sidelines, raising further issues about the team's backline options.

‌



Liverpool now face a nervous wait to discover the severity of Gomez's injury with the 29-year-old only starting seven times in the Premier League last season.

‌



Iraola has just taken over from Arne Slot and inherited a squad that has had Jeremy Jacquet added to it. The young defender was signed in January from Rennes but remained at the French club until the end of the summer, but their depth at the back is now being tested.

Iraola told LFCTV: "Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe. We were happy because we were going through training without losing any players and unluckily for us we've lost Joe straight away.

"With Jeremy we decided to take it easy with him, he's had a lot of months without playing, he's been training very well, but we're going to take it easy with him. He will play probably in the last game of this U.S. tour, he will have time to have minutes, but we were kind of happy, but we've lost one now."

‌



Jacquet, who set the Reds back £55 million, was ruled of Liverpool's win as a precaution having missed the second half of last season with a shoulder injury.

View 2 Images Joe Gomez didn't even last ten minutes on Saturday night

In light of Gomez's injury Iraola admitted after their win in the US that Liverpool's defence is "very thin" - which comes after Ibrahima Konate left for Real Madrid on a free. Giovanni Leoni is still working his way back to fitness after rupturing his ACL last September.

Article continues below

ESPN reports that Liverpool did not see the signing of a centre-half as a priority even if they did lose Konate, but their latest injury could force them into a change. Defensive leader Virgil Van Dijk has just turned 35 but only has one year left on his contract.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold's pick for England manager has just taken different job
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold's pick for England manager has just taken different job

Trent Alexander-Arnold's England career has stalled under Thomas Tuchel

View 3 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold's England career under Thomas Tuchel has yet to take off (Image: PA)

Trent Alexander-Arnold's dream of reuniting with Jurgen Klopp was shattered after the former Liverpool boss became the new Germany manager. Klopp, 59, has returned to management with the national team in his first coaching role since departing Anfield in the summer of 2024.

‌



The Real Madrid defender spent the entirety of his professional career at Liverpool under Klopp and previously admitted his desire to play under him again - but on the international stage.

‌



Speaking after Gareth Southgate stepped down as Three Lions boss following their Euro 2024 final defeat, Alexander-Arnold was asked about his thoughts on Klopp replacing him as the England boss.

‌



The 27-year-old said: "I enjoyed every moment I worked with him, we shared amazing memories, forged an amazing relationship, an amazing bond. So of course if that were to happen, we would pick up where we left off."

Klopp made the shock decision to depart Liverpool due to a lack of energy. His former pupil admitted at the time that he would have been surprised if he took the role just two months after leaving Merseyside.

Alexander-Arnold added: "I would be surprised if he did take it. It was clear when he announced when he was leaving, the conversations I have had with him, everything on social media, he seems to be enjoying his time off, so it would be a huge surprise."

‌



Klopp's first press conference as Germany boss on Friday started with a bang. He immediately handed an ultimatum to the German press by threatening to quit the job if they do not leave his family alone.

View 3 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold was managed by Jurgen Klopp for the entirety of his professional career at Liverpool (Image: Andrew Powell, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

"Now is the time where I'm really in the middle of the media focus," Klopp began. "I was surprised, not negatively or positively surprised, at how fast news spread. And it's sometimes hard for people to just think 'let's turn a blind eye to things' and not to divulge any information.

‌



"Sometimes that is the right thing to do, not to publish things that happened. I know full well this is job number one for me. It is my mission to make the national squad better and to hope the pool for me to choose from is bigger.

View 3 Images The Real Madrid defender missed out on England's World Cup squad this summer (Image: PA)

"But it is not something I will do against you, but I’m doing it for you. It is an honour. I will be remunerated very graciously and if tomorrow it's 'Jurgen Klopp is s***', then I will be gone. But if the DFB (German FA) says ‘Come on let us not continue the job’ then that’s it.

‌



"And if you (the media) behave badly and don’t let my family live in peace. I’ll be gone and I'll just turn away. I know there are other countries where the national team head coaches are treated even worse. But I love this job, but I’m always ready to call just call it quits if need be.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Jurgen Klopp is not going to have any ‘career’ after the national team, this is the absolute pinnacle of my footballing career as a coach. I will give everything I’ve got."

Article continues below

The ex-Liverpool star's international career has stalled under Thomas Tuchel, who stunningly left out the full-back from his World Cup squad this summer. Alexander-Arnold suffered an injury-hit debut campaign with Spain and made just 30 appearances across all competitions in what was a trophy-less season for Madrid.
