Sports.title: Malaysia will officially host F1's 2026 Bahrain GP
Sports.content:
Sepang will host the Bahrain Grand Prix from 2-4 October, as Formula 1 returns to Malaysia for the first time since 2017.

Initially featuring four rounds in the Middle East, the 2026 F1 calendar was compromised by the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has destabilised the whole region. The Bahrain and Saudi Arabian grands prix were initially cancelled, creating a five-week break in April.

F1 has therefore been seeking alternatives, and the Singapore round provided a perfect opportunity to run a race in Malaysia, with Sepang just 300km away.

Bahrain was still keen to have its own race on the calendar and has found an agreement with the FIA, F1 and Malaysia for Sepang to host it.

There will therefore be a triple-header from Baku to Singapore from late September to mid-October. The Azerbaijan Grand Prix is taking place on a Saturday, which makes the logistics much easier.

“We are delighted to confirm that Malaysia will host the Bahrain Grand Prix in 2026,” F1 president and CEO Stefano Domenicali said. “Once again, the sport has demonstrated its ability to adapt, find solutions, and deliver, creating an exciting moment for everyone who follows Formula 1.

F1 at Sepang in 1999 Photo by: LAT Images via Getty Images

“This is fantastic news for our fans. They will continue to enjoy a full and exciting Formula 1 calendar, while also seeing the sport return to a great venue. Malaysia is an incredible country, and Sepang holds a special place in Formula 1 history. It will provide a spectacular setting for racing and an unforgettable experience for fans at the circuit and watching around the world.”

Malaysia previously hosted F1 every year from 1999 to 2017. Declining ticket sales and TV ratings, allied to feeling “ripped off” by its deal with Bernie Ecclestone’s Formula One Management, led Sepang to terminate its contract early, giving up on its 2018 race.

No fewer than 10 current F1 drivers have raced at Sepang in the past. The final Malaysian Grand Prix coincidentally was Pierre Gasly’s F1 debut.

Sebastian Vettel is the most successful driver at the track near Kuala Lumpur with four wins to his name, while Fernando Alonso has the most of the current crop – three. Lewis Hamilton took a record five pole positions there but converted just one into victory, with his 2016 engine failure famously contributing to his world title defeat to team-mate Nico Rosberg.

It is worth noting that F1 is sticking to a theoretical 23-race calendar with the Qatar and Abu Dhabi season-ending rounds unchanged, though their fate obviously depends on the Iran war and alternative options are known to be considered.

Sports.title: Antonelli hit with grid drop for yellow flag infringement in F1 Hungarian GP qualifying
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has been given a three-place grid drop for Formula 1's Hungarian Grand Prix after being penalised for not heeding yellow flags.

Antonelli took fourth on the grid at the Hungaroring as Mercedes was beaten by both McLaren's polesitter Lando Norris and the two Ferraris. On his final qualifying run, however, Antonelli caught yellow flags in the final corner - where Red Bull's Max Verstappen was stationary in the runoff area after a spin.

Antonelli still improved his final sector time to take fourth, with the stewards investigating if the Italian had lifted enough to respect the local yellows.

The championship leader has been handed a three-place grid drop, which will demote him to seventh on the grid, because the stewards felt he had only lifted by the tiniest amount and was still faster through the corner than on his previous push lap.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton also received a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in Turn 1, with Piastri now moving up to third and Verstappen joining him on the second row.

Read Also: Formula 1 Hamilton slapped with grid drop for impeding Piastri in F1 Hungarian GP qualifying

"The driver of Car 12 stated that on seeing the yellow flag and light panel, he lifted off the throttle earlier than his previous push lap," the stewards wrote in their verdict. "This was verified by the telemetry. However the reduction in speed occurred for a very short period, and in fact the car’s speed when passing the scene of the incident involving Car 3, was slightly higher than that on the previous push lap.





Watch: Lando Norris Takes a Shock Pole | F1 Hungarian GP Qualifying

"The mini sector time was only 0.03 second slower than his best time for that mini sector, and whilst, because he had lifted 16 metres earlier, he was 14 km/h slower entering the yellow flag sector, but was 3 km/h faster when passing the incident site due to less application of the brakes entering the corner. The FIA representatives noted that the speed reduction in the mini sector was less than 1%.

"The Stewards considered this incident to be different to other incidents that have resulted in no further action, because unlike those cases, there was no significant speed delta through the mini sector compared to the driver’s previous fastest time under similar circumstances."

Antonelli could have faced a five-placed grid drop for the offence, but the stewards felt that the Italian at least scrubbing off some speed warranted a more lenient penalty. The 19-year-old also gets a penalty point on his licence.

"The recommended penalty according to the penalty guidelines, for this offence, is a drop of 5 grid positions," the FIA stewards added. "However in mitigation of penalty, we considered that the driver did make a reduction in speed, albeit, in our determination, an insufficient and unsustained one. Further, the driver had limited time and distance to react. Hence a lower penalty is applied."

Antonelli also received a warning for driving too slowly and exceeding the minimum delta times on his in-lap following his final qualifying attempt.

Sports.title: Hamilton slapped with grid drop for impeding Piastri in F1 Hungarian GP qualifying
Sports.content:
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton has been handed a three-place grid drop for impeding McLaren driver Oscar Piastri in Formula 1 Hungarian Grand Prix qualifying.

Towards the end of the final Q3 shootout, Hamilton was driving slowly on the main straight while Piastri was approaching behind him on a flying lap.

Unaware the Australian was approaching, Hamilton stuck to the racing line, forcing Piastri to take avoiding action and abort his final flying lap. Piastri sarcastically gave Hamilton a thumbs-up from the cockpit, while a confused Hamilton asked his race engineer why he hadn't been told the McLaren was approaching.

The FIA stewards handed the seven-time world champion a standard three-place grid drop, meaning Hamilton will drop from second to fifth on Sunday's starting grid. As a result, Charles Leclerc, Kimi Antonelli and Piastri will all move up a position on the grid.

"At the approach to Turn 1, Car 44 was travelling at a significantly reduced speed on the racing line while Car 81 was approaching on a push lap," the stewards wrote in their verdict.

"The driver of Car 44 explained that he had just completed a fast lap and did not receive the team's radio message regarding the approaching Car 81 until the latter was already in close proximity. He further stated that, due to the positioning of his car on the track, Car 81 was not visible in his mirrors.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

"Car 81, which was on a push lap, was forced to take avoiding action by running wide and being obliged to abort the lap.

"Having examined the available evidence, the Stewards determined that Car 44 unnecessarily impeded Car 81 during qualifying."

Antonelli is still awaiting his own verdict on allegedly infringing a yellow flag at the end of his final qualifying lap as he passed the stationary Red Bull of Max Verstappen.

"It was pretty bad," Piastri said. "I saw him from the start line, expecting him to get out of the way and I watched him basically all the way up until I nearly hit him. So, yeah, a shame."

Sports.title: Russell to undergo Mercedes engine change but avoids F1 Hungarian GP grid drop
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver George Russell will take a fresh V6 engine for the Hungarian GP following a water leak in qualifying, but will keep his seventh place on the grid.

Russell qualified a distant seventh at the Hungaroring after both he and team-mate Kimi Antonelli looked adrift in qualifying, with Mercedes struggling to keep its tyre temperatures under control.

Russell's second lap was ruined after he crossed the kerbs at the exit of Turn 4, with the impact from the vibrations causing a water leak inside the Mercedes power unit.

Team principal Toto Wolff says Russell's engine was "done", with Mercedes having to replace his power unit for Sunday's grand prix.

Mercedes provided further details in a subsequent statement. "During George’s final lap in Q3, we detected a loss of water pressure on his car and instructed him to stop as a precaution once he had completed the lap.

"Following further inspection, we have elected to change his power unit ahead of tomorrow’s race, moving to his fourth unit of the season and thus within his season allocation."

Russell's fourth internal combustion engine is the final one allowed before incurring grid penalties, moving onto the same number of engines as team-mate Antonelli. Both drivers will therefore likely face a grid drop sometime after the summer break.





Watch: Lando Norris Takes a Shock Pole | F1 Hungarian GP Qualifying

But as Mercedes is replacing a damaged component with one of the same specification, Russell avoids a pitlane start and gets to keep his seventh place on the starting grid. "We had a water leak, hit a bump in Turn 4," Russell explained. "The lap was feeling good until then and then suddenly the lap wasn't. I didn't think much of it, and the team told me the water was spraying over my tyres.

"As soon as we saw it in the data, the water leak, suddenly my tyre temperatures got really cold on the rear. So, I don't think much more, top three definitely not possible, but maybe a few positions higher would have been there."

Meanwhile team-mate Antonelli, who qualified fourth, is facing a trip to the stewards over alleged speeding under yellows as he passed Max Verstappen's stationary Red Bull during his final qualifying lap.

Reigning world champion Lando Norris handed Mercedes its first grand prix qualifying defeat of the season, taking pole ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.

However, Hamilton received a three-place grid drop for impeding Norris' McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri in Q3, meaning Antonelli would move up to third if he escapes a punishment of his own.

Sports.title: Verstappen on latest Red Bull woes: "Desperate? I'm already past that stage"
Sports.content:
Qualifying at the Hungaroring turned out to be a disappointing affair for Red Bull. Ahead of the weekend, team principal Laurent Mekies hoped that the energy-rich circuit near Budapest would suit the RB22 slightly better, but reality proved far more difficult than expected.

Verstappen will start Sunday's race from fourth on the grid - up two spots from where he qualified due to grid penalties for Lewis Hamilton and Kimi Antonelli - while team-mate Isack Hadjar will line up one row further back in eighth. To make matters worse, Verstappen also spun at the final corner, something he believes summed up the entire session.

"The weekend has been difficult in general, but when instead of the tyres degrading, your car is degrading, then you have a big problem. So that's what's happening," Verstappen said.

Verstappen made that clear over the team radio immediately afterwards. Following his spin, he told the team: "The car is just completely broken aerodynamically, it's just getting worse and worse. What a joke. What a joke honestly, what a shit weekend."

"The car became impossible to drive"

Speaking to Dutch media in the paddock, Verstappen explained that the team could see those aerodynamic issues in the data – though he could not yet specify what they were – to the point where the car became "undriveable".

"The car just kept developing more oversteer and all the problems only got worse. I arrived at the final corner and the car just spun again. At one point, the car simply became impossible to drive," he said.

After two crashes caused by the rotating rear wing, things went wrong in Hungary due to an aerodynamic problem

Where Verstappen's previous two crashes were caused by the rotating rear wing, he says the most frustrating aspect is that the issue is different every time: "There's always something different happening. It's difficult for me to make sense of it, because I don't know exactly what the problem was myself.

"But it's clear that something was wrong again, because they already told me during qualifying that something wasn't right in the data and that they could see the aerodynamics deteriorating.

"That's obviously not what you want during qualifying, and by that point you can't even adjust the front wing anymore. Then the whole car is no longer in the right balance."

For Verstappen, that made it particularly difficult to get the car into a good operating window over the course of the race weekend in Budapest.

"Well, that's basically impossible," the four-time world champion replied when asked by Autosport.

"This weekend has been very difficult and qualifying was just completely hopeless. There was absolutely nothing you could do with it."

Verstappen says Red Bull is hit by a different problem every weekend – problems that even the team itself does not always understand

Asked whether it leaves him feeling desperate that Red Bull seems to be facing a different problem every weekend, the Dutchman gave perhaps his most telling answer of the day and, by his own admission, he has already moved beyond desperation.

"No, no, desperate? That word doesn't even exist for me anymore," he said. "I'm already past that stage. We just let it go and try again tomorrow."

Earlier this year, after the Japanese Grand Prix, Verstappen said he had already moved beyond "all disappointment". Now, "desperate" can be added to that list as well.

Sports.title: Alonso explains how the impact of Aston Martin’s upgrades go further than Hungarian GP qualifying breakthrough
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso reckons qualifying at the Hungarian Grand Prix was an “important” boost for the Aston Martin Formula 1 team after his first Q2 appearance in grand prix qualifying in the 2026 campaign.

The two-time F1 world champion took 16th at the Hungaroring to end Aston Martin’s run of five consecutive qualifying sessions occupying the back row, with a deficit of around two seconds.

But round 11 in Budapest marked the Silverstone squad’s first major upgrade of the year, radically changing its AMR26’s chassis with an engine update coming next in Zandvoort.

“It was important,” said Alonso. “Definitely, it was important for everyone in the team as it has been a tough period in both factories.

“Having the deficit that we had in terms of performance in the first half of the year, and this package obviously didn't change many positions, but it changed a lot the momentum of everyone in the factory.

“It's not anymore that we are chasing something that we don't know. We know exactly what we are looking for and we know exactly the targets for the next package or the targets for next year.

“So that's, I think for me, the biggest change of this weekend.”

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

The biggest positive for the Spaniard is that he’s managed to complete a clean weekend up to now, while qualifying ahead of Haas, Williams and Cadillac by at least one tenth.

“When you bring a new car, you always believe that it is important to have the correlation right and you deliver what you expect to deliver,” the 44-year-old added.

“Even if it's what we expected, I think it was important to have it and not have a nasty surprise.

“The way the car drives, we just gain load and overall grip on the corners. Maybe a little bit more consistent to drive, so corner by corner, an entry meets an exit of the corner, the car is a little bit more forgiving, so it's a little bit easier to drive.

“The previous car we had, it was trickier to drive.”

But the weekend has not gone as well for Alonso’s team-mate Lance Stroll, who on Friday spun off at Turn 2 during first practice with a rear suspension failure, causing him to miss FP2.

Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

On Saturday, he eventually qualified 20th, ahead of both Cadillacs, and although he acknowledged Aston’s progress, Stroll was still left frustrated by the current weaknesses.

“Better, for sure,” said the Canadian. ”I think we're missing a lot on engine. So, yeah, we have to find more power. We're definitely much better on grip level, so we just need to find more power.

“The car didn't turn in Turn 12. I checked. I think we had a 10km/h tailwind and it just went straight into the gravel. So, annoying, because I think we could have got into Q2 today.”

Sports.title: Antonelli risks grid drop as stewards launch Hungarian GP qualifying investigation
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli is set to be investigated by the FIA stewards for a suspected yellow flag rule infringement in qualifying for the Formula 1 Hungarian Grand Prix.

Antonelli took fourth on the grid at the Hungaroring as Mercedes was beaten by both McLaren's polesitter Lando Norris and the two Ferraris.

But the championship leader is at risk of starting further down after being summoned to the stewards' office for allegedly infringing F1's yellow flag rules.

On his final qualifying run, Antonelli caught yellow flags in the final corner - where Red Bull's Max Verstappen was stationary in the runoff area after a spin.

Antonelli did improve his final sector time to take fourth, though, with the stewards now investigating if the Italian had lifted enough to respect the yellow flags.

Antonelli had complained over a lack of grip as both he and team-mate George Russell were unable to keep Mercedes' 2026 pole streak intact, the Silver Arrows suffering their first grand prix qualifying defeat of the year.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Russell could only manage seventh on the grid and then ground to a halt on the in-lap with a water leak.

Elsewhere, Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton faces a likely grip drop for impeding McLaren's Oscar Piastri in Turn 1. Hamilton had qualified second, just 0.012s behind polesitter Norris, and ahead of team-mate Charles Leclerc.

Sports.title: Hamilton under investigation by stewards over impeding Piastri in Hungarian GP qualifying
Sports.content:
The FIA stewards have summoned Lewis Hamilton regarding an incident involving the Ferrari driver and McLaren’s Oscar Piastri in Q3 at Formula 1’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Piastri lay fifth following his first run in Q3 and failed to improve on his last attempt after finding a slow Hamilton on the racing line in Turn 1, now known as Piquet Corner.

“Fuck me, man,” the Australian grumbled on the radio, showing his fist to the Ferrari driver on the approach to Turn 2 – coincidentally now named Hamilton Corner.

As it happens, the Briton was told “Piastri pushing” by race engineer Carlo Santi as soon as he crossed the finish line to conclude his flying lap, but this was followed by “yellow flag, yellow flag”, due to Max Verstappen’s spin in Turn 14 – Szisz Corner – taking centre stage in their conversation.

Then the McLaren racer was baulked by a confused Hamilton, who inquired: “Was Piastri on a lap, or…?”

Santi eventually admitted to being “caught by the yellow flag”.

“It was pretty bad,” commented Piastri, who did qualify fifth after all.

“I saw him from the start line and kind of watched him, expecting him to get out of the way, and I watched him basically all the way up until I nearly hit him. So, yeah, a shame.

Oscar Piastri, McLaren Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

“Even without that, it's not been easy for sure this weekend for me. I think missing FP1 definitely had a bit more of an impact than I thought it would because the track conditions have been pretty different to what we've been used to.

“In saying that, you know, today the conditions have been quite a lot different to yesterday, but it's just been difficult to catch up. And I felt like with every lap through qualifying I was slowly getting there and, you know, I felt like I needed that second lap in Q3 more than most weekends, and to not be able to do it was quite frustrating.”

Hamilton was surprised to be in a position to be impeding anyone as he didn’t expect any of his rivals to start their final attempt after he had finished his.

“I was told literally when he was at the apex behind me, so I had no idea he was coming,” he said. “I thought everyone came out behind me, I was the first out, so I thought everyone had finished their lap, and I think Charles was the car that was behind me when I left the pitlane, so as far as I was aware. So yeah, crazy, because it had been clean and obviously it wasn't intentional.”

Pole position eluded Hamilton by 0.012s as Lando Norris edged ahead, so a potential three-place penalty would drop him down to fifth – although that would be a switch from the notoriously dirty side of the grid to the cleaner one.

“Congratulations to Lando, he did a great lap,” the seven-time world champion said. “I felt solid throughout qualifying, but for some reason we went out first, which I don't think was the right call. And the grip wasn't there for either Charles or I. We were quickest throughout, so it's definitely one that got away.”

Sports.title: Formula 1 confirms it will hold ‘Bahrain Grand Prix’ in Malaysia in October | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 will replace its cancelled Bahrain Grand Prix with an extra round of the world championship which will take place in October.

But although the race will keep the same title, the race will not take place in Bahrain. The race instead take place 6,000 kilometres away at the Sepang International Circuit in Malaysia.

Bahrain’s round of the world championship was cancelled in April after the USA and Israel began bombing Iran, prompting the country to launch its own strikes against other countries in the region, including Bahrain. F1 was also forced to cancel the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix.

After the USA and Iran reached a Memorandum of Understanding over the conflict, leading to a cessation of strikes, the Bahrain race promoters expressed hope of reinstating their race to the calendar. However the resumption of bombing in recent weeks has renewed concerns over the viability of racing in the Middle East.

The final two rounds of the season are also due to take place in the Middle East at two other countries which Iran has attacked: Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Other series, including the World Endurance Championship, have already abandoned attempts to race in the region this year.

Malaysia’s race will slot in between Azerbaijan and Singapore’s rounds, forming a run of three consecutive events. The final 11 weeks of the season will now feature a total of nine events, providing the Qatar and Abu Dhabi rounds can go ahead.

Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali said the decision to reinstate one of the two cancelled races was “fantastic news for our fans.”

“They will continue to enjoy a full and exciting Formula 1 calendar, while also seeing the sport return to a great venue. Malaysia is an incredible country, and Sepang holds a special place in Formula 1 history.”

Sepang will return to the F1 calendar having previously hosted the championship between 1999 and 2017. Max Verstappen won the last race at the venue nine years ago.

Grands prix have been held outside their designated countries in the past, most notably when Italy’s second round of the world championship was dubbed the ‘San Marino’ Grand Prix between 1981 and 2006. The Luxembourg Grand Prix was twice held in Germany and Dijon in France held the 1982 Swiss Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Antonelli handed three-place grid drop and penalty point for yellow flag infringement | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli has been given a three-place grid drop for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags in qualifying.

The penalty means the world championship leader will start Sunday’s race from seventh on the grid instead of fourth.

Antonelli was also warned for failing to obey the race director’s instructions regarding the maximum time between the two Safety Car lines in qualifying.

The Mercedes driver committed the yellow flag breach when he passed yellow flags at the end of Q3, which were shown due to Max Verstappen’s spin. The stewards also gave him a single penalty point on his licence, putting him on a total of four.

At the Austrian Grand Prix last month, Antonelli backed off more than he needed to for yellow flags. Team mate George Russell, who did not slow down as much for the same incident, took pole position for that race.

Afterwards Antonelli admitted he had made a “mistake” by slowing down too much for the yellow flags, having thought he saw a double flag warning rather than a single.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The stewards heard from the driver of car 12 (Kimi Antonelli), team representative, the FIA F1 Race Director and the Sporting Director of the FIA Single Seater Department, and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry and in-car video evidence. The driver of car 12 stated that on seeing the yellow flag and light panel, he lifted off the throttle earlier than his previous push lap. This was verified by the telemetry. However the reduction in speed occurred for a very short period, and in fact the car’s speed when passing the scene of the incident involving car three [Verstappen], was slightly higher than that on the previous push lap. The mini sector time was only 0.03 second slower than his best time for that mini sector, and whilst, because he had lifted 16 metres earlier, he was 14 km/h slower entering the yellow flag sector, but was 3 km/h faster when passing the incident site due to less application of the brakes entering the corner. The FIA representatives noted that the speed reduction in the mini sector was less than 1%. The stewards considered this incident to be different to other incidents that have resulted in no further action, because unlike those cases, there was no significant speed delta through the mini sector compared to the driver’s previous fastest time under similar circumstances. The recommended penalty according to the penalty guidelines, for this offence, is a drop of five grid positions, however in mitigation of penalty, we considered that the driver did make a reduction in speed, albeit, in our determination, an insufficient and unsustained one. Further, the driver had limited time and distance to react. Hence a lower penalty is applied.

Stewards’ verdict on Antonelli – driving unnecessarily slowly

The stewards heard from the driver of car 12 (Kimi Antonelli), team representative and timing and in-car video evidence. The driver was on an in-lap and his time between SC2 and SC1 exceeded the prescribed maximum for this event. Car 12 was not overtaken by any other car. The driver acknowledged that he had exceeded the delta. He said he was pre-occupied by his push lap having being affected by a yellow flag and wasn’t focusing sufficiently on adhering to the delta. The team explained that they were dealing with an issue with car 63 [George Russell] and ought to have reminded the driver to speed up. The stewards determined that the driver drove unnecessarily slowly by not adhering to the delta but noted that no other car was affected. Consistent with previous infringements of this type where no other car is affected, the stewards imposed a warning.

Sports.title: Verstappen blames ‘car degradation’ after latest spin in qualifying | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen says he feels Red Bull are suffering from “car degradation” after spinning out at the end of qualifying.

The four-times world champion lost control of his car in the last corner on his final lap in qualifying, leaving him sixth on the grid.

“The whole weekend has been tough but in qualifying especially the car is just degrading,” said Verstappen after qualifying. “We don’t have tyre deg, we have car degradation.

“I really can’t make anything out of it, it’s just really, really tough. The car suddenly just started oversteering a lot and honestly every lap that I did in qualifying just was worse and worse.”

Verstappen said the lack of consistency in the problems the team are facing makes them difficult to solve.

“We keep having different problems all the time and that’s probably the biggest issue at the moment,” he said. “There’s always something else that arises and that’s not good.”

Today’s qualifying session is the third time in the last four rounds Verstappen has spun in a competitive sessions. He crashed in Q3 at the Red Bull Ring and spun out in the final laps of the British Grand Prix.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

After qualifying Verstappen told his team: “The car is just completely broken aerodynamically.”

“It’s just getting worse and worse, what a joke. What a joke. What a shit weekend.”

Team principal Laurent Mekies consoled Verstappen, telling him it was “Super difficult out there Max” and “we know what you feel, we’ll try and fix what we can fix for tomorrow.”

“I’m sorry, it’s just for me it’s just completely undriveable, really,” Verstappen replied. “It’s really, really bad. The degradation in qualifying is massive. There’s already a problem and then it’s really undriveable.”

Red Bull technical director Pierre Wache admitted “the drivers were not happy with the balance” after qualifying.

“The grip is very low, it’s dusty and very bumpy,” he explained. “The massive change in the wind in the afternoon made it even more complicated and it was a tough session for the drivers. We have to run the car quite stiff here and that leads to a similar feeling to the ground effect cars of the last generation.”

“When the cars are on the edge, like they are for everyone, then the smallest perturbation can upset things,” he added. “On a more positive note, we ran the new iteration of the rear wing here all day without any issue.”

Sports.title: Hamilton demoted to fifth on grid for impeding Piastri | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has been given a three-place grid drop for impeding Oscar Piastri at the end of qualifying.

Piastri caught Hamilton at turn one as the McLaren driver began his final flying run. After being held up by the Ferrari, Piastri backed off and gestured at his rival – Hamilton gave an apologetic wave in reaction.

Hamilton had the quickest time in the session and was preparing to begin his final run when he had his encounter with Piastri. He admitted afterwards his concern over the incident affected his final lap.

The stewards subsequently summoned both drivers over the incident. They ruled Hamilton received a late warning about Piastri from his team and should have left him space.

Hamilton said he did not have enough time to react to the warning Piastri was behind him. “I was told literally when he was at the apex behind me, so I had no idea he was coming,” he said.

“I thought everyone was on an out-lap. Everyone came out behind me. I was the first out, so I thought everyone had finished their lap.

“Charles, I think, was the car that was behind me when I left the pit lane, as far as I was aware. So it’s crazy, because it had been clean, and obviously it wasn’t intentional.”

Hamilton’s three-place grid drop moves him from second on the grid to fifth. His team mate Charles Leclerc takes his place on the front row.

The stewards’ verdict on Hamilton

The stewards heard from the driver of car 44 (Lewis Hamilton), the driver of car 81 (Oscar Piastri), team representatives and reviewed video, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. At the approach to turn one, car 44 was travelling at a significantly reduced speed on the racing line while car 81 was approaching on a push lap. The driver of car 44 explained that he had just completed a fast lap and did not receive the team’s radio message regarding the approaching car 81 until the latter was already in close proximity. He further stated that, due to the positioning of his car on the track, car 81 was not visible in his mirrors. Car 81, which was on a push lap, was forced to take avoiding action by running wide and being obliged to abort the lap. Having examined the available evidence, the stewards determined that car 44 unnecessarily impeded car 81 during qualifying. In accordance with the FIA F1 Regulations and the established penalty guidelines for this type of infringement in qualifying, the stewards impose a three-place grid penalty on the driver of car 44.

Sports.title: Norris snatches pole position off Hamilton, Antonelli under investigation | 2026 Hungarian GP qualifying report
Sports.content:
Lando Norris claimed his first pole position as reigning world champion with a superb final lap in qualifying at the Hungaroring.

The McLaren driver was one of few people to improve on their final runs in Q3. Lewis Hamilton held provisional pole position after the first runs but failed to find any further time, allowing Norris to pip him by just 0.012 seconds.

Hamilton therefore fell to second on the grid ahead of Charles Leclerc. Andrea Kimi Antonelli had to settle for fourth place despite beginning his final lap well – he encountered yellow flags at the final corner.

The yellow flags were caused by Max Verstappen, who had his third significant spin in the last four weekends. As in Austria, it occured late in qualifying, the Red Bull driver spinning at the final corner.

Verstappen’s spin also obliged George Russell to slow down. The Mercedes driver then came to a stop at turn one immediately after finishing his final lap. Verstappen and Russell will line up immediately behind Oscar Piastri. The McLaren driver and Hamilton are under investigation for a potential impeding incident.

Isack Hadjar rebounded from a spin in Q2 to claim eighth on the grid ahead of Arvid Lindblad and Nico Hulkenberg. Antonelli also had a drama in Q2 as his first flying lap was deleted as he cut the inside of turn seven, and the decision came so late he had already committed to starting his final run on a used set of tyres. Nonetheless, he pulled out a quick enough time on old rubber to reach the top 10.

However as the session came to an end race control announced Antonelli was under investigation for a potential yellow flag infringement.

Aston Martin’s upgraded car proved quick enough for the team to earn their first fully-merited participation in the second round of qualifying this year (Fernando Alonso have reached SQ2 in Montreal, but not participated in it, after crashing). He did his final run in Q2 early, however, and ended up 16th.

Liam Lawson failed to join his team mate in the final 10, saying the Racing Bulls was difficulty to drive. He took 11th ahead of the Alpines. Gabriel Bortoleto, 14th, lost his first attempt to a track limits infringement like Antonelli.

Alonso reached Q2 at the expense of Oliver Bearman, who had been less happy with the balance of the Haas than his team mate after sitting out first practice. The dejected Williams pair also fell at the first hurdle.

Lance Stroll, whose Friday was badly disrupted by a suspension failure, ended up half a second behind Alonso in 20th place. The Cadillac drivers occupied the back row.

Sports.title: Norris heads Hamilton in final practice at the Hungaring | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris denied Ferrari a sweep of all three practice sessions for the Hungarian Grand Prix, setting the fastest time of the weekend so far in his McLaren.

With the soft tyres surprisingly proving resilient enough to yield two competitive times, Norris lowered the benchmark to a 1’17.939. That ensured he came out on top after a spate of runs by the drivers from the leading teams.

Norris displaced Lewis Hamilton from the top of the times by a tenth of a second, the Ferrari driver enjoying a strong run through the final sector. There was almost nothing to choose between him and Andrea Kimi Antonelli in third.

Charles Leclerc put his Ferrari fourth while Oscar Piastri and George Russell were each almost half a second slower than their respective team mates.

The Red Bull drivers did not look especially happy with their cars, Isack Hadjar branding his “undriveable” after a mistake at turn 12. Max Verstappen was the quickest of the pair, albeit seven-tenths of a second off Norris.

Liam Lawson took ninth for Racing Bulls but his team mate Arvid Lindblad missed most of the session with a technical problem. He emerged from the pits just in time for a single flying run. The Audi drivers completed the top half of the field.

Sergio Perez failed to set a time as he came to a stop immediately after leaving the pits. The Cadillac driver’s rear brakes were smoking alarmingly, prompting race control to red-flag the session.

Without that, the Williams drivers might have ended the session slowest of all. Valtteri Bottas outpaced his former team’s drivers and the upgraded Aston Martins were ahead of all four.

Fernando Alonso ended practice just under two-and-a-half seconds off the pace, but set his time early in the session, indicating there could be more pace in the heavily revised AMR26. The team had a fright early in the session, however, when Alonso caught his team mate at turn 12, who did not seem to realise he was there, provoking a worrying near-miss.

Sports.title: Gene Tunney Halts Tom Heeney In Final Championship Defense
Sports.content:
A paid crowd of 43,191 attended, with thousands more admitted on complimentary tickets. The gate reached approximately $691,014.50, producing a net of about $521,422 after expenses. Tunney received a remarkable $525,000 purse, while Heeney earned $100,000. Motion picture rights generated another $20,000. Radio rights produced $15,000.

Referee Eddie Forbes officiated. Charles F. Mathison and Tom Flynn served as judges.

Heeney fought exactly as expected, charging forward in an effort to force exchanges at close range. Tunney relied on disciplined footwork. His steady left jab repeatedly disrupted the challenger before sharp counters landed cleanly. Much of the early action featured clinches as Heeney struggled to trap the champion along the ropes.

By the eighth round, Tunney had opened a damaging cut over Heeney’s left eye. The punishment increased in the 10th when a double jab followed by a chopping right hand dropped the challenger near the ropes. Heeney rose immediately. He kept pressing forward despite absorbing heavy punishment.

The finish came at 2:52 of the 11th round. Tunney unloaded another sustained attack, but Heeney refused to fall. Seeing the exhausted challenger taking unanswered punches, Forbes stepped between them and awarded Tunney a technical knockout victory.

The victory became the final chapter of one of boxing’s finest championship careers. Tunney retired as heavyweight champion. Later that year, The Ring magazine selected him as its inaugural Fighter of the Year for 1928. Heeney earned lasting respect for his determination, although the defeat effectively ended his pursuit of the world heavyweight title.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Outworks Errol Spence Jr. Over 12 Rounds
Sports.content:
The opening rounds were competitive. Tszyu stunned Spence with a right hand in the closing seconds of the first round, but Spence answered in the second with effective body work and a hard left that briefly shifted the momentum. The third round also favored Spence, although Tszyu finished strongly with another right hand.

Tszyu regained momentum in the fourth before another close fifth round. He began taking control in the sixth and seventh, landing the cleaner punches while increasing his work rate. Both fighters developed swelling under their left eyes.

Referee Will Soulos warned Spence several times for low blows in the eighth round as blood began flowing from Spence’s nose. Tszyu continued pressing the action over the final four rounds, repeatedly landing right hands while Spence’s output slowed.

Tszyu finished strongly in the twelfth, rocking Spence with another right hand during the closing minute to seal the victory.

Following the decision, Spence applauded Tszyu before announcing his retirement from boxing.

Reda Defeats Fleming

In the co-feature, Ahmad “Bloodshot” Reda earned a unanimous decision over former Olympian Paul “Showtime” Fleming after 10 entertaining rounds.

Reda controlled most of the early action with his speed and activity, although Fleming enjoyed his best success in the fifth after inviting Reda to exchange while standing against the ropes.

A clash of heads opened a cut over Fleming’s left eyebrow in the seventh. Reda continued to outwork the veteran over the closing rounds despite suffering a cut late in the fight.

The judges scored the bout 99-91, 97-93 and 96-94.

Peters Stops Actis

Australian Olympian Callum “50 Cal” Peters remained unbeaten by stopping Ivan “Gringo” Actis in the seventh round.

The opening rounds featured heavy exchanges before Peters gradually took control with sharper punching. A right hand opened a cut over Actis’ left eye in the fourth, and Peters continued to wear him down until referee Will Soulos halted the bout at 55 seconds of Round 7.

Aokuso Knocks Out Tejeda

Former Olympian Paulo “Sweet P” Aokuso captured the vacant IBF Intercontinental light heavyweight title with a dramatic 10th-round knockout of Luis Antonio Tejeda.

Aokuso rocked Tejeda early, but the Dominican battled back and had the Australian badly hurt against the ropes during the seventh round.

The fight ended suddenly in the final round when Aokuso landed a crushing counter left hand that flattened Tejeda for the count.

Rahimi Wins Pro Debut

Former Olympian Tina Rahimi opened her professional career with a unanimous decision over Sacha Ryan Dryden.

Rahimi boxed well throughout the four-round contest, using her speed and combinations to edge most of the rounds before finishing strongly.

The judges scored it 40-36, 40-36 and 39-37.

Grach Defeats Pluto

Heavyweight Brandon “The Bull” Grach earned a unanimous decision over Ike “From Pluto” Pluto in a five-round battle.

Grach hurt Pluto with a right hand in the third round and scored a knockdown in the fourth. Pluto rallied late and landed several solid punches in the fifth, but Grach had already done enough to secure the victory.

The judges scored the fight 49-45, 49-45 and 48-46.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer for the main event.

Sports.title: Errol Spence Jr. Retires After Tim Tszyu Loss
Sports.content:
Errol Spence Jr. brought his boxing career to an end Saturday night after losing a unanimous decision to Tim Tszyu, saying his health, family and financial security made retirement an easy choice. The former unified welterweight champion made the announcement moments after suffering a 12-round defeat at Afterpay Arena in Sydney, Australia.

“It was a great fight. Congratulations to Tim and Jeff Fenech. It was a good showing by Tim. I answered a lot of questions about myself, and now it’s time to go home with my family and start a new life,” Spence said before confirming his decision. “Yeah, for sure. I’ve got my faculties intact. My money is good and working for itself, so everything’s good, man. I’ve got a beautiful family and I thank God that I’m able to leave this sport with my faculties intact and my family by my side. Everything’s going to go well.”

The judges scored the fight 117-111, 117-111 and 118-110 for Tszyu, who gradually took control after a competitive opening. Spence was returning from a layoff of nearly three years and showed flashes of his former ability, but Tszyu’s pressure and higher punch output proved decisive over the second half of the contest.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Hands Errol Spence Jr. Tough Return Defeat
Sports.content:
“Middleweight is my new division and I feel strong,” said Tszyu. “This was one hell of a show. There were sleepless nights where I was thinking about facing a legend like Spence. I understand why he’s one of the greats.”

The opening rounds were competitive, with Spence finding success behind his jab and left hand while investing in body shots. Tszyu refused to give ground, walking the former unified welterweight champion down and landing hard right hands whenever Spence paused in front of him.

The fight changed as the rounds wore on.

Tszyu began timing Spence with increasing regularity, connecting with right hands to the head and body while forcing the Texan backward. Spence’s timing and punch output declined as the pace caught up with him, a predictable challenge after such a lengthy absence from the ring.

By the championship rounds, Tszyu had taken firm control. Spence continued fighting back and showed the toughness that defined much of his career, but he spent long stretches covering up, holding and trying to slow the Australian’s momentum. Tszyu never allowed him to regain control, continuing to press forward and outwork him until the final bell.

“The advice from corner was to get in there,” said Tszyu. “I’m trying to replicate Kostya Tszyu and my trainer Jeff Fenech. if I can be half as great as them, I’ll go down as a great man.”

The victory gives Tszyu one of the biggest wins of his career and strengthens his position among the leading names at 160 pounds. He entered the bout under pressure after a difficult run over the last two years, but responded with a disciplined performance against one of boxing’s most accomplished former champions.

“I’d love to fight for a world title. I want Erislandy Lara and all the champions,” said Tszyu. “That’s what I’m aiming for. But beating a great like Errol Spence tops any world title for me.”

After the fight, Spence addressed his future while giving Tszyu credit for his performance.

“It was a good fight and congratulation to Tim,” said Spence. “It’s been a great event and everyone has treated me well. It was a good showing by Tim.

For Spence, the defeat raises fresh questions about what comes next. His decision to return after nearly three years away was one of the sport’s biggest stories, yet the layoff appeared to take its toll as the fight progressed. Although he lasted the full 12 rounds, Tszyu’s steady pressure exposed the difficulty of returning against a proven contender without a tune-up first.

“I answered a lot of questions for myself and now it’s time to go home with my family and start a new life. I’ve got my faculties intact and my money is working for itself. I’m thankful to leave this sport with my family by my side.”

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Eyes Boots Ennis After Bloody Title Defense
Sports.content:
His ambition is understandable. Ennis owns the WBA and WBO titles at 154 pounds, making a unification bout one of the biggest opportunities in the division. Eddie Hearn also backed the idea after the fight, pointing toward a possible event in the United States later this year.

The bigger issue is recovery.

Kelly didn’t leave the ring looking like someone ready to begin another training camp. Agyarko landed plenty of hard punches throughout the contest, and Kelly’s injuries weren’t limited to accidental head clashes. He also complained afterward that the referee allowed too much roughhouse work, describing stretches of the contest as feeling like “an MMA fight.”

That criticism comes with some irony. Kelly repeatedly landed rabbit punches during the fight and eventually had a point deducted for hitting behind Agyarko’s head. Both fighters contributed to the physical nature of the contest.

Kelly has made it clear he wants Ennis next. The bigger question is how long it will take for the damage from the Agyarko fight to heal before he can begin preparing for a unification bout.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Claims Keyshawn Davis Has Gone Missing
Sports.content:
Under the WBO order, the winning bid would be split 75 percent to Haney as champion and 25 percent to Davis as the mandatory challenger. The organization has set a minimum bid of $200,000, although the sides remain free to reach their own agreement before the scheduled hearing.

Bill Haney’s latest post appears aimed at increasing the pressure with little time left on the negotiating clock. Rather than discussing specific terms, he questioned Keyshawn Davis’ willingness to complete a deal while portraying the challenger as absent during one of the biggest business opportunities of his career.

No agreement between the camps has been announced, leaving Monday’s purse bid on course unless a deal is reached beforehand, with time still remaining.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Thought Anthony Joshua’s Career Was Over
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua’s dramatic comeback knockout of Kristian Prenga left Eddie Hearn celebrating by the end of the night, but the Matchroom promoter admitted his thoughts were very different after the opening round.

Joshua climbed off the canvas twice before stopping Prenga in the second round at the Jeddah Superdome, surviving a scare that nearly derailed his comeback.



“When he got dropped, I was like, that’s career over,” Hearn said to Charlie Parsons at The Stomping Ground. “I’m kind of thinking to myself, ‘You know what? I’m proud of him for even getting back in the ring.’ If it ends like this, he should be really proud of the fact that he even returned to boxing. He had 24 breaks in his ribs or something. He couldn’t move, was in hospital for weeks and weeks. To even be in the ring was incredible.” Hearn said Joshua’s recovery changed everything. “He held on. He walked onto an uppercut and somehow found a way to recover,” Hearn said. “When he got back to the stool, I felt if he could just find his legs, this guy had thrown a lot of punches in the first round and was going to wear himself out. AJ has incredible knockout power. It doesn’t matter if he’s hurt. He has the ability to take you out with one punch.” Joshua answered those concerns by stopping Prenga in the second round, but Hearn did not ignore the warning signs. He believes the performance should not overshadow the determination Joshua displayed by overcoming the knockdowns and finishing the fight. Share via: Facebook

Ghana News.title: First-ever Wa Vendors Expo sparks economic boom and empowers female entrepreneurs
Ghana News.content:
The forecourt of the Upper West Regional Coordinating Council (Ministries) has been transformed into a bustling epicentre of commerce and networking as the Upper West Region hosts its maiden Wa Vendors Expo.

The unprecedented two-day trade fair has successfully drawn vendors from across the country to one central location, creating a vibrant marketplace designed to empower local startups, foster crucial wholesale connections, and champion women in business.

Organised by Mary Baalie, CEO of Masung Royal Stores, the event was borne out of a desire to elevate female entrepreneurs and streamline regional trade.

"It's a trade fair that brings businesses together. We are primarily focused on empowering women, especially those in business, and it also helps create valuable business connections," Baalie explained.

She noted that while many locals have the drive to do business, they often struggle to access wholesale suppliers directly. The expo bridges this gap by bringing diverse regional vendors directly to the people of Wa.

For the participating startups, the high foot traffic has been a game-changer. At Stand 2, a massive crowd flocked to Fari's Bag, where quality items such as cloth bags and towels were being sold for as little as GH₵10. The vendor, Kanton Farihana, was visibly overwhelmed by the huge patronage.

"Since morning when I arrived, I've not rested," she shared, adding that she underestimated the turnout and would need to bring extra help next time to manage the rush. "Because they are affordable and they are quality... I will always come, anytime."

The sheer variety of goods on display has kept attendees captivated and their wallets open. Taadu Amanda, representing Fragrance World by Ella, praised the initiative as an excellent platform to introduce the brand to a new audience, assuring buyers that their products can keep them smelling fresh for up to 48 hours.

Similarly, a representative of Naaj Collections, who travelled all the way from Tamale to participate, attracted curious buyers with a playful marketing pitch by advertising clothes for "only 1 Cedi" before revealing the actual, yet highly affordable, prices. Buoyed by the large crowd and the success of similar events previously held in Tamale, the vendor expressed immense optimism about their sales.

"Alhamdulillah, we are just starting, and you can see the crowd. So there's hope," the vendor said. "Insha'Allah, by tomorrow we'll be going home with 50k! We hope so."

As the first event of its kind in the region, the Wa Vendors Expo is already proving to be a resounding success. It has not only provided a vital financial boost for emerging enterprises but has also firmly demonstrated that the Upper West Region has a strong appetite for dynamic, large-scale commercial opportunities.

Ghana News.title: Joshua knocked down twice as dramatic win sets up Fury fight
Ghana News.content:
Anthony Joshua suffered two knockdowns - the first happening after just 20 seconds - before recovering to dramatically stop Kristian Prenga in the second round of his comeback fight in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The British heavyweight was fighting for the first time since surviving the December car crash in Nigeria that claimed the lives of his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele.

He was sensationally rocked by a huge uppercut from underdog Prenga in the opening round, and then hit the canvas again later in the round.

At that point he looked on the verge of one of the biggest shock defeats in heavyweight history, with the long-awaited Tyson Fury fight hanging by a thread.

But Joshua produced one of the greatest escapes of his career, and now that fight is on.

He unleashed his right hand in the second round, with the final shot sending Albanian Prenga crashing down and forcing the referee to halt the contest.

"It's more than punch power. That was spirit, that was Latz, that was Sina, that was the families. It hurts to even talk about it. It has been tough," Joshua, 36, said.

He choked up and stepped away from the microphone, before adding: "It's my brothers. I don't want to talk about it."

There had been speculation fellow Briton Fury might make an appearance despite insisting he would not attend.

But the master of mind games stayed true to his word, with Fury nowhere to be seen barely 24 hours on from his own warm-up win over Mariusz Wach in Thailand.

"I respect everything he has done and everything that he has achieved, but as a fighting person, we're here now. I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat," Joshua said about the prospect of fighting Fury.

Contracts have been signed, but the venue and date for a fight more than a decade in the making are still unknown.

This chaotic night, however, belonged to Joshua in a victory forged through adversity during the most difficult months of his life.

Joshua extended his record to 30 victories and four defeats in one of the most dramatic fights of his career.

Given the circumstances, this was never going to be a straightforward return for Joshua. Few, however, could have predicted the drama that unfolded inside six minutes.

Joshua carried the names of Ghami and Ayodele on his chest and walked to the ring alongside his entire team in a quiet show of unity. The canvas carried their names too, alongside the words 'My Brother's Keeper'.

His comeback could scarcely have begun in any worse fashion. Just 20 seconds in, a right uppercut from Prenga sent Joshua crashing to the canvas and stunned the arena.

Joshua smiled as he climbed to his feet. Prenga, who arrived with 20 knockouts from his 20 victories but little profile even with boxing's hardcore followers, sensed an opportunity.

Promoter Eddie Hearn barked instructions from ringside, while Joshua stablemate Oleksandr Usyk watched on with a look of concern.

A left uppercut later in the round dumped Joshua on the canvas again. He was still unsteady at the start of the second round and appeared to be there for the taking, but Prenga surprisingly began to box off the back foot and let the Watford fighter off the hook.

Joshua capitalised and, using his years of experience - and perhaps the emotion - he drew Prenga on to a jab before uncorking a crushing right hand. More rights followed as Prenga collapsed to the canvas and the referee had seen enough.

This was 35-year-old Prenga's second loss in his career.

It was Joshua's first test against a recognised professional opponent since Daniel Dubois stopped him in September 2024.

His only fight since had come against YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in December, 10 days before the fatal crash that left him injured.

Joshua passed the Prenga test, but not in the manner anyone expected. It was not the destructive, free-flowing champion who once swept opponents aside.

'Tonight wasn't about Tyson Fury'

Joshua made his pro debut in 2013 after winning gold at the London 2012 Olympics

After defeating 46-year-old Wach in Pattaya, the question of whether Fury would show up to watch Joshua became a subplot of fight night.

A Fury lookalike briefly fooled reporters when he stepped out of a taxi, while Fury's manager Spencer Brown insisted the 'Gypsy King' would be "there in spirit".

The fight between two of the most recognisable names in British boxing is understood to have been agreed for November.

Neither man is at the peak of his powers, but while the commercial appeal remains strong, Joshua's struggles are likely to leave Fury a clear favourite.

The bout is expected to stream on Netflix. British fans are hoping for a homecoming event, but it is understood Saudi organisers and broadcasters favour a venue in the United States to cater for American audiences.

"We've signed the contract. Everything is done," Hearn said.

"But tonight wasn't about Tyson Fury. It was about the strength Anthony Joshua has shown just to be here.

"No-one knows what he's been through over the last seven months. When he went down in the first round, I thought he'd come back too soon."

Ghana News.title: NSMQ 2026: Edinaman SHS storms to nationals with highest opening score in Central region qualifiers
Ghana News.content:
Edinaman Senior High School has qualified for the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) national championship after recording the highest score on the opening day of the Central Regional Qualifiers.

Edinaman SHS – 71 points

With more contests scheduled in the coming days, schools across the Central Region will continue battling for the remaining qualification places in Ghana's premier science and mathematics competition.

Ghana News.title: ‘It’s not just an inconvenience’: We’ve underestimated the health impacts of heavy periods
Ghana News.content:
Heavy menstrual bleeding is a serious health condition. Only now are we starting to understand what causes it – and how it can be treated.

From the age of 12-13 onwards, Michelle Alston slept off the worst days of her menstrual periods in the school nurse's office, battling severe pain as she bled through period products. "I was taught that this is just normal," she says. "This is just something that you have to learn to cope with."

She felt weak, failing to cope with her periods as well as her peers seemed to. It wasn't until she reached her early 40s that she learned weakness had little to do with it – her periods were unusually heavy. When bleeding during periods is so extensive that it interferes with quality of life, doctors call it heavy menstrual bleeding, and it's a serious medical problem.

Studies of populations from around the world estimate that between 10 and 30% of reproductive-aged women experience heavy menstrual bleeding like Alston's. And due to under-reporting and a general lack of understanding of how much bleeding is too much, studies suggest it may actually occur in half of all reproductive-aged women. Heavy menstrual bleeding can also signify other health problems and have serious consequences when unchecked, such as anaemia.

Yet, only recently have researchers began exploring the resulting harms from heavy menstrual bleeding in depth, pursuing better diagnostics and treatments. A search of PubMed (a database of biomedical research publications) for the term "menstrual blood" yielded just 400 publications in the last decade. Publications for "semen", for instance, number over 15,000.

"Women are probably owed years, if not decades, of research," says Jackie Maybin, a gynaecologist at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland and programme director of The Missed Vital Sign, a research initiative for heavy menstrual bleeding. "And I think the time is now."

How much blood is too much?

For researchers, heavy menstrual bleeding is blood loss of over 80ml per cycle, blood clots exceeding the size of a US quarter, or periods lasting beyond seven days. But for those of us who menstruate, there's no standardised or metric conversion for the practical ways of measuring bleeding: the number of bathroom visits, pads or tampons changed, or bloodstained pairs of underwear.

Some clinicians try to meet patients halfway, asking them to judge their blood loss using charts featuring progressively bloodier pads and tampons. But that too is imprecise, as all period products aren't created equal and often vary widely in absorption.

As a result, determining how much blood is too much during a period isn't straightforward, and often clinicians have to determine heavy menstrual bleeding by whether it interferes with quality of life.

"The patient sometimes doesn't realise that the amount of bleeding they're having is not normal, and that actually, something can be done about it," says Adwoa Christy, a clinical professor in the department of gynaecology, obstetrics, and reproductive sciences at the University of California, San Francisco.

Alston routinely bled through her sheets and clothes, and once, onto an unforgivingly white chair at a mobile phone shop. She just thought she was doing something wrong, and maybe that she needed different period products to contain the flow.

She was told to accept that experiencing painful cramps and embarrassing bloodstains while on your period is normal. In other regions of the world, period taboos and stigma run deeper.

"I think there are a lot of people in my part of the world who may not complain about it, and who, maybe because of normalisation [of pain] and stigma, don't actually come to a doctor," says Hemantha Senanayake, emeritus professor of obstetrics and gynaecology at the University of Colombo in Sri Lanka and head of the Asian Society of Endometriosis and Adenomyosis (both conditions that can cause heavy menstrual bleeding).

And while gynaecologists may know to ask detailed questions to detect heavy menstrual bleeding, clinicians outside the field may overlook the signs. Alston waited nearly 30 years before someone identified her heavy menstrual bleeding, and she's far from alone.

Heavy menstrual bleeding is not just a symptom

While a problem in its own right, heavy menstrual bleeding is primarily a symptom of a larger issue. It arises from a variety of conditions, including polyps, fibroids, cancer, blood disorders, ovulatory issues, and endometrial disorders, such as endometriosis. It is also common – though still something to address – when someone first starts having periods and during the transition to menopause, when the body’s hormonal choreography is in a period of transition.

Treating these conditions can lessen the heavy bleeding, but scientists still don't know how these conditions interfere with the quantity of blood loss, exactly. "There's been a lot of research focusing on the fibroids themselves, but not why they cause the heavy bleeding, for example," says Maybin, who notes that fibroids are noncancerous growths in uterine muscle.

On the other hand, forgoing treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding can create new problems, such as iron deficiency. Iron is an essential mineral for maintaining healthy cells, immune systems, muscles, skin, hair and nails. Brain fog, dizziness, shortness of breath, easy bruising and hair loss can all set in when iron levels begin to flag.

In this way, the harms of heavy menstrual bleeding persist even outside of menstrual periods: studies estimate that over 40% of women with heavy menstrual bleeding also have iron deficiency. Alston found herself in those statistics too: she was always cold and often craved eating ice cubes, a bizarre but telling clue of iron deficiency that's still poorly understood by researchers. If unaddressed, iron deficiency can escalate to anaemia, in which the bone marrow doesn't have enough iron to produce the requisite haemoglobin for red blood cells to carry oxygen throughout the body – a serious condition that can, in extreme cases, requires blood transfusions to correct.

In low and middle-income countries, Senanayake says, where haemorrhage is a leading cause of maternal death, iron deficiency anaemia that isn't resolved before pregnancy can undermine the body's ability to recover from blood loss. It can also harm the brain development of the foetus.

The costs of heavy menstrual bleeding

While there's growing scientific recognition of the medical seriousness of heavy menstrual bleeding, there's less research on what it's like to live with it.

Like Alston, Emily Young, a lecturer in psychology at Sheffield Hallam University in the UK, experienced heavy menstrual bleeding. She has fainted from blood loss more than once, she explains, and always carried a change of clothes as her unpredictable periods could strike at any time. But her doctors assured her that her periods would settle down once she had a baby. Fuelled by the sting of two decades of dismissal from medical professionals, she now researches the experiences of others with heavy periods.

"It's not just an inconvenience. It is having to structure your entire life around your menstrual cycle," says Young.

Adolescents in the UK with heavy menstrual bleeding miss up to nine days of school per year on average.

For a study published in 2025, Young combed through online forum posts from people with heavy menstrual bleeding to bring similar experiences into focus. What she saw ranged from maddening to darkly funny, she says. Several posts described people needing multiple blood transfusions before a doctor recognised the severity of their problem.

Others contained vivid descriptions, such as, "Yeah, if they ever luminol [a chemical used in forensics to highlight blood at crime scenes] my bathroom, I'm going to jail while they excavate my yard for the obviously dozens of murder victims". There were posts about dropping out of school or work, or not having a healthy sex life due to heavy menstrual bleeding. Some posts mentioned mental health issues, and others, Young says, were heartbreaking, describing suicidal thoughts because periods were so severe and life-altering.

For transgender men or non-binary individuals, periods can be distressing enough – heavy menstrual bleeding adds insult to injury. "We see a lot of transgender patients who identify as male, yet have heavy periods, which is in itself an added horrific experience for them," says Julie Jaffray, a paediatric haematologist at the University of California San Diego Rady Children's Hospital.

Ultimately, the cumulative effects of heavy menstrual bleeding on individuals' personal lives can leak into education and work, and ripple through society. Whenever Alston had her period, she would effectively miss school, she says, sleeping in the nurse's office even though her mother insisted she still attend.

In the UK, on average, adolescents with heavy menstrual bleeding miss up to nine days of school per year. In low and middle-income countries, such as Sri Lanka, Senanayake suspects the numbers are higher. Girls in less affluent areas may attend schools that lack facilities to change or dispose of period products.

During adulthood, this translates to missed work days and opportunities. The last time she had a bad period, Alston, a telehealth therapist in New York City, ended up losing a client when she had to cut their session short. "I couldn't hear her anymore, the pain was so bad," Alston says. "I literally told her: 'I can't finish the session'." After she ended the call, she got up from her chair to see a pool of blood beneath her.

"Women with heavy menstrual bleeding can't go to work for 3.6 weeks of the year [on average]. It's costing the economy billions," says Maybin. "If we get this right for women… we really get it right for everyone in society."

Treatment and trials

There's still a lot of work to do to get it right. While there are treatments available for heavy menstrual bleeding, "it's totally not enough," says Erica Marsh, a professor of obstetrics and gynaecology at the University of Michigan Medical School. "We have frighteningly few interventions."

Treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding depends on the underlying condition. If the bleeding isn't too severe, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, like ibuprofen, can ease the flow. There are hormonal treatments too, such as the birth control pill or hormonal intrauterine devices, one of the most effective treatments at reducing blood loss during periods.

Though these methods are fairly accessible, there are deterrents for their uptake, like pain that can accompany the insertion of a intrauterine device. Birth control worked for Alston, but due to the stigma surrounding the pill in her household, she had to wait until she was older – she got a prescription once she left for college.

Hormonal treatments don't work for everyone, and people often discontinue them due to side effects like tender breasts and mood changes, says Maybin. There are non-hormonal medications people can turn to, such as tranexamic acid, that can staunch the flow. "The issue is they are kind of like a band-aid," says Jaffray, and they don't address the underlying cause.

Medications can't always solve the problem. In her mid-thirties, Alston had come off birth control for a time and her periods came back in full force, with intense mood changes too. She finally saw a gynaecologist who performed an ultrasound and found some potential causes. "She's like, 'Scratch birth control. You have seven or eight large fibroids on your uterus, and you might have endometriosis'," a painful condition in which endometrial tissue that lines the uterus starts growing outside the uterus, Alston recalls.

As a result, she chose to have a hysterectomy and completely remove her uterus. In fact, heavy menstrual bleeding is one of the most common reasons people receive hysterectomies. She's happy with her choice, and her heavy menstrual bleeding story ends with a resolution.

But, of course, a hysterectomy is major surgery, it's permanent, and it makes pregnancy impossible. This is especially problematic when providers seem to prioritise fertility over the health of the patient. One of Young's research participants had three children, and her husband had a vasectomy. Her provider still denied her a hysterectomy to treat heavy menstrual bleeding, just in case that the woman got divorced and married another man who wanted children, Young says.

For Maybin, her frustration and embarrassment with the treatment landscape for her patients motivated her to spearhead The Missed Vital Sign, a global research programme funded by the health philanthropy organisation Wellcome Leap. The programme's name reflects the idea that menstrual changes can be the first sign of other health issues, making it a vital sign just like blood pressure, body temperature or heart rate.

Ghana News.title: Sonzele Community Bank works to meet BoG’s GH₵5m capital requirement, declares 25.8% dividend
Ghana News.content:
Sonzele Community Bank PLC has launched an aggressive share mobilisation campaign to meet the Bank of Ghana's (BoG) new GH₵5 million minimum capital requirement by December 2026 while rewarding its shareholders with a substantial 25.8% dividend payout for the 2025 financial year.

The bank, which currently has a stated capital of GH₵2.28 million, is calling on indigenes, members of the diaspora, and the youth to increase their investments to bridge the capital shortfall and secure the financial institution's future.

Speaking at the bank's 36th Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Jirapa, Board Chairman Michael Zuraih revealed that despite economic turbulence and falling Treasury bill rates, the bank's total assets grew by 19.19% to GH₵84.3 million in 2025.

Outlining the regulator's new directive, Mr Zuraih noted that the BoG now requires all rural and community banks to rebrand.

"The Bank of Ghana has recently issued a directive requiring all rural and community banks in the country to change their names to 'Community Banks' and to increase their minimum stated capital from GH₵1 million to GH₵5 million by 31 December 2026," Mr Zuraih stated.

To mitigate the economic shocks of the COVID-19 pandemic, the central bank had previously halted dividend payments for seven years. However, following a pre-tax profit of GH₵3.7 million in 2025, Sonzele Community Bank secured regulatory approval to reward its investors.

"The Board is proposing a payment of GH₵0.258 per share for the year under review," the Board Chairman announced, representing an impressive 25.8% return on investment.

Reiterating the bank's financial strength, Chief Executive Officer Abdul-Sallam Bamie emphasised that the rebranding from a "rural bank" to a "community bank" is a strategic move aimed at greater inclusivity, particularly to attract younger investors.

"The change to 'Community Bank' is also intended to provide a wider, much more inclusive identity. Because when you say 'rural bank,' it is limiting," Mr Bamie explained. "I don't know where else you can put your money and get about a 25.8% return in just one year, while your share capital in the bank remains intact."

The urgency of the recapitalisation drive drew high-profile political and traditional support at the AGM. Upper West Regional Minister Charles Lwanga Puozuing, who revealed that he is also a shareholder, challenged the people of the region to think beyond the current BoG requirements.

"It is my prayer that by next year, we will all buy shares to enable the bank to grow and become even bigger," the Regional Minister urged. "Maybe one day we will convert it from a community bank into a fully fledged commercial bank once our shareholding and capital increase."

This sentiment was echoed by traditional leaders, who reminded the gathering of the bank's deep roots in the region. Speaking on behalf of the Paramount Chief of Jirapa, Konkuo Naa, Naa Angdelle Haara noted that true banking strength lies in the confidence of the people, not just the size of a building.

"Long before many financial institutions discovered the economic potential of our communities, Sonzele Rural Bank had already laid its foundations here," Konkuo Naa remarked. "Let us honour loyalty with loyalty, and let us continue to uphold and strengthen Sonzele Rural Bank PLC as one of our foremost financial partners in development."

However, the consequences of failing to meet the new capital threshold remain severe. The Wa Branch Manager of ARB Apex Bank, Fred Tweneboa, who spoke on behalf of the Acting Managing Director, Curtis William Brantuo, issued a stern reminder to shareholders about the ticking regulatory clock.

"Failure to bridge the gap within the stipulated timeline may expose the bank to operational limitations, heightened supervisory interventions, or the need to consider alternative strategic options provided under the reform framework," Mr Tweneboa warned.

Local government officials underscored the broader socioeconomic and security implications of a strong local banking sector. The District Chief Executive (DCE) for Nadowli-Kaleo, Mary Haruna, who was the guest of honour, linked sound banking practices directly to community safety.

"The responsibility of recapitalising our community banks rests not only on management and directors but also on every shareholder here who believes in the future of the institution," the DCE stated. "Once you are not sleeping with your money, you will not be the target of armed robbers."

The AGM also highlighted a deep sense of solidarity within the Upper West regional banking fraternity. Fredrick Ahah Diegol, CEO of Lawra Area Community Bank PLC, speaking on behalf of sister community banks, praised Sonzele's financial strength and made a passionate appeal to affluent residents to support other struggling banks in the region to prevent their collapse.

"If we allow two to go down, we will be left with only two giants," Mr Diegol urged. "Don't allow the two struggling banks to go down. Come in your numbers and support us so that we too can stand tall, and together we can be stronger."

Ghana News.title: Bohyen chief appeals for fire station
Ghana News.content:
The Chief of Bohyen in the Ashanti Region, Nana Antwi Boasiako II, has appealed to the government to establish a fire station in the area.

He says the absence of fire stations in communities including Bantama, Bohyen, Abrepo, Barekese, Mankranso, Adugyama and Offinso makes it difficult for firefighters to respond quickly to fire outbreaks.

Nana Boasiako II made the appeal at Bohyen during celebrations to mark his 25th anniversary on the throne.

He also called for the National Ambulance Service to extend its services to the area to improve emergency response.

The Chief wants a community centre built at Bohyen to reduce the practice of blocking roads during funerals and other social gatherings, which he says contributes to traffic congestion.

He praised the Member of Parliament for Bantama and former Roads and Highways Minister, Francis Asenso-Boakye, for his contribution to development in Bohyen.

He mentioned a police station, inner roads, a classroom block, an Astroturf football park and a community library among projects he said had helped transform the community.

The week-long anniversary celebration included a clean-up exercise, a health walk, a health screening, a blood donation, an interdenominational church service, an old-school street jam, and a cultural display.

The celebrations brought together traditional leaders, government officials, members of the clergy, business leaders, Assembly Members, members of the Muslim community and residents.

Nana Boasiako II also inaugurated a refurbished palace as part of the anniversary activities.

The chairperson for the occasion, businessman Dr Nana Kwaku Duah, commended the Chief for what he described as his commitment to the development of Bohyen in the last 25 years.

He pledged his support for the Chief's development plans for the people of Kumasi-Bohyen.
