World.title: ‘Play for my team’ – How Nelson Mandela persuaded Bucs legend to join Orlando Pirates
World.content:
Orlando Pirates legend Williams Okpara has revealed that former South African president Nelson Mandela played a pivotal role in convincing him to join the Buccaneers.



The retired Nigerian goalkeeper arrived at Pirates in 1990 and went on to enjoy a remarkable 15-year spell at the club, establishing himself as one of the greatest goalkeepers in the club’s history.

Before signing for Pirates, Okpara spent time training with both Kaizer Chiefs and Mamelodi Sundowns as he searched for a club in South Africa.

Speaking to Lebohang Mokoena on SoccerBeat, Okpara recalled a memorable encounter with Mandela at the Mariston Hotel in Johannesburg, where the ANC regularly held meetings during that period.

“That was when I saw Tata Mandela for the first time face to face because the ANC used to use that place for their meetings. So I was fortunate enough,” said Okpara.

The former goalkeeper said Mandela’s warm welcome immediately made him feel at home.

“When I heard Tata Mandela was coming, I said I need to see him. He was a very gentle and adorable person. He called me and said, ‘Come, you are the son of the soil.’ That statement boosted my confidence.  Okpara says Mandela was a Pirates fan

“He then said, ‘Okay, you have to play for my team. Do you know my team?’ I said, ‘No, I don’t know.’

“He said, ‘One day when you start playing, I’ll remind you.’ I asked my friend, ‘Which team does Nelson Mandela support?’ and he said, ‘Pirates.'”

That conversation proved decisive, with Okpara ultimately choosing Orlando Pirates, where he became a club icon and enjoyed one of the most successful careers by a foreign player in South African football.

Who is the best Pirates keeper?

World.title: How long do you have to wait until debt is prescribed?
World.content:
If you’re wishing your debt would go away, your wish may come true if the debt is prescribed. Prescription essentially means your debt has expired and you’re under no legal obligation to repay it.

Besides, it becomes illegal for a collector to ask you to make payments.

How do you know if your debt is prescribed?

Most debt prescribes after three years. But that only happens if you meet three conditions:



Haven’t acknowledged or made arrangements to repay the debt for that period.

Didn’t make any payments toward the outstanding balance.

You haven’t received a summons, or there hasn’t been a judgment on the debt.

This three-year countdown doesn’t begin when you sign the contract. It starts from the last time you made a payment or acknowledged your debt.

Often, debt collectors won’t share that debt is prescribed or is months away from prescribing when they start pursuing you aggressively.

Debt collectors typically don’t share this information because they’ve purchased your debt. To get a return on the investment, they need you to resume payments. When you resume payments, no matter how small, you restart the clock.

Therefore, it is your responsibility not to get taken in by threats, even if they include blacklisting or judgments.

Managing debt collection calls on old debts

If you’re unsure if a debt has prescribed, you can ask the caller when the last payment was made on the account. Don’t acknowledge the debt.

Instead, ask them to clarify what they are calling about and follow up with: “when was the last payment made?”



At this stage, they may become vague and give a month. Ask them to clarify the year.

If it’s been more than three years, you should report this debt collector to the Council for Debt Collectors.

It is against the law to pursue repayment on a debt that has prescribed. Specifically, it is against Section 126b of the National Credit Act 34 of 2005.

If it’s closing in on 3 years, don’t agree to make a payment or acknowledge the debt.

Debt that takes longer than 3 years to prescribe

Debts arising from credit cards, store cards and store credit, bank fees, cell phone contracts, gym memberships and personal loans prescribe after 3 years, if they meet the conditions mentioned above.

However, a home loan, outstanding taxes, municipal rates, and debts where there’s been a judgment, only prescribe after 30 years.

What happens to prescribed debt?

When a debt prescribes, it will no longer show up on your credit report.

You should check your credit report and dispute all debts that you believe have prescribed.

Years of unpaid debt will mean your credit score is low. If you want to get better interest rates when you apply for credit, you need to rebuild your credit.

That means paying all your current bills on time. You can also rebuild your credit by closing unused credit. Your credit exposure adds to your debt-to-income ratio, even if you’re not using it.

World.title: Faf and Frans innovate with on-field communication for Cheetahs
World.content:
On Friday night, one moment stood out during the Cheetahs’ Currie Cup game against the Sharks XV. During a break in play, Faf de Klerk could be seen speaking on a two-way radio, and coach Frans Steyn later revealed the scrumhalf had been communicating with him as part of an interesting innovation.



It will draw comparisons to the style of Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus, who is always thinking up different ways of doing things, most famously using lights to communicate from the top of the stadium way back when he was Cheetahs coach.

“If Faf has something on his mind and picks up the radio to share it with me, I love it,” the former Bok utility back told Rapport.

“I’m not out there on the field with them. We in the coaches’ box see things from a different perspective than the players do on the pitch.

“And after Faf and I spoke over the radio, there was a shift in the game. If I’m not mistaken, we scored points shortly afterwards.”

Faf de Klerk stars for Cheetahs

Besides his leadership role, De Klerk – who caught many by surprise when he signed for the Cheetahs – was named Man of the Match after Friday’s 43-21 Currie Cup win in Bloemfontein, scoring two tries and creating several others.

“Faf has only been with us for a few weeks, but his quality is already shining through,” he said.



First Division result to note

Meanwhile, the Eagles were crowned Currie Cup First Division champions on a frosty Friday evening in George when they delivered a dominant second half performance to beat the Valke 41-21, after they led by 19-14 at the break.

The hosts outscored the visitors from the East Rand by six tries to three in an entertaining final staged at Outeniqua Park.

The game was evenly balanced by the halfway mark, with the Eagles leading by only five points. However, the second half belonged entirely to the hosts as they dominated the forward battle, showed impressive defensive resolve, and displayed clinical finishing to round off a number of scoring opportunities.

The Eagles’ deserved victory brought smiles and joy to the rugby supporters of the Garden Route after their side had earlier missed out on qualifying for the Premier Division.

World.title: RIP | Man dies after boat capsizes at Kowie River mouth in Port Alfred
World.content:
A man has died after a rigid hull inflatable boat capsized while attempting to exit the Kowie River mouth in Port Alfred on Sunday morning. Image: Instagram @royalalfredmarina

A man has died, while his grandson survived, after a rigid hull inflatable boat (RHIB) capsized while attempting to exit the Kowie River mouth in Port Alfred on Sunday morning.

The National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) said emergency services were alerted shortly after 08:20 following reports that two people had been thrown into the water.

READ | NSRI rescues three after rip current drama at Port Edward



Extensive rescue response

According to the NSRI, its Port Alfred Station 11 duty crew was activated at 08:23 after eyewitnesses reported the capsized vessel in the Kowie River mouth.

The NSRI launched its rescue craft Rescue 11 Alpha and dispatched a rescue vehicle to the scene.

Emergency responders included NSRI rescue swimmers, the South African Police Service (SAPS), Multi-Security, Eastern Cape Government Health EMS, Gardmed Ambulance Services and Life First paramedics.

One man declared dead

When rescuers arrived, they found the boat overturned in the surf zone at East Beach.

A local adult man was recovered from the water, and emergency personnel immediately began cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR).

Despite extensive efforts to revive him, he was declared dead at the scene.



His grandson, an adult from Gauteng, was found on the shoreline. He was taken to a local doctor for treatment and is recovering in the care of his family.

Inquest opened

The deceased man’s body has been placed in the care of SAPS and the Eastern Cape Government Health Forensic Pathology Services.

Police have opened an inquest into the incident.

The NSRI said early indications suggest the boat may have been overturned by waves while attempting to leave the Kowie River mouth and head out to sea.

The capsized vessel has since been recovered and handed over to police.

The NSRI conveyed its condolences to the family and friends of the deceased, saying its thoughts remain with them during this difficult time.

World.title: DA demands full disclosure of Schröder Street name change costs
World.content:
The DA has called on the Dawid Kruiper Municipality to disclose how much public money has been spent on the renaming of Schröder Street. Image: Dawid Kruiper Municipality website

The Democratic Alliance (DA) has called on the Dawid Kruiper Municipality to disclose how much public money has been spent on the controversial renaming of Schröder Street while a criminal fraud investigation involving Executive Mayor David Kazi remains under way.

The party argues that taxpayers deserve full transparency as South African Police Service (SAPS) investigators continue probing allegations surrounding the petition used to justify the street name change.

Fraud allegations under investigation

According to the DA, the police investigation stems from allegations that the ANC submitted a fraudulent petition supporting the renaming of Schröder Street to Alfred Qayiso Gubela Street.



The party claims the petition contained manipulated information taken from DA petition forms, as well as the name of a deceased DA member.

Despite these allegations, the municipality proceeded with the name change based on a petition containing 1 317 signatures, the DA said, while rejecting its own petition of 7 055 residents who opposed the proposal.

The DA said it welcomed what it described as recent progress in the investigation after making enquiries about the case and the resurfacing of the police docket.

Concerns over public spending

The opposition party said it is deeply concerned that the municipality has continued spending public funds on implementing the name change while the legality of the process remains under criminal investigation.

According to the DA, some road curb markings have already been repainted with the new street name, several new street signs have been erected and municipal funds were also used for the Heritage Day launch of the renamed street earlier this year.

The party warned that if the investigation ultimately finds wrongdoing in the process, taxpayers could end up footing the bill for a project that should not have proceeded.



DA seeks full cost breakdown

The DA is demanding that the municipality provide council with a detailed breakdown of all expenditure related to the project, including:

Street signage

Road markings

Launch events

Administrative costs

Any other expenditure linked to the renaming process

The party maintains that the street name change was politically motivated and pushed through despite significant public opposition.

“The people of Upington deserve a municipality that puts responsible governance ahead of political agendas,” the DA said.

It added that it would continue to hold those responsible accountable while ensuring residents know how public funds have been spent.

Your thoughts of the constant renaming of streets and cities?

World.title: DA grows rural support as more than 500 Eastern Cape residents quit ANC
World.content:
The DA says it is gaining momentum in the Eastern Cape's rural communities after more than 500 residents from two villages joined the party. Image: DA

The Democratic Alliance (DA) says it is gaining momentum in the Eastern Cape’s rural communities after more than 500 residents from two villages joined the party during a week-long outreach campaign.

According to DA Eastern Cape leader Andrew Whitfield, the new members are former African National Congress (ANC) supporters who have decided to back the DA ahead of the 4 November 2026 Local Government Elections.

Hundreds sign up in two villages

Whitfield visited several rural communities across the province during the week.



More than 300 residents. One clear message: It's time for change. 💙🧢



Today, Eastern Cape Provincial Leader Andrew Whitfield and Constituency Leader Bax Nodada welcomed over 300 new DA members from Ward 14 in Umzimvubu Local Municipality.



People are choosing the DA because… pic.twitter.com/yFsxCtR1h8 — DA Eastern Cape (@DAEasternCape) July 24, 2026

On Thursday, accompanied by DA OR Tambo Constituency leader Mlindi Nhanha MP, he addressed residents in Lwandlana Village in the Ingquza Hill Local Municipality.

The DA said more than 200 residents joined the party during the visit.

A day later, Whitfield travelled to Makolonini Village in the Umzimvubu Local Municipality, where he was joined by DA Alfred Nzo Constituency leader Bax Nodada MP.

According to the party, more than 300 residents signed up as new DA members there.

Service delivery concerns

Whitfield said residents in both communities cited poor service delivery as one of the main reasons for switching political allegiance.



He said communities were frustrated by unreliable access to water and electricity, inadequate sanitation services, deteriorating roads and a lack of economic opportunities.

“The people of Lwandlana are tired of living without reliable access to water and electricity, without basic service delivery, and with roads that are often impassable,” Whitfield said.

He added that residents in Makolonini wanted honest government, improved infrastructure and sustainable economic growth to help lift their communities out of poverty.

Election campaign gathers pace

The announcement comes as political parties intensify campaigning ahead of South Africa’s municipal elections on 4 November.

Whitfield said the DA would continue campaigning across the province on a platform of improved governance, service delivery, job creation and economic growth.

“The Eastern Cape has the people, the natural resources, the entrepreneurs and the potential to become South Africa’s most investable and liveable province,” he said.

He urged voters to support the DA in the upcoming local government elections, saying the party believes it can help ensure that villages, towns, cities and municipalities “start working for all.”

World.title: Bontebok National Park announces phased reopening
World.content:
Bontebok National Park will welcome visitors again from 1 August 2026 as SANParks begins a phased reopening following extensive flood damage. Image: SANParks

Bontebok National Park will welcome visitors again from Saturday, 1 August 2026, as South African National Parks (SANParks) begins a phased reopening following extensive flood damage sustained in May.



Significant rehabilitation work has been completed over the past two months, allowing parts of the popular Swellendam reserve to safely reopen while repairs continue in other sections of the park.

First phase of reopening

The initial reopening will include:

Six self-catering chalets

The park’s camping site

Aloe Hill Hiking Trail

Acacia Hiking Trail

Termite Hiking Trail

Visitors will once again be able to enjoy overnight stays and selected outdoor activities as SANParks gradually restores normal operations.

Some facilities remain closed

Not all areas of the park are ready to reopen.

The following facilities remain unavailable while rehabilitation work continues:

Eight riverside chalets damaged during the floods

Die Stroom Picnic Site

Bushbuck Trail

SANParks said these facilities will reopen once restoration work has been completed and it is safe to welcome visitors back.



More facilities to reopen in phases

The conservation authority said it will continue with a phased reopening, with additional accommodation and visitor experiences becoming available as rehabilitation progresses.

Future updates on the reopening of the remaining facilities will be communicated as work is completed.

SANParks thanks visitors

SANParks thanked visitors, tourism partners and stakeholders for their patience and ongoing support during the recovery process.

The organisation said it looks forward to welcoming guests back to Bontebok National Park while remaining committed to restoring the park’s facilities safely and responsibly.

Visitors seeking accommodation bookings or the latest visitor information can do so through the official SANParks website.

World.title: Taxi licence backlog a thing of the past, says Gauteng MEC
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The taxi industry has raised concerns over the slow issuing of operating licences and compliance documents.

Gauteng Roads and Transport MEC Kedibone Diale-Tlabela said the backlog in taxi operating licences has been reduced.

The department has given out more than 3,000 operating licences since November 2025. That's because of improvements in administrative and internal capacity in the department.

"We don't like law enforcement as a society, generally. We want it, we want to see it happen, but when it happens we don't want it.

“And I think this is a classical case. Remember we came in, there have been challenges, well pronounced by the industry, and we started focusing on dealing with the challenges.

“And amongst them is backlog on operating licenses, which by the way, were far advanced. Now we're issuing operating licenses to individual operators in our province.

“The backlog is gone. Now we are entering what we've been suspecting. That's a massive milestone. No, it is, it is. When you win, you win. And I think we did our best; we won because we worked closely with them, we partnered with them to understand the material contradictions.”

World.title: Reading begins at home | Experts call on parents to tell more stories
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's literacy crisis doesn't begin or end in the classroom.

Experts say parents and guardians play a vital role in developing a child's love of reading, even if they don't have books or struggle with literacy themselves.

Nal’ibali’s Etienne Bramley said something as simple as telling stories can help lay the foundation for lifelong learning.

“I think one of the big reasons I think we see parents especially not reading to children is they themselves are not necessarily that literate.

“We have quite a high illiteracy rate among adults as well. But there are a lot of ways you can tell stories to children. Get them interested in stories. Tell them stories from your youth and from when you were young.

“So I think our plea to parents especially is, you know, tell stories to your children. You know, you can do that while you make food, while you give them chores in the home, or you play with them.

“Tell them stories and read stories to them, even if you just get a picture book and make up your own story. You know, I think children need to hear the rich stories as you say that we have on this continent and our rich diversity, which is a beautiful thing of our country that we can share with our children."

World.title: Andrea Johnson back to Madlanga Commission hot seat
World.content:
PRETORIA - IDAC Head Andrea Johnson is set to return to the Madlanga Commission on Monday to resume her testimony.

It comes after she admitted that parts of her evidence were incorrect, acknowledging key errors in her testimony to parliament's ad hoc committee.

Johnson conceded that IDAC had solicited a Section 27 affidavit for suspended Crime Intelligence Chief Dumisani Khumalo, after previously denying ever receiving the document.

Her appearance comes as a formal complaint has been lodged with the IDAC Ombud.

It's calling for an investigation into her conduct and alleges abuse of prosecutorial authority.

World.title: City of Joburg cracks down on alleged R4bn financial misconduct
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The City of Johannesburg wants officials held responsible for financial misconduct.

The council has approved the referral of 13 cases worth R4-billion to the city's independent disciplinary board.

Deputy mayor Loyiso Masuku said investigations are due to start and an update on these cases is expected next month.

“An incredible amount of money, money that is supposed to be utilized properly for service delivery because it's taxpayers' money. The disciplinary board sits every two weeks as they've been set up and we expect that by the September council meeting we will be able to get a preliminary investigative update.

“The preliminary investigative update assists us to determine in the interim what actions to take, if there are any actions to take. They also assist us to enable us to see if there are cases that need time, further time to investigate.

“Perhaps they need assistance with other state institutions, which is outside just the purview of our own work. So that is the work that they do and they have to report to council and we do, you are correct, we have a responsibility to make sure that citizens know if there were any acts of maladministration, if there were any acts of corruption.

“That is why we use the word in council, alleged financial misconduct, because they still have to be investigated,” she said.

World.title: Mapiyeye cleared of sexual harassment abuse
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A disciplinary hearing has found that the City of Ekurhuleni failed to prove allegations of sexual harassment and abuse of authority against EMPD Chief Isaac Mapiyeye.

The case centred on a relationship between Mapiyeye and a junior employee.

The chairperson found that while the power imbalance was not in dispute, the employer failed to prove that the relationship was unwanted or maintained through coercion.

Mapiyeye always alleged that the relationship was consensual.

The disciplinary inquiry concluded that the employer did not discharge the burden of proof to establish misconduct.

Mapiyeye testified against several Ekurhuleni officials at the Madlanga Commission, accusing them of corruption.

He said he faced threats after trying to discipline rogue subordinates like Julius Mkhwanazi.

World.title: ‘We declare war’ – Patriotic Alliance Cape Town mayoral candidate
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Patriotic Alliance has used fighting words to outline its election strategy for Cape Town.

The party leadership held a dialogue to outline its state of readiness for the municipal polls.

Cape Town mayoral candidate Cheslyn Daniels called on supporters to unite to win the metro.

“And today I ask you, each candidate, each ward representative, to focus, block out the noise, block out the doubt, patriots. Focus on the goals. The goal is to take the city of Cape Town.

“The goal is to bring the Patriotic Alliance to the city of Cape Town. To achieve this goal, we must trust the process. And therefore I ask you, do you believe in a united Cape Town? Do you believe in a better Cape Town? Do you believe in one Cape Town? And therefore, patriots, if you do, then stand as one and unite behind the patriotic alliance. Because today, we declare war! We declare war!” he said.

World.title: ATM heads to court over Western Cape High Court ruling
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – The African Transformation Movement is heading to the Constitutional Court to seek clarity on the implementation and effect of its order relating to the Section 89 impeachment process.

The party has instructed its legal team to approach the court on an urgent basis.

Last week, the Western Cape High Court granted President Cyril Ramaphosa an interim interdict preventing Parliament from proceeding with the public hearings of the impeachment inquiry.

In a statement, the party’s national spokesperson Zama Ntshona said they were concerned that the judgment has created significant constitutional uncertainty.

“Importantly, the decision was not unanimous. A dissenting judgment found that the President had failed to establish a proper case for interim relief, illustrating that the constitutional issues involved remain contested and require authoritative determination by the Apex Court.

“The integrity of South Africa's constitutional democracy depends on clarity, consistency, and respect for the authority of the country's highest court. These are principles that must be protected irrespective of the individuals involved,” Ntshona said.

The party has said it ATM remains “unwavering” in its commitment to constitutional accountability and to ensuring that the Phala Phala matter is not indefinitely delayed through procedural litigation.

“The public must also be reminded that the President has secured only an interim interdict. He has not been exonerated or cleared of the serious allegations arising from the Phala Phala matter. Those allegations remain unresolved and must ultimately be subjected to the constitutional accountability mechanisms established by our democratic order.”

World.title: Alleged mastermind in Sinovuyo Dyokwe murder arrested
World.content:
PARKLANDS – Police have arrested a man suspected to be the mastermind in the killing of DA candidate councillor Sinovuyo Dyokwe.

She was murdered last month while returning home after participating in voter registration activities in Dunoon. She was allegedly followed before two armed suspects fatally shot her.

Police spokesperson Colonel Andrè Traut said the suspect, aged 37, was arrested during a joint intelligence-driven operation conducted by Provincial SVCI detectives and the SAPS Special Task Force in Parklands. He had allegedly been evading arrest.

“The arrest follows an intensive investigation during which detectives acted on information received from members of the public regarding the suspect’s whereabouts. The suspect has been positively linked to the murder through the ongoing investigation.

“Preliminary investigations indicate that the deceased had allegedly been subjected to extortion and was reportedly forced to pay protection money. It is further alleged that after she refused to continue making these payments, threats were made against her,” Traut said.

During the operation, police seized the vehicle allegedly used in the commission of the offence, as well as seven cellular phones that will form part of the ongoing investigation.

The suspect is expected to appear in the Cape Town Magistrate’s Court on Monday, 27 July 2026, on charges of murder and extortion.

The investigation remains ongoing, and further arrests are expected as detectives continue to pursue all those involved in this matter.

World.title: Imported sugar undermining local industry, farmers say
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sugarcane farmers during a meeting at Kobodo trading centre in Ndhiwa West sub-county, Homa Bay County. [James Omoro, Standard]

Sugarcane farmers in South Nyanza have decried the importation of sugar, saying it is driving the region into abject poverty.

The imported sugar is packaged and sold in the local market at lower prices, prompting consumers to shun locally produced sugar from Kenyan industries.

The farmers lamented that the trend denies local industries the much-needed revenue to purchase sugarcane from farmers or pay for cane already delivered.

The farmers supply their sugarcane to Sukari Industry at Riat Trading Centre in Ndhiwa West Sub-county, Homa Bay County, and Sony Sugar Company in Awendo Town, Migori County.

Addressing journalists at Kobodo Trading Centre in Ndhiwa West Sub-county, the farmers said sugar imports are impoverishing them.

"The problem has escalated to a point where many farmers are unable to receive payment for sugarcane supplies because the sugar market has been flooded with imported sugar," Austine Ouma said.

Ouma said the importation of sugar is jeopardising economic growth in the region.

"We are losing money because our sugarcane is neither paid for nor purchased properly. The importation of sugar is making us poor," he said.

He lamented that the situation has left mature sugarcane to overstay on farms.

"Our well-being is threatened because mature sugarcane dries up on the farms before it is harvested," he said.

Ouma, who spoke on behalf of the sugarcane growers, said life had become unbearable for them.

"Most of us are unable to educate our children and meet our household needs. It is painful that these problems persist even as we toil on our farms to grow sugarcane," he said.

The farmers want the government to stop the importation of sugar into the country.

Raphael Owino said farmers will only get value for their efforts if sugar imports are stopped.

"We are sure of getting the value of our sweat only if local millers can sell their sugar without the ongoing interference," Owino said.

Sukari Industry Advisory Board Chairperson Vitalis Okinda said the issues affecting the sugar industry deserve serious attention from the government and elected leaders to cushion the sector from collapse.

"We call on the government to address sugar importation. We also want our elected leaders to take this matter seriously," Okinda said.

He warned that many Kenyans would lose their jobs if sugar industries collapsed.

"The sugar sector has employed many people and deserves support just like other sectors. Kenya will experience unprecedented unemployment if the sugar industry dies in this country," Okinda said.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).
